headline: Saud Shakeel, Saqib put Pakistan in control in first Test
description: Left-hander hits 93 to lift hosts to 434-9 declared before debutant Saqib strikes twice to unsettle Sri Lanka
author: Alam Zeb Safi
article_text:
KARACHI: Pakistan were in a good position as after declaring their first innings at 434-9 they reduced Sri Lanka to 114-3 when bad light hastened the stumps on the second day of the first Test of the two-match series at the Pindi Stadium in Rawalpindi on Tuesday.

Sri Lanka still trail by 320 runs with seven wickets in hand.

Sri Lanka had a disastrous response as they lost their two early wickets inside three overs that put Pakistan on top.

Seasoned pacer Mohammad Abbas removed Pasindu Sooriyabandara for a duck in the third over after he edged it to keeper Ghazi Ghori.

In the next over 31-year old debutant pacer Saqib Khan got rid of Dinesh Chandimal, held by Agha Salman, to leave the visitors reeling at 12-2 in the fourth over.

However, at this stage skipper Kamindu Mendis and opener Lahiru Udara dug deep to revive the innings. The duo shared 53 runs for the third wicket association. It was Saqib Khan who broke the stand by claiming the wicket of Lahiru who was caught by Ghazi Ghori behind the stumps.

And Sri Lanka were 65-3 at that stage. Lahiru hit seven fours in his solid 42 which came off 52 balls.

Dhananjaya de Silva then joined his skipper Mendis and both batted with great responsibility and built their team’s total without further losing any wicket at close.

They added 49 runs for the fourth wicket unbroken stand. Mendis had struck five fours in his 40 while Dhananjaya made 22 not out with two fours.

Saqib, who belongs to Karachi, had a good day on his debut as he captured 2-54 in 10.1 overs.

Mohammad Abbas claimed 1-23.

Earlier Pakistan declared their first innings on 434-9 with Saud Shakeel scoring 93.

Debutant Arafat Minhas, who also did well in the ODI tri-series recently, contributed a solid fifty to showcase his batting skills in the longest format.

Pakistan resumed at 281-5 with Saud batting on 57 and Ghazi Ghori on seven and added 153 runs before declaring after 106.3 overs.

Saud looked set for his fifth test century but fell seven runs short when he was caught behind by wicket-keeper Kusal Mendis off Asitha Fernando for 93 from 199 deliveries, ending a valuable innings that included nine fours.

Ghori also made a significant contribution, scoring 48 from 72 balls before being caught by Pasindu Sooriyabandara off Dilshan Madushanka.

The pair added 96 runs for the sixth wicket to strengthen Pakistan's position after the hosts had lost five wickets for 253.

Minhas, playing his first test, impressed with an attacking 52 from 72 balls, hitting nine fours and a six. He was caught by Dhananjaya de Silva off Madushanka, with Pakistan reaching 434-8 at the time.

Razaullah added ten before falling to Lahiru Kumara, while Saqib Khan remained unbeaten on nought when Pakistan declared.

Fernando (3-107) and Madushanka (3-108) claimed three wickets apiece while Lahiru Kumara (1-104) and Milan Rathnayaka (1-72) finished with one wicket each.

Pakistan had earlier benefited from half-centuries by Tayyab Arif, Mohammad Taha and captain Babar Azam on the opening day after Sri Lanka elected to field.

“Earlier on we had started well but pitch was not easy and had we attacked it could have created problems but we latter controlled that,” Saud Shakeel said. “It really hurts you when you get out without achieving a milestone. I had no plan to play quick but the ball I received was a bit faster off the pitch and I responded a bit slow which resulted in my dismissal,” said Saud, who missed his fifth Test century by just seven runs.

headline: Trump says FBI probing Nvidia CEO Huang as China controversy deepens
description: US president says he 'was amazed' by allegations about Huang as Nvidia shares close down more than 4% on Monday
author: Reuters
article_text:
United States President Donald Trump said on Monday the FBI was looking into Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with a Chinese businesswoman alleged to be a spy for Beijing.

Trump said he "was amazed" by allegations about Huang, among the president's closest allies in Silicon Valley. Trump said he had spoken to the CEO, who told him that he had no idea that the woman was a spy. "I know the FBI is looking into it," Trump said. "I think that he'll be in good shape," he added.

Nvidia shares closed down more than 4% on Monday after the company's board launched an internal investigation into whether Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence effort. The probe, announced on Sunday, has put a spotlight on 63-year-old Huang's future given Nvidia's status as the world's most valuable chipmaker and the CEO's role as the most prolific salesman of the AI boom.

Huang told Nvidia's employees that he had been unfaithful to his wife, without disclosing details of the relationship.

The leather-jacketed Huang enjoys rock-star status worldwide, particularly in Asia, where he often mingles freely with fans, taking selfies and signing autographs for his devoted followers. He is Nvidia's fifth-largest shareholder with a roughly 3.6% stake, according to LSEG data, and keeps a tight grip on the company through an unusually flat structure in which dozens of executives report directly to him.

But unlike Mark Zuckerberg's Meta Platforms or Elon Musk's SpaceX, Nvidia has no dual-class shares that would give co-founder Huang majority voting control.

The New York Times reported that Trump was briefed on Huang's relationship with the woman and that she was giving information to the Chinese government, and that the president chose not to act on the information.

"The so-called Chinese spy narrative is purely a groundless accusation, slander, and a smear," Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun told reporters in Beijing.

Huang's relationship with Trump has coincided with several favourable policy developments for the company, and the president has lavished Huang with praise, awarding him the nation's highest honour for scientific achievement in October. The same day Trump gave Huang the award, the president disclosed buying up to $1.6 million and selling up to $1 million of Nvidia shares during the summer.

'Not an ordinary CEO'

Nvidia said its board has confidence in Huang, thought by many on Wall Street to be the most important person underpinning the AI trade. Analysts acknowledged uncertainty around succession, but most do not expect the investigation to result in the longtime CEO stepping down.

"Nvidia is not an ordinary company and Jensen is not an ordinary CEO; he is Nvidia, clearly sets the long-term strategy and direction, and pulls most of the company's strings himself," said Stacy Rasgon, an analyst at Bernstein.

Nvidia shareholders were quick to sue Huang and the company in a proposed class action on Monday, accusing them of defrauding shareholders by concealing Huang's ties with a suspected Chinese spy.

Lawmakers and advocates told Reuters that Congress was more likely to pass legislation to tighten China's access to AI chips in light of news of Huang's relationship with a suspected Chinese intelligence agent.

US House of Representatives Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries said on Monday that Congress needs more answers and called for the House to pass an annual defence bill that includes restrictions on chip sales to China.

The New York Times reported last month that Huang had a relationship with Alice Huang, an unrelated former executive of Singapore-based company Megaspeed, who US authorities investigated and concluded was a Chinese intelligence asset.

Megaspeed did not respond immediately to a request for comment on Monday, a public holiday in Singapore. Alice Huang did not respond to the New York Times last month when it first reported her relationship with Huang, and Reuters could not determine her location to seek comment on Monday.

article_html:
United States President Donald Trump said on Monday the FBI was looking into Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with a Chinese businesswoman alleged to be a spy for Beijing.

Trump said he "was amazed" by allegations about Huang, among the president's closest allies in Silicon Valley. Trump said he had spoken to the CEO, who told him that he had no idea that the woman was a spy. "I know the FBI is looking into it," Trump said. "I think that he'll be in good shape," he added.

Nvidia shares closed down more than 4% on Monday after the company's board launched an internal investigation into whether Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence effort. The probe, announced on Sunday, has put a spotlight on 63-year-old Huang's future given Nvidia's status as the world's most valuable chipmaker and the CEO's role as the most prolific salesman of the AI boom.

Huang told Nvidia's employees that he had been unfaithful to his wife, without disclosing details of the relationship.

The leather-jacketed Huang enjoys rock-star status worldwide, particularly in Asia, where he often mingles freely with fans, taking selfies and signing autographs for his devoted followers. He is Nvidia's fifth-largest shareholder with a roughly 3.6% stake, according to LSEG data, and keeps a tight grip on the company through an unusually flat structure in which dozens of executives report directly to him.

Read: Nvidia boss criticises 'cheap' AI doomsday warnings

But unlike Mark Zuckerberg's Meta Platforms or Elon Musk's SpaceX, Nvidia has no dual-class shares that would give co-founder Huang majority voting control.

The New York Times reported that Trump was briefed on Huang's relationship with the woman and that she was giving information to the Chinese government, and that the president chose not to act on the information.

"The so-called Chinese spy narrative is purely a groundless accusation, slander, and a smear," Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun told reporters in Beijing.

Huang's relationship with Trump has coincided with several favourable policy developments for the company, and the president has lavished Huang with praise, awarding him the nation's highest honour for scientific achievement in October. The same day Trump gave Huang the award, the president disclosed buying up to $1.6 million and selling up to $1 million of Nvidia shares during the summer.

'Not an ordinary CEO'

Nvidia said its board has confidence in Huang, thought by many on Wall Street to be the most important person underpinning the AI trade. Analysts acknowledged uncertainty around succession, but most do not expect the investigation to result in the longtime CEO stepping down.

"Nvidia is not an ordinary company and Jensen is not an ordinary CEO; he is Nvidia, clearly sets the long-term strategy and direction, and pulls most of the company's strings himself," said Stacy Rasgon, an analyst at Bernstein.

Nvidia shareholders were quick to sue Huang and the company in a proposed class action on Monday, accusing them of defrauding shareholders by concealing Huang's ties with a suspected Chinese spy.

Lawmakers and advocates told Reuters that Congress was more likely to pass legislation to tighten China's access to AI chips in light of news of Huang's relationship with a suspected Chinese intelligence agent.

US House of Representatives Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries said on Monday that Congress needs more answers and called for the House to pass an annual defence bill that includes restrictions on chip sales to China.

The New York Times reported last month that Huang had a relationship with Alice Huang, an unrelated former executive of Singapore-based company Megaspeed, who US authorities investigated and concluded was a Chinese intelligence asset.

Megaspeed did not respond immediately to a request for comment on Monday, a public holiday in Singapore. Alice Huang did not respond to the New York Times last month when it first reported her relationship with Huang, and Reuters could not determine her location to seek comment on Monday.

headline: James Gunn and Peter Safran announce sudden DC Studios exit as Jeremy Latcham takes over
description: James Gunn and Peter Safran will leave DC Studios on December 1, with Jeremy Latcham replacing them
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
James Gunn and Peter Safran are stepping down as co-CEOs of DC Studios, with former Marvel executive Jeremy Latcham set to take over their responsibilities on December 1.

The announcement, confirmed by Skydance, raises questions about the future direction of the DC Universe (DCU).

Gunn and Safran will remain involved in several ongoing projects during the transition. They are overseeing post-production on Man of Tomorrow, directed by Gunn, and will continue producing projects already in development, including The Batman Part 2.

In a joint statement, Skydance chairman and CEO David Ellison and co-CEO Ynon Kreiz credited the pair with establishing a new creative direction for DC Studios. They also expressed confidence in Latcham and said they expected a collaborative transition.

Gunn and Safran said they were proud of their work over the past four years, highlighting projects including Superman, Peacemaker, Creature Commandos, Lanterns and Clayface. They also welcomed Latcham, describing him as a longtime creative partner from their previous work at Marvel.

In a separate statement, Gunn described his experience leading DC Studios as rewarding but also "trying" because of its corporate responsibilities.

He confirmed that he is writing at least one more DC film, although he remains uncertain about his future in the franchise after completing the script.

The departure comes less than halfway through the approximately 10-year plan the pair had outlined for the DCU. It also follows reports that their positions were secure after the Paramount and Warner Bros. merger received approval.

headline: Security forces recover 700kg of explosives during North Waziristan clearance operation: sources
description: Searches were completed at 17 compounds between Api village and Haider Khel, 28 in Maski and 17 in other areas
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Security forces on Tuesday recovered 700 kilogrammes of locally made explosives, a missile and other equipment during a search and clearance operation in different areas of North Waziristan, security sources said.

The operation was underway in several areas, where security forces searched 62 more houses and several compounds, the sources said.

They said searches were completed at 17 compounds between Api village and Haider Khel, 28 in Maski and 17 in other areas. Fourteen targeted locations were also cleared in Hassu Khel.

During an operation in Mosaki, security forces recovered 700 kilogrammes of locally made explosives, while an Al-Farooq missile, 200 kilogrammes of urea and other related equipment were recovered from Hassu Khel, the sources added.

The operation would continue until the possible presence of terrorists in the area and locations used by them had been cleared, the sources said.

The latest operation came a day after security forces had recovered a large cache of improvised explosive devices, explosives, weapons and ammunition from two terrorist hideouts established inside mosques in Muzak village, on the southern outskirts of Mir Ali, also in North Waziristan.

According to ISPR, the hideouts belonged to Indian proxy Fitna al-Khawarij, the state-designated term for the banned Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP). The military said the hideouts had been used to store explosives and operate torture cells.

Terrorism is a growing problem for Pakistan, with the number of attacks rising every year since 2022, according to Armed Conflict Location & Event Data (ACLED), a global monitoring organisation. Data from ACLED shows attacks in Pakistan rose nearly fourfold to 2,425 in 2025 from 658 in 2022.

The scale of the threat continued to grow in 2026. Two security reports presented to the federal cabinet in October showed that terrorist incidents in K-P had increased by 195 per cent between March 2024 and September 2026.

The reports also found that 73 per cent of attacks recorded in the province during 2026 had targeted police and security personnel, while the use of drones and improvised explosive devices (IEDs) had emerged as growing threats.

Pakistan has repeatedly accused the Afghan Taliban authorities of allowing the banned Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) to operate from Afghan territory and launch attacks inside Pakistan.

A United Nations Security Council monitoring report published in February 2026 supported Islamabad's concerns, saying TTP attacks originating from Afghanistan had increased and that the group was being afforded greater liberty and support by Afghanistan's de facto authorities.

The report also noted that Al Qaeda continued to provide training and support to TTP, while the group had acquired advanced weapons, including night-vision equipment and drone systems.

Security forces on Tuesday recovered 700 kilogrammes of locally made explosives, a missile and other equipment during a search and clearance operation in different areas of North Waziristan, security sources said.

The operation was underway in several areas, where security forces searched 62 more houses and several compounds, the sources said.

They said searches were completed at 17 compounds between Api village and Haider Khel, 28 in Maski and 17 in other areas. Fourteen targeted locations were also cleared in Hassu Khel.

During an operation in Mosaki, security forces recovered 700 kilogrammes of locally made explosives, while an Al-Farooq missile, 200 kilogrammes of urea and other related equipment were recovered from Hassu Khel, the sources added.

The operation would continue until the possible presence of terrorists in the area and locations used by them had been cleared, the sources said.

The latest operation came a day after security forces had recovered a large cache of improvised explosive devices, explosives, weapons and ammunition from two terrorist hideouts established inside mosques in Muzak village, on the southern outskirts of Mir Ali, also in North Waziristan.

According to ISPR, the hideouts belonged to Indian proxy Fitna al-Khawarij, the state-designated term for the banned Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP). The military said the hideouts had been used to store explosives and operate torture cells.

Terrorism is a growing problem for Pakistan, with the number of attacks rising every year since 2022, according to Armed Conflict Location & Event Data (ACLED), a global monitoring organisation. Data from ACLED shows attacks in Pakistan rose nearly fourfold to 2,425 in 2025 from 658 in 2022.

The scale of the threat continued to grow in 2026. Two security reports presented to the federal cabinet in October showed that terrorist incidents in K-P had increased by 195 per cent between March 2024 and September 2026.

The reports also found that 73 per cent of attacks recorded in the province during 2026 had targeted police and security personnel, while the use of drones and improvised explosive devices (IEDs) had emerged as growing threats.

Pakistan has repeatedly accused the Afghan Taliban authorities of allowing the banned Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) to operate from Afghan territory and launch attacks inside Pakistan.

A United Nations Security Council monitoring report published in February 2026 supported Islamabad's concerns, saying TTP attacks originating from Afghanistan had increased and that the group was being afforded greater liberty and support by Afghanistan's de facto authorities.

The report also noted that Al Qaeda continued to provide training and support to TTP, while the group had acquired advanced weapons, including night-vision equipment and drone systems.

headline: Sabalenka downs Muchova to win WTA Finals opener
description: The Belarusian edges Muchova 7-6 (7/2), 7-5, while Andreeva cruises to a 6-4, 6-0 victory
author: AFP
article_text:
Aryna Sabalenka battled past Karolina Muchova in straight sets to make a winning start at the season-ending WTA Finals in Indian Wells on Monday.

Former world number one Sabalenka was forced to dig deep before finally prevailing 7-6 (7/2), 7-5 in just under two hours. Second-seeded Sabalenka is chasing her first ever WTA Finals victory after suffering defeats in the 2022 and 2025 finals.

The four-time Grand Slam champion from Belarus looked to be in trouble after conceding a break of serve to go 5-4 down in the opening set. But she broke back immediately for 5-5 and subsequently went on to hold her nerve in the tie-break 7-2 to seize the early initiative.

Both players struggled on serve in the second set, with Sabalenka suffering her fourth break as she served for the match at 5-4 up.

Crucially though, Sabalenka responded to that stumble by breaking back immediately to lead 6-5 and she made no mistake when serving for the match again, wrapping up victory when Czech opponent Muchova netted a backhand.

"I'm just trying to win every match I play, and at the same time trying to stay in the moment and focus on my game on each point and trying to stay calm and in control," Sabalenka said afterward.

In Monday's other group game, WTA Finals debutant Mirra Andreeva motored past Ukraine's Elina Svitolina in straight sets, winning 6-4, 6-0, despite overcoming pre-match tightness.

Third-seed Andreeva, the 19-year-old reigning French Open champion, took control with a break to open up a 4-2 first-set lead and never looked back against her sixth-seeded opponent.

She duly held serve to close out the first set, and then demolished Svitolina in the second set, rattling off three service breaks to wrap up victory.

"I was so tight, I felt I was moving like a turtle," the teenager said afterwards. "I felt like I couldn't really hit the ball so I'm just very happy to get through the match and control my emotions."

Andreeva will face Sabalenka in her second round robin game on Wednesday.

This year's WTA Finals were scheduled to be held in Saudi Arabia but in July were moved to Indian Wells after US military strikes on Iran in February and the subsequent war in the region.

headline: Rain washes out third NZ-India ODI
description: India retain 2-0 series lead with two matches remaining
author: AFP
article_text:
India retain 2-0 series lead with two matches remaining

The third one-day international between New Zealand and India was abandoned on Tuesday without a ball being bowled because of rain in Hamilton.

India lead the five-match series 2-0 heading into the fourth and fifth matches, which take place in Mount Maunganui on Friday and Sunday.

The teams will then play a two-Test series, starting in Wellington next week and Christchurch at the end of the month.

New Zealand and India are marking 100 years of sporting rivalry between the two countries.

headline: PSX roars back after long weekend as KSE-100 jumps 5,449 points
description: Remittance inflows, falling oil prices and easing US-Iran tensions bolster investor sentiment
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
The Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) staged a powerful rally on Tuesday as investors returned from the long weekend with renewed buying interest, driving the benchmark KSE-100 Index up more than 5,400 points amid support from strong remittance inflows and easing international oil prices.

The benchmark index settled at 179,335.24 points, gaining 5,448.56 points, or 3.13%, from the previous close of 173,886.68. It touched an intraday high of 179,424.04 points, while the day's low stood at 176,273.72.

The market reopened after a long weekend, with trading suspended on Monday on account of Iqbal Day. The return of investors coincided with improving domestic and international sentiment, providing support for an across-the-board upward move.

The rally followed a strong opening, with the index gaining 2,852.32 points, or 1.64%, to reach 176,739.00 within minutes of the opening bell. By midday, it had climbed to 178,540.36, up 4,653.68 points, or 2.68%, as buying momentum continued to build.

On the domestic front, strong remittance inflows helped reinforce investor confidence by supporting the country's external account outlook. Meanwhile, the decline in international oil prices offered additional relief, particularly amid concerns over Pakistan's exposure to imported energy and the potential impact of higher fuel costs on inflation and the balance of payments.

Internationally, oil prices extended losses after United States President Donald Trump downplayed the need for further military action against Iran, easing fears of sustained supply disruptions in the Middle East.

Brent crude futures fell $2.39, or 2.58%, to $90.18 a barrel by 0930 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) futures declined $2.11, or 2.43%, to $84.74 a barrel. The retreat in crude prices reflected reduced concerns about a prolonged disruption to regional oil supplies, while prospects of an oversupplied global market also remained in focus.

The sharp retreat in oil prices improved investor sentiment, triggering broad-based buying across the board and helping the benchmark index reclaim the 175,000 level for the first time since September 1, 2026.

From the index contribution perspective, UBL, LUCK, MEBL, SYS, ENGROH, BAHL, HBL, HUBC, OGDC and PPL were the major contributors to the rally, collectively adding approximately 1,981 points to the benchmark index.

Going forward, the market is likely to maintain its bullish momentum amid easing oil prices and improved global risk appetite. However, profit-taking may emerge at higher levels, keeping investors selective and cautious, Arif Habib Limited's Ali Najib wrote.

Cumulatively, trading volume decreased to 972.4 million from Friday's close of 1.47 billion while the value of traded shares stood at Rs50.6 billion. Shares of 501 companies were traded in the ready market, of which 363 stocks closed higher, 107 fell and 31 remained unchanged.

Cnergyico PK was the volume leader with trading in 70 million shares.

headline: Israeli forces kill Palestinian teen, wound 3 others in occupied West Bank
description: AJ reports Israeli soldiers join occupier groups, attack Palestinians in West Bank while wearing civilian clothes
author: Anadolu Agency
article_text:
Israeli forces killed a 14-year-old Palestinian boy and wounded three other people late Monday in Burqa, northwest of Nablus in the occupied West Bank.

The Palestinian Health Ministry identified the boy as Moataz Iyad Daghlas. It said the General Authority of Civil Affairs had notified it that he was killed by Israeli gunfire.

Local sources said Israeli troops entered Burqa and fired live ammunition at residents. They also blocked the village’s main road, cutting off access in both directions.

The Palestine Red Crescent Society said Israeli forces prevented its ambulance crews from reaching a wounded person and detained three volunteer medics responding to clashes in the village.

Earlier that evening, Red Crescent crews transported a young man to the hospital after he sustained gunshot wounds to his abdomen and pelvis. The Palestinian Medical Relief Society, a nongovernmental organisation, said its crews took another young man to the hospital after he was shot in the hand.

Israeli soldiers in civilian clothes join attacks on Palestinians in West Bank: probe

Israeli soldiers have joined armed groups of Israeli occupiers attacking Palestinians in the West Bank while wearing civilian clothes, an Al Jazeera investigation broadcast Monday found.

The Qatar-based network documented the killings of 14 Palestinians by Israeli occupiers who were found to be serving in the military or appeared in army uniform during attacks. The investigation showed soldiers taking part in assaults on Palestinian villages in civilian clothing, making them difficult to distinguish from armed Israeli occupiers.

It focused on the Israeli army’s Hagmar regional defence units, which recruit Israeli occupiers as reservists. According to the investigation, their ranks have grown sixfold since 2023, while their role has shifted from guarding illegal settlements to directly supporting attacks on Palestinian communities.

The investigation, citing informed sources, said military service gives Israeli occupiers access to sensitive information about Palestinians, licensed weapons and regular military training.

In one case, the investigation linked the fatal shooting of a Palestinian on farmland in Hebron province in the southern West Bank to a soldier wearing civilian clothes. It identified him as an activist in Israeli occupier groups who had been placed under United States sanctions in 2024 before the restrictions were lifted. The report did not name him.

The investigation also presented images showing another Israeli soldier in civilian clothes assaulting Palestinian olive farmers in Nablus province.

Israeli army raids and attacks by Israeli occupiers have intensified in the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, since October 2023, with reports of killings, arrests, home demolitions, arson attacks, the bulldozing of land and the displacement of Palestinian communities.

The Palestinian Wall and Settlement Resistance Commission recorded 1,369 attacks by Israeli occupiers in October. The commission also documented 12,506 attacks between October 2023 and June 2026, resulting in the deaths of 52 Palestinians and 890 fires on Palestinian property and farmland.

headline: Netanyahu calls Trump 'every day' to push for resuming Iran war: report
description: Arab, Muslim leaders alarmed by Netanyahu’s persistent lobbying for resumption of Iran war, the Financial Times says
author: Anadolu Agency
article_text:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has been calling US President Donald Trump “every day” to urge him to resume military action against Iran despite diplomatic efforts to end the conflict, The Financial Times reported on Monday.

“Netanyahu calls him every day [to urge him to resume the war],” a person briefed on the discussions told the British newspaper.

He said figures inside and outside the White House who oppose renewed fighting have been trying to counter Netanyahu’s pressure to resume the war.

“The regional leaders are telling him (Trump) not to escalate and prioritise negotiations,” the source said.

Another person familiar with the situation in Israel said Netanyahu wants military action against Iran to resume, but there was not currently a coordinated “push” to persuade Trump.

The Financial Times said Arab and Muslim leaders have been alarmed by Netanyahu’s persistent lobbying for a resumption of the Iran war.

On Monday, Trump said that Gulf allies oppose a new military campaign against Tehran.

“Qatar, Saudi Arabia, UAE, Bahrain, Kuwait and others would prefer the status quo,” Trump wrote in a Truth Social post following his talks with Qatari Prime Minister Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani.

Netanyahu, who remains a caretaker prime minister following last month’s inconclusive elections in Israel, has called for renewed US-Israeli strikes aimed at forcing the collapse of Iran’s government.

Trump, however, said there was “positive momentum” toward ending the nearly nine-month war and that renewed US strikes on Iran now appeared “quite unlikely.”

Diplomacy

A diplomat briefed on Trump’s meeting with the Qatari prime minister said there was agreement that “diplomacy is the preferred way forward to get a deal.”

According to the Financial Times, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, UAE President Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, and Qatari Emir Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani have spoken with Trump in recent days to urge him to give diplomacy more time.

Regional leaders fear renewed fighting could trigger a broader Iranian response and deepen instability across the Middle East, the report said.

Iran, for its part, has warned that it is prepared to respond to any renewed attacks and could expand the conflict beyond the Middle East.

Mediators have struggled for weeks to break a deadlock between Washington and Tehran over an interim agreement, with both sides discussing a proposal based on a seven-day plan Iran presented in September that Trump previously rejected.

On Monday, Qatar-based television Al Jazeera reported that Sheikh Mohammed’s separate talks with Trump and his Vice President JD Vance had made “good progress” on Iran, citing a source familiar with the discussions.

A diplomatic source told the channel that the talks sought to narrow differences between Washington and Tehran and advance negotiations.

An unnamed Iranian official meanwhile told the semi-official Fars News Agency on Monday that reports of talks to reopen the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for the release of $8 billion in frozen Iranian assets were false.

The official said Tehran would negotiate only within the framework of seven conditions it had conveyed to Washington, including lifting the naval blockade and unilateral sanctions, releasing frozen assets and ending the war.

The US and Israel launched attacks on Iran on Feb. 28. A memorandum of understanding was reached in July to end hostilities, but fighting resumed as diplomatic efforts stalled.

headline: Pochettino favored to be next Manchester United manager
description: The Red Devils consider alternatives as their Premier League struggles continue
author: REUTERS
article_text:
The Red Devils consider alternatives as their Premier League struggles continue

United States men's national team coach Mauricio Pochettino is the top candidate to be the next Manchester United manager, ESPN reported ‌on Monday.

Manchester United reportedly are considering firing manager Michael Carrick after the squad has slipped to 18th in the Premier League table with a 4-4 draw against Aston Villa on ⁠Sunday.

The Red Devils are winless (three losses, five draws) in the league since Aug. 30. With one victory and eight points through 10 games, they are off to their worst-ever Premier League start.

Pochettino, 54, coached Tottenham, Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain before joining the USMNT in 2024.

In August, the Argentine ‌had ⁠his contract extended until 2030 after leading the U.S. to the round of 16 at the World Cup.

Per ESPN, Manchester United's hierarchy also are considering former ⁠Newcastle United manager Eddie Howe for the position, as well as former Ipswich Town coach Kieran McKenna and ⁠former German national team coach Julian Nagelsmann.

Nagelsmann resigned following Germany's elimination in the round of 32 ⁠at the World Cup in July.

Manchester United's next match is at Liverpool on Nov. 22 following an international break this week.

Per ESPN, Manchester United's hierarchy also are considering former ⁠Newcastle United manager Eddie Howe for the position, as well as former Ipswich Town coach Kieran McKenna and ⁠former German national team coach Julian Nagelsmann.
Nagelsmann resigned following Germany's elimination in the round of 32 ⁠at the World Cup in July.
Manchester United's next match is at Liverpool on Nov. 22 following an international break this week.

headline: Kim Kardashian’s ‘Skims’ faces refund requests after advent calendar criticism
description: The 12 day countdown included hair accessories, keychains and a compact mirror
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Kim Kardashian’s Skims is offering full refunds to customers who purchased its $148 advent calendar after the product attracted widespread criticism online over the contents of its 12 day countdown.

The calendar was marketed as a collection of “twelve days of fun surprises”, but customers and social media users questioned whether the items justified its price. The contents included hair ties, logo hair clips, keychains and a compact mirror, with several products attracting particular attention from critics.

A spokesperson for Skims acknowledged that the calendar had disappointed some buyers, telling multiple media outlets that “for some, the calendar did not meet expectations”. The company said it had personally contacted every customer to offer either a full refund or credit towards other products.

The reaction gathered momentum on TikTok, where users shared their opinions about the selection. One account, spicychathouse, compared the items to things a cat might collect around a home. Another suggested the contents resembled miscellaneous objects taken from Kardashian’s bedside table.

Some users even filmed themselves emptying their sofas and presenting the recovered items as their own versions of the Skims calendar, turning the product into a running joke.

The advent calendar contained 12 individual gifts. These included a tartan teddy bear keychain, several sets of hair ties, Skims branded hair clips, a logo squishy ornament, beige elastic straps, a comb keychain and a furry compact mirror keychain.

Skims was co-founded by Kardashian in 2019 and has since become a major name in the shapewear and clothing industry. Forbes has described Kardashian as a billionaire, while the company was valued at $5bn in 2025 after raising additional funding.

The refund offer comes as the criticism puts renewed attention on the gap between the calendar’s premium price and the relatively small accessories included inside.

headline: Lahore Qalandars appoint Aminul Islam as advisor
description: Former Bangladesh captain to guide franchise's high-performance centres and youth development
author: Sports Desk
article_text:
Former Bangladesh captain to guide franchise's high-performance centres and youth development

Lahore Qalandars have appointed former Bangladesh captain Aminul Islam as an advisor to the franchise's High-Performance Centres, the Pakistan Super League side said on Tuesday.

Islam will advise on the development of the centres, focusing on player development, coaching practices and creating pathways for young cricketers to progress in the game.

The appointment is part of Lahore Qalandars' efforts to strengthen their grassroots cricket initiatives and expand their outreach in Bangladesh by drawing on Islam's experience in international cricket and administration.

Islam served as the International Cricket Council's Cricket Development Manager for Asia from 2015 to 2025 and previously worked as a Cricket Development Officer at the Asian Cricket Council.

He also served as president of the Bangladesh Cricket Board, bringing administrative experience alongside a lengthy career in international cricket.

During his playing days, Islam represented Bangladesh from 1988 to 2002 and captained the national side at the 1999 Cricket World Cup.

Lahore Qalandars have built a reputation for identifying and developing emerging talent through their grassroots and high-performance programmes, with the latest appointment expected to add further experience to those efforts.

headline: Starc denies knowledge of ball-tampering plot
description: CA has also ruled out fresh probe as Warner backs Khawaja's claims
author: REUTERS
article_text:
Fast bowler Mitchell Starc denied on Tuesday any prior knowledge of Australia's plot to tamper with the ball during the 2018 tour of South Africa, as Cricket Australia boss Todd Greenberg ruled out another investigation into 'Sandpapergate'.

Starc is the first of Australia's bowlers to respond to Usman Khawaja's assertions in his autobiography and on social media that the whole team knew of a plan ⁠to manipulate the ball in order to get it to reverse swing.

Starc reiterated the bowlers' position from a 2021 statement that they did not know a "foreign substance" had been taken onto the field to alter the condition of the ball.

“I haven’t really paid much attention to be fair, obviously there’s differing opinions of eight years ago," Starc told reporters in Sydney on Tuesday.

"We were heavily drilled through the process at the time, and ⁠since and I guess I won’t speak on behalf of the bowlers, but where I stand, my opinion hasn’t changed. My recollection hasn’t changed from what we said in 2021."

The scandal triggered an integrity probe by Cricket Australia (CA) and led to bans and other penalties for then-captain Steve Smith and former test openers David Warner and Cameron Bancroft four days after the incident came to ⁠light during the Cape Town test.

Khawaja said the team began tampering with the ball at ⁠the second test against South Africa in Gqeberha, not in the third at Cape Town where they were caught. Starc said Khawaja's account was the first time he was aware of ball-tampering taking place in Gqeberha. "I'll leave said authors to explain," he said.

Warner, who retired from international cricket more than two years ago, broke his silence about the scandal on Monday to throw his support behind Khawaja.

In a video posted on social media, Warner described his former teammate's account as 100% accurate and the CA investigation as "botched" and "rushed".

'VERY DIFFERENT VIEWS'

Media pundits, including former captain Michael Clarke, have demanded CA re-investigate ⁠the case.

However, Greenberg told local radio station SEN on Tuesday there was "no compelling reason" to reopen the investigation and could not see anything to be gained ⁠from it. He said players had "very different views" to Khawaja's version of events.

"There are specific details in his book that contradict the versions that have been provided by others," he said. "But we have said we’re comfortable with the outcome of the investigation based on the information we’ve received.

"That includes what we’ve seen from Usman, and our position hasn’t changed on that." Former Cricket Australia CEO James Sutherland, who was in charge of the governing body during the incident, declined to comment on Tuesday. Bancroft, who played his last international in 2019, declined to comment to Australian media on Monday.

He said in a 2021 ⁠interview with the Guardian that it was "self-explanatory" that teammates apart from Smith and Warner were aware of the ball-tampering plan. Captain Pat Cummins said in South Africa last month that he had spoken to Khawaja before the release of the autobiography and was not concerned about any potential fallout.

"Answered every question a million times. So, yeah, it was dealt with then," he said. Some commentators have questioned why Khawaja waited eight years to speak out and accused him of trying to boost sales of his book "Sabr". Khawaja responded on social media on Tuesday, saying he had no commercial motives.

"I'm very fortunate, I don't need the money," he said.

Starc is the first of Australia's bowlers to respond to Usman Khawaja's assertions in his autobiography and on social media that the whole team knew of a plan ⁠to manipulate the ball in order to get it to reverse swing.

Starc reiterated the bowlers' position from a 2021 statement that they did not know a "foreign substance" had been taken onto the field to alter the condition of the ball.

“I haven’t really paid much attention to be fair, obviously there’s differing opinions of eight years ago," Starc told reporters in Sydney on Tuesday.

"We were heavily drilled through the process at the time, and ⁠since and I guess I won’t speak on behalf of the bowlers, but where I stand, my opinion hasn’t changed. My recollection hasn’t changed from what we said in 2021."

The scandal triggered an integrity probe by Cricket Australia (CA) and led to bans and other penalties for then-captain Steve Smith and former test openers David Warner and Cameron Bancroft four days after the incident came to ⁠light during the Cape Town test.

Khawaja said the team began tampering with the ball at ⁠the second test against South Africa in Gqeberha, not in the third at Cape Town where they were caught. Starc said Khawaja's account was the first time he was aware of ball-tampering taking place in Gqeberha. "I'll leave said authors to explain," he said.

Warner, who retired from international cricket more than two years ago, broke his silence about the scandal on Monday to throw his support behind Khawaja.

In a video posted on social media, Warner described his former teammate's account as 100% accurate and the CA investigation as "botched" and "rushed".

'VERY DIFFERENT VIEWS'

Media pundits, including former captain Michael Clarke, have demanded CA re-investigate ⁠the case.

However, Greenberg told local radio station SEN on Tuesday there was "no compelling reason" to reopen the investigation and could not see anything to be gained ⁠from it. He said players had "very different views" to Khawaja's version of events.

"There are specific details in his book that contradict the versions that have been provided by others," he said. "But we have said we’re comfortable with the outcome of the investigation based on the information we’ve received.

"That includes what we’ve seen from Usman, and our position hasn’t changed on that." Former Cricket Australia CEO James Sutherland, who was in charge of the governing body during the incident, declined to comment on Tuesday. Bancroft, who played his last international in 2019, declined to comment to Australian media on Monday.

He said in a 2021 ⁠interview with the Guardian that it was "self-explanatory" that teammates apart from Smith and Warner were aware of the ball-tampering plan. Captain Pat Cummins said in South Africa last month that he had spoken to Khawaja before the release of the autobiography and was not concerned about any potential fallout.

"Answered every question a million times. So, yeah, it was dealt with then," he said. Some commentators have questioned why Khawaja waited eight years to speak out and accused him of trying to boost sales of his book "Sabr". Khawaja responded on social media on Tuesday, saying he had no commercial motives.

"I'm very fortunate, I don't need the money," he said.

headline: Cricket Scotland suspends cricket ties with Afghanistan outside ICC events
description: The move follows similar decisions by Australia and England over treatment of women in Afghanistan
author: REUTERS
article_text:
Cricket ​Scotland ​said it will not schedule matches against Afghanistan outside International Cricket Council (ICC) events, citing concerns over the treatment of women and girls under ‌the Taliban government and broader human rights issues.

Women's sport has effectively disappeared in Afghanistan since the Taliban ‌returned to power in 2021, ⁠while ​access to education and employment opportunities ​for women has been ‌severely curtailed.

The Taliban say they ​respect women's rights in accordance with their interpretation of Islamic law and local customs and that internal matters should be ⁠addressed locally.

Scotland's move aligns with decisions by Cricket Australia and ‌the England and Wales Cricket Board to suspend bilateral ties with Afghanistan, which the ICC made a Full Member in 2017. "This policy will be ⁠kept under review annually or following ⁠any significant ICC ​decision or material ‌change in circumstances," Cricket Scotland said on Monday.

It added that its decision was based on its commitment to growing women's and girls' participation in the sport, as well as the humanitarian situation in Afghanistan.

Reuters has contacted the Afghanistan Cricket Board (ACB) for comment. Scotland have not ⁠faced Afghanistan in a full international match since the 2021 Twenty20 World ⁠Cup, but the governing body said the ACB had requested training facilities in July ahead of their men's series against Ireland.

The ACB had made another request for training facilities in Scotland in September regarding the T20 Afghanistan Premier League, it added. Cricket Scotland also said it would continue to consider ⁠its contractual obligations to players and would issue ​no-objection certificates (NOCs) if the ICC gives the Afghan league official approval.

"If an NOC is issued, participation by that player/s must not be interpreted as an endorsement by Cricket Scotland ​of the current Afghan regime or its ‌policies," the statement said.

headline: Inside the tech 2026: How AI keeps Pakistan's ride-hailing safer
description: inDrive integrates AI-driven risk detection and human judgment to make urban journeys safer for Pakistanis nationwide
article_text:
In Pakistan’s rapidly evolving digital economy, ride-hailing has transformed from a modern convenience into an essential urban utility. Leading this shift is inDrive, the nation’s top ride-hailing platform across major app stores.

Known globally for its peer-to-peer (P2P) model, inDrive distinctively allows passengers and drivers to negotiate fares directly based on real time market suggestions updated every 30 minutes, ensuring fair choice without algorithmic pressure or penalties. However, behind this transparent transaction model lies a sophisticated technological transformation involving the deployment of an AI-native safety ecosystem designed to protect millions of daily journeys across Pakistani cities. For inDrive, safety is viewed not as an isolated post-incident response, but as a continuous, intelligent system deeply integrated into every operational layer.Rather than relying exclusively on reactive measures, the company’s safety architecture harnesses artificial intelligence to shift focus towards preventive technologies.

By continuously evaluating interconnected data signals in real time, including account verification, communication streams, route mapping, and user feedback, the system builds a comprehensive model capable of identifying potential risks before they escalate. A foundational pillar of this AI shield begins before a trip even starts, during onboarding and account verification. Through automated machine learning algorithms, inDrive meticulously cross checks driver documentation, vehicle registration details, and profile photos. High level automation minimises human oversight errors and speeds up verification. Aditionally, intelligent fraud detection models actively spot duplicate profiles or multi-account usage on a single device, automatically restricting access to preserve platform integrity and protect honest drivers. Once a ride is requested, AI safeguards extend directly into user communication. Machine learning models continuously scan order feed details, usernames, and profile avatars for platform violations. In-app chats and photo exchanges are moderated by real time automated filters designed to instantly detect and suppress offensive content, explicit material, harassment, or prohibited subjects. In instances where severe safety policy violations occur, automated systems issue immediate account warnings or trigger temporary platform bans, referring serious cases directly to specialised safety resolution teams. Crucially, inDrive’s technological framework adheres to a human-centric approach.

While advanced machine learning processes millions of data points simultaneously to flag anomalies, the platform refuses to delegate final safety decisions strictly to algorithms. AI operates as an intelligent detection shield, identifying risk patterns and elevating critical flags to human safety experts who make the final operational determinations. By merging cutting-edge artificial intelligence with human judgment and a transparent P2P model, inDrive is redefining urban mobility security across Pakistan. In doing so, the platform demonstrates that true digital innovation must empower its users with both financial fairness and unwavering peace of mind.

headline: Cabinet committee approves changes to boards of NESPAK, HESCO and SEPCO
description: Finance minister calls for competent, experienced officials to serve as ex-officio directors on SOE boards
author: Web Desk
article_text:
The Cabinet Committee on State-Owned Enterprises (CCoSOEs) on Tuesday approved proposals concerning the appointment of a chairman/independent director at National Engineering Services Pakistan (NESPAK), the reconstitution of the board of Hyderabad Electric Supply Company (HESCO) and the appointment of an independent director to the board of Sukkur Electric Power Company (SEPCO), according to a statement issued by the Ministry of Finance.

The decisions were taken at a meeting of the committee chaired by Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb at the Finance Division. "The Cabinet Committee on State-Owned Enterprises (CCoSOEs) was held today under the chairmanship of Federal Minister for Finance and Revenue, Senator Muhammad Aurangzeb, at the Finance Division," the statement said.

Minister for Science and Technology Khalid Hussain Magsi also attended the meeting along with relevant Federal Secretaries and senior representatives of various ministries, divisions and regulatory bodies.

The statement said the committee considered two agenda items concerning the appointment of a chairman/independent director at NESPAK and the reconstitution of HESCO's board, alongside the appointment of an independent director to SEPCO's board.

"After deliberations, both proposals were approved," the Finance Division said.

"The finance minister emphasised that government representatives serving as ex-officio directors on these boards should be appropriately placed, competent and possess the requisite experience and institutional understanding to effectively represent their respective divisions," the statement concluded.

The appointments came amid the government's broader efforts to improve governance and performance at state-owned enterprises (SOEs), particularly power distribution companies. In May 2025, the boards of most distribution companies had been reconstituted, but the process for Hyderabad Electric Supply Company (HESCO) and Sukkur Electric Power Company (SEPCO) was still being finalised.

The government had said the new boards were intended to strengthen corporate governance, strategic oversight and operational efficiency.

The reconstitution of distribution company boards followed concerns over their performance and governance. In June 2024, the government had moved to replace the boards of loss-making power distribution companies amid allegations of poor governance and political influence.

The Power Division had cited projected losses of Rs589 billion across 10 government-owned distribution companies during the then-ongoing fiscal year.

The State-Owned Enterprises (Governance and Operations) Amendment Bill, 2024, was subsequently passed by the Senate in July that year. The legislation aimed to improve the efficiency and independence of SOE boards by introducing an institutionalised mechanism for appointing independent directors, providing for a majority of independent directors and setting criteria for their removal and tenure.

headline: Russell Brand's ex, Jemima Goldsmith, accuses him of abuse after his sentencing
description: Jemima Goldsmith says she called police during alleged violent incident involving Russell Brand in 2014
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Jemima Goldsmith has accused former boyfriend Russell Brand of violence, coercive control and abuse during their relationship, revealing that she once called the police following an alleged violent incident at her home.

Goldsmith, who dated the comedian for approximately a year around 2014, made the allegations in a statement shared on social media on Monday.

She said she had contacted police to have Brand removed from her house during an incident in 2014 but decided against pressing charges.

The 52-year-old explained that she was concerned about the effect media attention could have on her teenage children at the time. She also expressed support for the women who testified against Brand during his criminal trial, saying she was "glad and relieved" he had "finally faced justice".

Brand, 51, was sentenced to 10-and-a-half years in prison on Monday after being convicted of rape and three counts of sexual assault involving four women between 2004 and 2009. He was found not guilty of two other rape charges and one count of attempted indecent assault.

Goldsmith said she had not seen or spoken to Brand since 2014 but had assisted journalists investigating allegations against him. She also said she would have been willing to testify about his alleged behaviour if the journalists had faced legal action.

Her statement addressed a 2015 injunction involving Goldsmith, Brand and a woman named Szilvia Berki. Goldsmith said Berki had visited her home in June 2014 to give Brand a massage, but the arrangement did not proceed after Goldsmith arrived.

According to Goldsmith, Berki later alleged that Brand had pushed her while she was leaving. Goldsmith said she did not witness anything untoward and that police concluded there was no case to answer after reviewing her statement and CCTV footage.

Goldsmith also claimed Berki subsequently sent threatening and antisemitic messages. She said recent coverage of the injunction had exposed her to online abuse.

headline: US attempts new peace push at first Russia-Ukraine talks in nine months
description: Rubio describes US-brokered meeting as 'very productive', Zelenskyy says talks included humanitarian, security issues
author: Reuters
article_text:
Russian and Ukrainian officials met in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday for their first peace talks since February as US President Donald Trump's envoys launched a new push ​to end the war in Ukraine.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio described the US-brokered meeting as very productive, without giving details.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called the talks "constructive and quite substantive" and ‌said they had included humanitarian and security issues.

"The release of prisoners (of war) is a priority. They spoke in detail about the substance of security guarantees for Ukraine and the foundations for ensuring these guarantees function over the long term," he posted on X.

"Real tools are needed to block any recurrence of the war. The need for de-escalation steps was also touched upon."

Gulf between Russia and Ukraine on terms for a deal

Despite public optimism from Trump, the warring sides remain far apart ​on terms for a possible settlement, more than 4-1/2 years after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

Russian forces control about a fifth of Ukraine, but territory is not the only issue at ​stake. Others include future security guarantees, which both sides say they need, and Moscow's demands that Ukraine adopt neutral status and not join NATO.

There was no immediate ⁠comment from Russia on what was discussed. A second day of negotiations was scheduled for Wednesday.

The meeting followed US contacts with both sides in recent weeks that Trump's representative Jared Kushner said had narrowed ​gaps between their positions. Addressing delegates at the start of the meeting, he said Washington had some good ideas on how to make progress.

Trump has intensified pressure on Kyiv to reach a deal, saying it is ​time for Ukraine to end the war or face "a very bad thing". Last week he said the war was close to being settled in a "big beautiful agreement" that might involve the security of all Europe, but he has frequently predicted breakthroughs that have not materialised.

Russia wants security framework to come first

Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov underlined Moscow's preference for negotiating a broad European security framework before tackling the specifics of the war.

"The idea of defining clear parameters for a future security ​architecture, and only then moving on to resolving the actual Russia-Ukraine conflict, is absolutely reasonable," he said in Moscow.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said on Monday wider security talks should only follow ​a ceasefire. Lavrov rejected the notion of a truce, saying the Europeans were trying to secure breathing space for Ukraine.

The new American drive for a deal has galvanised European officials into pushing for a place at the table to ‌seek an ⁠end to Europe's deadliest conflict since World War Two.

Before the main meeting, the Ukrainians met separately with European, NATO and European Union representatives and the two American envoys, Kushner and Steve Witkoff.

France said there could be no lasting peace in Ukraine without addressing European security, and that this required the Europeans' involvement.

European governments have mostly shunned contact with Russian President Vladimir Putin during the war, though Finnish and Norwegian leaders held a call with him on October 27 that was criticised by some of their European peers.

Russia had made clear it did not see a place for Europeans at the meeting with the Ukrainians and Americans.

Rubio, speaking in ​Paris, said the US aimed to expand the ​trilateral talks to include Europe at some point. "In ⁠the days to come, perhaps we can make some progress on including them in that front," he said.

New attacks

On the eve of the talks, Trump said Washington saw a "very strong inclination" towards ending the war, with both sides "tired of fighting".

Overnight, Russian forces struck 10 Ukrainian regions in attacks on five major electrical substations that ​caused power outages and killed two people, officials said.

Russia said an industrial facility was damaged in a Ukrainian drone attack in the northern city ​of Novgorod. Industry sources said ⁠Ukrainian drone attacks on Russian oil refineries since late October had cut Russia's refining capacity by about 30%.

There has been no public sign that Putin is willing to drop his demand that Ukraine surrender the entire eastern region of Donbas before a peace deal can be struck. Zelenskyy has refused to hand over land that his forces have died defending.

Russian advances have slowed to a virtual halt, but Moscow has been pounding Ukrainian cities and energy facilities, ⁠while Ukraine has ​stepped up attacks on Russian oil refineries and other infrastructure.

US negotiators believe Zelenskyy and Putin may be willing to reach ​a compromise on territory, with each ceding a little, a US official told Reuters on Monday.

Under the proposed deal, Ukraine would get an end to the war, security guarantees and a roadmap to accession to the EU.

A senior Ukrainian official denied the government ​would consider such concessions.

article_html:
Russian and Ukrainian officials met in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday for their first peace talks since February as US President Donald Trump's envoys launched a new push ​to end the war in Ukraine.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio described the US-brokered meeting as very productive, without giving details.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called the talks "constructive and quite substantive" and ‌said they had included humanitarian and security issues.

Read: Putin agrees to resume US-mediated Ukraine talks

Russia and Ukraine held their first U.S.-mediated talks in nine months on ending their war, with U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio calling the meeting "very productive" and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy saying the session was "constructive and quite substantive."…

— PBS News (@NewsHour) November 10, 2026

"The release of prisoners (of war) is a priority. They spoke in detail about the substance of security guarantees for Ukraine and the foundations for ensuring these guarantees function over the long term," he posted on X.

Received a report from our negotiating team. Today was the first day of meetings in Abu Dhabi. First came a meeting with our European and American partners, followed by a trilateral format between our delegation and the American and Russian delegations. I am grateful to all of… pic.twitter.com/mesjgP1U8S

— Volodymyr Zelenskyy / Володимир Зеленський (@ZelenskyyUa) November 10, 2026

"Real tools are needed to block any recurrence of the war. The need for de-escalation steps was also touched upon."

Gulf between Russia and Ukraine on terms for a deal

Despite public optimism from Trump, the warring sides remain far apart ​on terms for a possible settlement, more than 4-1/2 years after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

Russian forces control about a fifth of Ukraine, but territory is not the only issue at ​stake. Others include future security guarantees, which both sides say they need, and Moscow's demands that Ukraine adopt neutral status and not join NATO.

There was no immediate ⁠comment from Russia on what was discussed. A second day of negotiations was scheduled for Wednesday.

The meeting followed US contacts with both sides in recent weeks that Trump's representative Jared Kushner said had narrowed ​gaps between their positions. Addressing delegates at the start of the meeting, he said Washington had some good ideas on how to make progress.

Trump has intensified pressure on Kyiv to reach a deal, saying it is ​time for Ukraine to end the war or face "a very bad thing". Last week he said the war was close to being settled in a "big beautiful agreement" that might involve the security of all Europe, but he has frequently predicted breakthroughs that have not materialised.

Russia wants security framework to come first

Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov underlined Moscow's preference for negotiating a broad European security framework before tackling the specifics of the war.

"The idea of defining clear parameters for a future security ​architecture, and only then moving on to resolving the actual Russia-Ukraine conflict, is absolutely reasonable," he said in Moscow.

Russia's Foreign Minister Lavrov:

We will not agree to another truce, another ceasefire — whatever you want to call it — without understanding what comes next. pic.twitter.com/Mkja3XRoSL

— Clash Report (@clashreport) November 10, 2026

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said on Monday wider security talks should only follow ​a ceasefire. Lavrov rejected the notion of a truce, saying the Europeans were trying to secure breathing space for Ukraine.

"Any meaningful discussions about Europe's security architecture can only be undertaken once a ceasefire in Ukraine has been achieved," Ursula von der Leyen said in reply to Jared Kushner's proposal. pic.twitter.com/2Y6DYmg4C2

— euronews (@euronews) November 9, 2026

The new American drive for a deal has galvanised European officials into pushing for a place at the table to ‌seek an ⁠end to Europe's deadliest conflict since World War Two.

Before the main meeting, the Ukrainians met separately with European, NATO and European Union representatives and the two American envoys, Kushner and Steve Witkoff.

France said there could be no lasting peace in Ukraine without addressing European security, and that this required the Europeans' involvement.

European governments have mostly shunned contact with Russian President Vladimir Putin during the war, though Finnish and Norwegian leaders held a call with him on October 27 that was criticised by some of their European peers.

Russia had made clear it did not see a place for Europeans at the meeting with the Ukrainians and Americans.

Rubio, speaking in ​Paris, said the US aimed to expand the ​trilateral talks to include Europe at some point. "In ⁠the days to come, perhaps we can make some progress on including them in that front," he said.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio on European involvement in Russia-Ukraine negotiations: "Europe set the table...they're right alongside us." pic.twitter.com/fRuhT1vLXA

— CSPAN (@cspan) November 10, 2026

New attacks

On the eve of the talks, Trump said Washington saw a "very strong inclination" towards ending the war, with both sides "tired of fighting".

Read More: Russia, Ukraine trade fresh attacks

Overnight, Russian forces struck 10 Ukrainian regions in attacks on five major electrical substations that ​caused power outages and killed two people, officials said.

Russia said an industrial facility was damaged in a Ukrainian drone attack in the northern city ​of Novgorod. Industry sources said ⁠Ukrainian drone attacks on Russian oil refineries since late October had cut Russia's refining capacity by about 30%.

There has been no public sign that Putin is willing to drop his demand that Ukraine surrender the entire eastern region of Donbas before a peace deal can be struck. Zelenskyy has refused to hand over land that his forces have died defending.

Russian advances have slowed to a virtual halt, but Moscow has been pounding Ukrainian cities and energy facilities, ⁠while Ukraine has ​stepped up attacks on Russian oil refineries and other infrastructure.

US negotiators believe Zelenskyy and Putin may be willing to reach ​a compromise on territory, with each ceding a little, a US official told Reuters on Monday.

Under the proposed deal, Ukraine would get an end to the war, security guarantees and a roadmap to accession to the EU.

A senior Ukrainian official denied the government ​would consider such concessions.

Last week he said the war was close to being settled in a "big beautiful agreement" that might involve the security of all Europe, but he has frequently predicted breakthroughs that have not materialised.

Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov underlined Moscow's preference for negotiating a broad European security framework before tackling the specifics of the war.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said on Monday wider security talks should only follow a ceasefire. Lavrov rejected the notion of a truce, saying the Europeans were trying to secure breathing space for Ukraine.

The new American drive for a deal has galvanised European officials into pushing for a place at the table to ‌seek an ⁠end to Europe's deadliest conflict since World War Two.

Before the main meeting, the Ukrainians met separately with European, NATO and European Union representatives and the two American envoys, Kushner and Steve Witkoff.

France said there could be no lasting peace in Ukraine without addressing European security, and that this required the Europeans' involvement.

European governments have mostly shunned contact with Russian President Vladimir Putin during the war, though Finnish and Norwegian leaders held a call with him on October 27 that was criticised by some of their European peers.

Russia had made clear it did not see a place for Europeans at the meeting with the Ukrainians and Americans.

Rubio, speaking in Paris, said the US aimed to expand the trilateral talks to include Europe at some point. "In ⁠the days to come, perhaps we can make some progress on including them in that front," he said.

New attacks

On the eve of the talks, Trump said Washington saw a "very strong inclination" towards ending the war, with both sides "tired of fighting".

Overnight, Russian forces struck 10 Ukrainian regions in attacks on five major electrical substations that caused power outages and killed two people, officials said.

Russia said an industrial facility was damaged in a Ukrainian drone attack in the northern city of Novgorod. Industry sources said ⁠Ukrainian drone attacks on Russian oil refineries since late October had cut Russia's refining capacity by about 30%.

There has been no public sign that Putin is willing to drop his demand that Ukraine surrender the entire eastern region of Donbas before a peace deal can be struck. Zelenskyy has refused to hand over land that his forces have died defending.

Russian advances have slowed to a virtual halt, but Moscow has been pounding Ukrainian cities and energy facilities, ⁠while Ukraine has stepped up attacks on Russian oil refineries and other infrastructure.

US negotiators believe Zelenskyy and Putin may be willing to reach a compromise on territory, with each ceding a little, a US official told Reuters on Monday.

Under the proposed deal, Ukraine would get an end to the war, security guarantees and a roadmap to accession to the EU.

A senior Ukrainian official denied the government would consider such concessions.

headline: BISE Bannu postpones SSC Part-II exams in North Waziristan amid security concerns
description: The board says it will announce a revised examination schedule later
author: Nasruminallah
article_text:
The Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education (BISE) Bannu postponed the remaining SSC Part-II examinations in North Waziristan until further orders amid security concerns, as authorities imposed a curfew in Mir Ali during an ongoing security operation and closed the Bannu-Miranshah Road to traffic, it emerged on Tuesday.

According to a notification issued by the Bannu board on Monday, the decision was taken on the directions of the North Waziristan deputy commissioner, conveyed through a letter dated November 8.

The board said the remaining papers at all examination centres across the district had been postponed until further orders and that it would announce a revised examination schedule later. It advised students, parents and educational institutions to await further instructions.

However, the papers at Cadet College Razmak in North Waziristan and the Bakakhel tehsil examination centres along Miranshah Road were to be held according to the original schedule.

Meanwhile, authorities imposed a curfew in Mir Ali for the duration of the ongoing security operation. The administration also said that curfew restrictions would continue from Isha to Mir Ali and Bobli.

In a message about the restrictions, area representative and development council member Malik Rohullah Khan said the GOC North had issued instructions following his request, allowing local residents to visit markets in Miranshah and Datta Khel to purchase essential daily-use items.

He added that residents wishing to travel outside North Waziristan could use the Miranshah, Isha and Razmak routes.

The postponement came amid intensified security operations in North Waziristan. Earlier in the day, security forces had recovered 700 kilogrammes of locally made explosives, an Al-Farooq missile, 200 kilogrammes of urea and other equipment during search and clearance operations in different areas of the district.

A day earlier, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) had said security forces recovered improvised explosive devices, explosives, weapons and ammunition from two terrorist hideouts inside mosques in Muzak village, on the southern outskirts of Mir Ali. The hideouts were allegedly being used to store explosives and operate torture cells, while a sanitisation operation was underway in the area.

On October 7, security forces killed 13 terrorists in an intelligence-based operation in North Waziristan, a day after five others were killed and two wounded in a separate operation. On October 1, security forces also killed three terrorists in Mir Ali and foiled an attempt to intercept a ration truck near Mir Ali Bazaar, according to security sources.

MIRANSHAH:

The Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education (BISE) Bannu postponed the remaining SSC Part-II examinations in North Waziristan until further orders amid security concerns, as authorities imposed a curfew in Mir Ali during an ongoing security operation and closed the Bannu-Miranshah Road to traffic, it emerged on Tuesday.

According to a notification issued by the Bannu board on Monday, the decision was taken on the directions of the North Waziristan deputy commissioner, conveyed through a letter dated November 8.

The board said the remaining papers at all examination centres across the district had been postponed until further orders and that it would announce a revised examination schedule later. It advised students, parents and educational institutions to await further instructions.

However, the papers at Cadet College Razmak in North Waziristan and the Bakakhel tehsil examination centres along Miranshah Road were to be held according to the original schedule.

Meanwhile, authorities imposed a curfew in Mir Ali for the duration of the ongoing security operation. The administration also said that curfew restrictions would continue from Isha to Mir Ali and Bobli. 

In a message about the restrictions, area representative and development council member Malik Rohullah Khan said the GOC North had issued instructions following his request, allowing local residents to visit markets in Miranshah and Datta Khel to purchase essential daily-use items.

He added that residents wishing to travel outside North Waziristan could use the Miranshah, Isha and Razmak routes.

Read: IEDs, ammunition recovered from terrorist hideouts inside mosques in North Waziristan: ISPR

The postponement came amid intensified security operations in North Waziristan. Earlier in the day, security forces had recovered 700 kilogrammes of locally made explosives, an Al-Farooq missile, 200 kilogrammes of urea and other equipment during search and clearance operations in different areas of the district.

A day earlier, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) had said security forces recovered improvised explosive devices, explosives, weapons and ammunition from two terrorist hideouts inside mosques in Muzak village, on the southern outskirts of Mir Ali. The hideouts were allegedly being used to store explosives and operate torture cells, while a sanitisation operation was underway in the area.

On October 7, security forces killed 13 terrorists in an intelligence-based operation in North Waziristan, a day after five others were killed and two wounded in a separate operation. On October 1, security forces also killed three terrorists in Mir Ali and foiled an attempt to intercept a ration truck near Mir Ali Bazaar, according to security sources.

headline: Eleven dead, 50 injured in Bulgarian motorway pile-up
description: Interior ministry general secretary says fog likely cause of accident
author: Reuters
article_text:
Eleven people died in a traffic accident involving dozens of vehicles on both sides of a foggy stretch of highway in eastern Bulgaria on Tuesday, Prime Minister Rumen Radev said.

Police, firefighters and ambulance crews rushed to the scene on the A1 road that links the capital Sofia with the eastern city of Burgas. Images on local media showed cars and trucks piled up across six lanes of highway, many crushed, overturned, or veered off to the side.

50 injured people were transported to hospital, according to the interior ministry.

Radev described the accident as a "tragedy" in a statement during a visit to Bulgaria by European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen. He said that he had deployed aircraft to evacuate the wounded and planned to visit the scene.

Von der Leyen said she would cut her visit short. "I would like to express my deepest condolences and I would like to pay respects to the rescue teams," von der Leyen said.

Briefing reporters at the site of the accident, General Secretary of the Interior Ministry, Lyubomir Nikolov, said that fog was the likely cause of the accident which started with a collision between a bus and a truck on the side of the highway heading towards Burgas.

Chief Inspector Todor Mishinev from the Yambol Regional Directorate of the Ministry of Internal Affairs told Nova TV that some people were still trapped in their cars. "Right now, the priority is rescue operations. Once they are completed, the procedural and investigative actions will be carried out," he said.
