headline: Ocarina of Time remake unknowingly brings back original Navi voice actor through blind audition
description: Kaori Mizuhashi reprises her role as Navi after blind auditions led Nintendo to rehire her
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Nintendo has unknowingly brought back an original voice actor from the Nintendo 64 version of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for its 2026 remake, after blind auditions led the development team to select the same performer.

During a recent instalment of Nintendo's Ask the Developer interview series, music lead Masato Ohashi discussed the process of recreating the game's original soundtrack and sound effects while introducing a more orchestral approach.

The interview also covered the remake's voice acting, including the return of Navi, Link's fairy companion known for phrases such as "Hey, listen!" Japanese voice actor Kaori Mizuhashi has reprised her role as the character, despite the development team initially being unaware of her involvement in the original game.

Producer Eiji Aonuma explained the unexpected discovery, saying, “As fate would have it, one of the actors we selected had actually voiced the same character in the Nintendo 64 version. None of us saw that coming.”

The auditions were conducted blindly, meaning the team selected Mizuhashi without realising she had previously portrayed Navi. Her return marks a connection between the remake and the original 1998 release.

The American version of the remake, meanwhile, features Lisa Reimold as Navi. None of the actors from the original American voice cast returned for the new version.

Ohashi also discussed the work involved in updating the game's soundscape, including the use of live recordings of an actual ocarina player to recreate the breathiness heard when Link performs music in the game.

headline: IHC orders one-hour jail meeting for Imran Khan, Bushra Bibi with lawyers
description: Latif Khosa refuses to argue £190m case appeals until allowed to meet PTI founder as hearing is adjourned for 10 days
author: Fiaz Mahmood
article_text:
The Islamabad High Court (IHC) on Tuesday ordered a one-hour jail meeting between Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf founder Imran Khan and his wife, Bushra Bibi, and their lawyers, Barrister Salman Safdar and Latif Khosa, in the £190 million case, directing counsel to begin arguments on the appeals at the next hearing.

A division bench comprising Chief Justice Sarfraz Dogar and Justice Muhammad Asif heard the appeals. The bench also directed that arguments begin at the next hearing and that the paper books in the cases be prepared beforehand. The appeals were adjourned for 10 days.

At the outset, Khosa told the court that an earlier order allowing him to meet Imran had not been implemented. Chief Justice Sardar Sarfraz Dogar, who headed the bench, clarified that the previous order had been for Barrister Salman Safdar to meet the PTI founder, not Khosa.

“You are not the one whose meeting was ordered; the order was for Salman Safdar’s meeting,” the chief justice told Khosa.

Khosa responded that an order for a meeting already existed but that no meeting had taken place. He said his undertaking to argue the appeals was conditional on being allowed to meet Imran.

The chief justice, however, said it had already been settled that Khosa would argue the appeals and urged him to begin. He asked Islamabad Advocate General Naveed Malik whether arrangements could be made for the meeting within one or two days.

“I want to remove this obstacle and proceed with the matter,” Chief Justice Dogar said, adding that he wanted Khosa to begin his arguments even if he had only two sentences to make. He also said the lawyer could argue for two or four hours.

Khosa subsequently requested a one-hour meeting with Imran, prompting the chief justice to direct the advocate general to arrange it within two days.

During the hearing, Safdar also raised concerns over delays in his access to Imran and Bushra Bibi, telling the court that he had met the PTI founder after seven months and his wife after 11 months. “I felt embarrassed when I met my client after 11 months,” he said, adding that he had received instructions from both to argue their appeals.

He requested the court to provide the paper books and grant him time to prepare his arguments. He said Bushra Bibi's meeting with her lawyer after 11 months reflected a serious lack of trust.

Safdar also asked the court to fix appeals against sentences in the other cases for hearing and take up a miscellaneous application. He said his first protest in the matter concerned the failure to arrange a meeting with Bushra Bibi for 11 months. He added that he had filed an affidavit in the case, something he had never done before.

The lawyer said he could file a fresh bail application on new grounds but had not done so yet. He then drew the court's attention to Bushra Bibi's health, saying she had been wearing dark glasses and that her eyesight had deteriorated.

According to Safdar, jail authorities had informed him that her next operation was scheduled for November 15. He said he did not know who was treating her or where she was receiving treatment.

“I am not asking for bail; a medical board should be formed,” he told the court, seeking an independent assessment of her condition. He added that even if Bushra Bibi was not entitled to bail, she could be granted temporary bail for four to six weeks to receive treatment.

Safdar said women were entitled to concessions in such matters and asked the court to obtain complete medical reports from Adiala jail. He maintained that proper treatment was not possible in prison and questioned why Bushra Bibi had been returned to her cell on the same day after an operation.

He told the court that doctors had performed emergency surgery and warned that he would regret arguing the appeal if her condition worsened. “If I argue the appeal and my client becomes blind in jail, I will regret it,” Safdar said.

He also conveyed Imran's concerns about his own health, saying the PTI founder had told him that his blood pressure was not under control and had risen above 190, putting him at risk of a brain haemorrhage. Safdar added that Imran had said his eyesight had improved.

Safdar requested a meeting with Imran lasting between one and one-and-a-half hours, while Salman Akram Raja, another counsel for the PTI founder, asked the court to allow both lawyers to meet him together.

The chief justice observed that Safdar had already met Imran. The court also remarked that allowing the lawyers to meet him together could lead to a request for five people to be permitted to meet him.

The advocate general told the court that medical treatment was a fundamental right and that the government was not neglecting its responsibilities.

“All medical facilities are being provided,” he said, presenting a record of the treatment provided to Bushra Bibi.

He said the matter concerned not just one prisoner but around 10,000 inmates. He also referred to records summoned by the Federal Constitutional Court (FCC) from the Supreme Court in cases involving three prisoners.

The chief justice observed that applications concerning Imran's health were pending before the FCC. Safdar, however, told the bench that no case concerning Bushra Bibi was pending before that court.

During the proceedings, a National Accountability Bureau prosecutor asked Safdar to submit an undertaking regarding the proceedings.

At the conclusion of the hearing, the court directed that the paper books be provided to the lawyers and prepared before the next hearing. It also instructed counsel to begin their arguments at the next hearing, following the arrangement of Khosa's meeting with Imran.

Access to Imran and Bushra Bibi at Adiala Jail has remained restricted, with meetings between the PTI founder and his lawyers becoming increasingly infrequent. Authorities have denied weekly meetings between Imran and his family and legal team since December 2025.

In April 2026, Barrister Salman Safdar met Imran for a 60-minute legal consultation on the IHC’s orders, but Bushra Bibi was not brought in to join the meeting. Safdar said Imran and Bushra were being kept in solitary confinement for almost 24 hours a day, with no access to books, television, family or lawyers.

The courts subsequently intervened to facilitate access. In June, the IHC directed authorities to arrange a meeting between Imran, Bushra Bibi and their legal counsel within seven days to complete legal formalities and pursue their appeals.

The Supreme Court also ordered weekly meetings between Imran and his family in August. Imran’s sister Noreen Niazi met him at Adiala Jail on August 18 after a gap of around nine months, with the meeting lasting approximately 15 minutes. However, Safdar was not allowed to meet both his clients again until November 2, when jail authorities facilitated a 40-minute meeting with Imran and Bushra Bibi.

article_html:
ISLAMABAD:

The Islamabad High Court (IHC) on Tuesday ordered a one-hour jail meeting between Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf founder Imran Khan and his wife, Bushra Bibi, and their lawyers, Barrister Salman Safdar and Latif Khosa, in the £190 million case, directing counsel to begin arguments on the appeals at the next hearing.

A division bench comprising Chief Justice Sarfraz Dogar and Justice Muhammad Asif heard the appeals. The bench also directed that arguments begin at the next hearing and that the paper books in the cases be prepared beforehand. The appeals were adjourned for 10 days.

At the outset, Khosa told the court that an earlier order allowing him to meet Imran had not been implemented. Chief Justice Sardar Sarfraz Dogar, who headed the bench, clarified that the previous order had been for Barrister Salman Safdar to meet the PTI founder, not Khosa.

“You are not the one whose meeting was ordered; the order was for Salman Safdar’s meeting,” the chief justice told Khosa.

Khosa responded that an order for a meeting already existed but that no meeting had taken place. He said his undertaking to argue the appeals was conditional on being allowed to meet Imran.

The chief justice, however, said it had already been settled that Khosa would argue the appeals and urged him to begin. He asked Islamabad Advocate General Naveed Malik whether arrangements could be made for the meeting within one or two days.

Read: Long wait ends as lawyer meets jailed Imran, Bushra

“I want to remove this obstacle and proceed with the matter,” Chief Justice Dogar said, adding that he wanted Khosa to begin his arguments even if he had only two sentences to make. He also said the lawyer could argue for two or four hours.

Khosa subsequently requested a one-hour meeting with Imran, prompting the chief justice to direct the advocate general to arrange it within two days.

During the hearing, Safdar also raised concerns over delays in his access to Imran and Bushra Bibi, telling the court that he had met the PTI founder after seven months and his wife after 11 months. “I felt embarrassed when I met my client after 11 months,” he said, adding that he had received instructions from both to argue their appeals.

He requested the court to provide the paper books and grant him time to prepare his arguments. He said Bushra Bibi's meeting with her lawyer after 11 months reflected a serious lack of trust.

Safdar also asked the court to fix appeals against sentences in the other cases for hearing and take up a miscellaneous application. He said his first protest in the matter concerned the failure to arrange a meeting with Bushra Bibi for 11 months. He added that he had filed an affidavit in the case, something he had never done before.

The lawyer said he could file a fresh bail application on new grounds but had not done so yet. He then drew the court's attention to Bushra Bibi's health, saying she had been wearing dark glasses and that her eyesight had deteriorated.

Read: PIMS doctors visit Imran, Bushra

According to Safdar, jail authorities had informed him that her next operation was scheduled for November 15. He said he did not know who was treating her or where she was receiving treatment.

“I am not asking for bail; a medical board should be formed,” he told the court, seeking an independent assessment of her condition. He added that even if Bushra Bibi was not entitled to bail, she could be granted temporary bail for four to six weeks to receive treatment.

Safdar said women were entitled to concessions in such matters and asked the court to obtain complete medical reports from Adiala jail. He maintained that proper treatment was not possible in prison and questioned why Bushra Bibi had been returned to her cell on the same day after an operation.

He told the court that doctors had performed emergency surgery and warned that he would regret arguing the appeal if her condition worsened. “If I argue the appeal and my client becomes blind in jail, I will regret it,” Safdar said.

He also conveyed Imran's concerns about his own health, saying the PTI founder had told him that his blood pressure was not under control and had risen above 190, putting him at risk of a brain haemorrhage. Safdar added that Imran had said his eyesight had improved.

Also Read: Gohar demands immediate implementation of SC order on Imran's medical treatment

Safdar requested a meeting with Imran lasting between one and one-and-a-half hours, while Salman Akram Raja, another counsel for the PTI founder, asked the court to allow both lawyers to meet him together.

The chief justice observed that Safdar had already met Imran. The court also remarked that allowing the lawyers to meet him together could lead to a request for five people to be permitted to meet him.

The advocate general told the court that medical treatment was a fundamental right and that the government was not neglecting its responsibilities.

“All medical facilities are being provided,” he said, presenting a record of the treatment provided to Bushra Bibi.

He said the matter concerned not just one prisoner but around 10,000 inmates. He also referred to records summoned by the Federal Constitutional Court (FCC) from the Supreme Court in cases involving three prisoners.

The chief justice observed that applications concerning Imran's health were pending before the FCC. Safdar, however, told the bench that no case concerning Bushra Bibi was pending before that court.

During the proceedings, a National Accountability Bureau prosecutor asked Safdar to submit an undertaking regarding the proceedings.

Read More: IHC fixes Imran and Bushra's appeals against sentences in £190m case for Nov 10

At the conclusion of the hearing, the court directed that the paper books be provided to the lawyers and prepared before the next hearing. It also instructed counsel to begin their arguments at the next hearing, following the arrangement of Khosa's meeting with Imran.

Access to Imran and Bushra Bibi at Adiala Jail has remained restricted, with meetings between the PTI founder and his lawyers becoming increasingly infrequent. Authorities have denied weekly meetings between Imran and his family and legal team since December 2025.

In April 2026, Barrister Salman Safdar met Imran for a 60-minute legal consultation on the IHC’s orders, but Bushra Bibi was not brought in to join the meeting. Safdar said Imran and Bushra were being kept in solitary confinement for almost 24 hours a day, with no access to books, television, family or lawyers.

The courts subsequently intervened to facilitate access. In June, the IHC directed authorities to arrange a meeting between Imran, Bushra Bibi and their legal counsel within seven days to complete legal formalities and pursue their appeals.

The Supreme Court also ordered weekly meetings between Imran and his family in August. Imran’s sister Noreen Niazi met him at Adiala Jail on August 18 after a gap of around nine months, with the meeting lasting approximately 15 minutes. However, Safdar was not allowed to meet both his clients again until November 2, when jail authorities facilitated a 40-minute meeting with Imran and Bushra Bibi.

headline: GTA 6 digital pre-orders reportedly almost reach 8m ahead of launch
description: New report estimates GTA 6 has generated $751m in digital pre-orders, led by PS5 buyers
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Grand Theft Auto 6 has reportedly accumulated an estimated 7.71 million digital pre-orders approximately two weeks before launch, with potential revenue reaching $751 million, according to analytics firm Sensor Tower.

The figures are based on the company's modelling of consumer activity and have not been confirmed by Rockstar Games or parent company Take-Two Interactive.

PlayStation 5 accounts for 74% of the estimated pre-orders, representing approximately $559 million in projected revenue. Xbox Series X|S makes up the remaining 26%, equivalent to around $192 million. Sensor Tower's data does not establish a definitive reason for the difference between the platforms.

The majority of customers have also reportedly opted for the more expensive edition. Earlier Sensor Tower estimates indicate that 89% of pre-orders were for the $100 Ultimate Edition, while 11% selected the $80 Standard Edition. The split was broadly similar across both platforms.

The estimated pre-order figures also place GTA 6 ahead of Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2, with Sensor Tower reporting a 148% lead at the equivalent point before launch. However, the comparison covers US digital pre-orders only and excludes physical sales.

Sensor Tower senior vice president and Video Game Insights general manager Karl Kontus estimates that GTA 6 could reach approximately 25 million pre-orders by launch, rather than the 40 million or more associated with a typical pre-order trajectory. He has suggested that demand is unusually concentrated in the pre-launch period.

Kontus also referenced Cyberpunk 2077, which recorded eight million publisher-confirmed pre-orders before release. His projection of approximately $2 billion in GTA 6 pre-order sales by launch remains an analyst estimate.

headline: Pakistan blames India's Diwali fireworks for Lahore's toxic air
description: Marriyum Aurangzeb says pollutants been carried by light winds and air drifting from Delhi in aftermath of Diwali
author: Reuters
article_text:
The Punjab government blamed poor air quality this week on pollution drifting from India, where firecrackers set off during the Hindu festival of Diwali over the weekend blanketed much of the north in toxic smog.

Lahore topped Swiss group IQAir's ranking of the world's most polluted major cities for a second day on Tuesday, with an air quality index (AQI) of 263, categorised as "very unhealthy".

The city's concentration of PM2.5, harmful airborne particles small enough to penetrate deep into the lungs, was 37.2 times above the World Health Organisation's annual guideline, IQAir said.

Punjab Senior Minister Marriyum Aurangzeb said pollutants had been carried into the region by light winds and air drifting from India in the aftermath of Diwali. "However, air pollution is expected to gradually decrease from early afternoon as weather conditions improve and winds shift direction," she said.

IQAir ranked Delhi the world's second-most polluted major city on Tuesday, with an AQI of 188. Indian government data showed that firecrackers were responsible for nearly 55 per cent of the PM2.5 in the Indian capital a day earlier.

Vehicle emissions, construction dust and smoke from crop-waste burning are also major contributors to winter pollution on both sides of the border.

Pakistan had similarly attributed its toxic air in 2024 to crop-waste burning in Indian Punjab, but officials from India's weather department had said at the time that the wind direction meant the airflow was actually from Pakistan into India.

Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party has also blamed crop-waste burning in Indian Punjab — governed by a regional opposition party — for Delhi's poor air quality this month. Local media reported a sevenfold increase in farm fires in the state on Sunday, when Diwali was celebrated.

Indian Punjab's state government, however, says incidents of crop-waste burning have fallen compared with previous years.

headline: Public service wins elections as political slogans have limited lifespan: Maryam Nawaz
description: Says voters judge parties by performance, criticises the opposition's reliance on political narratives
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz on Tuesday said political narratives, allegations and slogans could not replace public service, stressing that voters ultimately judged political parties on their performance and the development work carried out for their welfare.

Addressing a Honhaar Scholarship and laptop distribution ceremony at Government Comprehensive High School in Jhelum, Maryam said political parties could not sustain public support through rhetoric alone if they failed to deliver services to the people.

She said political narratives had a limited lifespan and that parties which failed to serve the public eventually lost their relevance.

The chief minister referred to two elections held in Sahiwal and Gujranwala, saying that the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) had secured victories in both despite opposition parties joining forces against it.

She said opposition parties had formed alliances and made efforts to defeat the PML-N but had failed to secure public support.

CM Maryam maintained that the results demonstrated that voters preferred development and public service over political slogans and allegations, adding that the PML-N had repeatedly received public support over the past four decades because people associated the party with development and the resolution of their problems.

The chief minister criticised political opponents for their reliance on political narratives rather than practical measures to address public concerns. She said popularity could be measured through electoral results and public confidence rather than claims made by political parties.

Referring to the opposition's electoral performance, CM Maryam claimed that political opponents had lost elections both while in government and after moving into opposition. She said people voted for political parties when development projects and public services reached their homes. The chief minister also criticised misleading information circulating on social media and urged students to assess political claims critically.

She advised young people to examine whether roads were being constructed, streets were being cleaned, and public services were improving before forming opinions about government performance, further adding that the provincial government had undertaken development projects worth trillions of rupees and claimed that these initiatives were improving the lives of people across Punjab.

She maintained that development work was no longer restricted to major cities and that smaller districts were receiving facilities previously concentrated in larger urban centres. The chief minister said she had visited Sahiwal, Mandi Bahauddin and Attock before arriving in Jhelum and had witnessed development work in these cities.

She claimed that her administration had broken the longstanding practice of concentrating public resources and development projects in major cities. She also criticised the tenure of former Punjab chief minister Usman Buzdar, questioning why students had not received scholarships, laptops and other educational facilities during his administration. The chief minister said the provincial government was providing facilities that should have been made available to citizens in previous years.

Responds to corruption allegations

Responding to allegations of corruption, the chief minister said her government had launched development projects worth trillions of rupees during its tenure. She maintained that she had not misappropriated public funds and was accountable to the people and God for the use of public resources.

CM Maryam said she would not spare any minister found involved in bribery or corruption if credible evidence was presented against them. She acknowledged that corruption had not been completely eliminated from Punjab but claimed that her administration was actively pursuing corruption cases and taking action against those responsible.

The chief minister also referred to alleged corruption in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa and questioned the performance of previous provincial administrations. She said the governments of other provinces should answer to their own people, while she remained responsible for the use of public funds in Punjab.

CM Maryam pledged that every rupee collected through taxes would be spent on public welfare, development and improving citizens' lives. She also questioned why individuals who criticised the government continued to hold ministerial positions instead of resigning.

Punjab to distribute 100,000 scooties to students

Turning to education and student welfare, CM Maryam announced that the Punjab government would distribute 100,000 scooties to students, with the first phase expected to begin in December. She said the programme had initially been scheduled for inauguration on November 5 but had been delayed because of the large number of scooties being manufactured.

The chief minister advised students who had applied for scooties to undergo proper driving training and wear helmets to ensure their safety. She congratulated students receiving Honhaar Scholarships and laptops, saying their achievements reflected their hard work and the sacrifices made by their parents.

CM Maryam said the scholarships, laptops and other facilities were not personal favours from the government but the students' rights, earned through merit and dedication. She pledged to establish a system in which educational and employment opportunities would be determined by merit rather than political influence, recommendations or the influence of wealthy individuals.

The chief minister said students from underprivileged families would not be deprived of employment opportunities after completing their education because of influential individuals. She encouraged students to participate in public service, politics and national development.

CM Maryam also praised Rana Sikandar for his efforts in the education sector and said the provincial government was responsible for approximately 50,000 schools across Punjab.

The chief minister said the provincial government was establishing nearly 300 Nawaz Sharif Schools of Eminence (NSSE) across Punjab. She said these institutions would provide air-conditioned classrooms, computer laboratories, artificial intelligence laboratories, science laboratories and qualified teaching staff, further adding that the facilities available at these institutions were comparable to, or better than, those provided by expensive private schools.

She said the government intended to extend similar educational facilities to children attending public schools throughout the province. The chief minister also referred to plans concerning an NSSE in Jhelum on December 15. She claimed that students who previously attended private schools were increasingly moving towards government institutions because of improvements in educational facilities.

CM Maryam said the provincial government was committed to ensuring that students received opportunities based on their abilities and academic performance.

Green bus services expanded to smaller cities

Highlighting transport initiatives, CM Maryam said green bus services operating in Lahore were also being provided in Rawalpindi, Jhelum, Khushab, Layyah, Bhakkar, Rahim Yar Khan, Bahawalpur and Multan. She said similar bus facilities and infrastructure were being developed in other districts, including Kasur, Rajanpur, Mandi Bahauddin and Pakpattan.

The chief minister said students were being allowed to travel free of charge on green buses to schools, colleges and universities. She stated that the government had been advised to introduce a nominal fare but had decided to continue providing free transport to students.

CM Maryam said the initiative was intended to provide students with comfortable transport and improve access to education. She maintained that smaller cities were receiving facilities similar to those available in Lahore and other major urban centres.

Discussing healthcare initiatives, the chief minister said she had visited the District Headquarters Hospital in Jhelum and inaugurated a catheterisation laboratory established in recent months. She said patients were receiving cardiac procedures, including angiograms, angioplasty, stenting and pacemaker implantation, free of charge.

CM Maryam said catheterisation laboratories and cardiac centres were being established in 25 smaller cities where such facilities had previously been unavailable. She added that cancer hospitals were being established at divisional headquarters, while a government cancer hospital was also being developed in Lahore.

The chief minister recounted meeting a patient who had travelled from Faisalabad to Jhelum for cardiac treatment after facing a longer waiting period in his home city. She said the patient had undergone a procedure the day after arriving in Jhelum.

Maryam described the case as an example of improved healthcare access in smaller cities, saying patients were now travelling from larger cities to smaller districts for treatment.

Housing scheme benefits low-income families

The chief minister also highlighted the provincial government's Apni Chhat, Apna Ghar housing programme, saying approximately 250,000 to 275,000 homes were being constructed for low-income families. She said she had visited a family in Jhelum that had previously lived in rented accommodation for 25 to 30 years.

According to her, the family had previously paid Rs15,000 in monthly rent and was now paying Rs14,000 a month towards its own home. She said hundreds of similar cases existed in Jhelum, where families who previously lacked the resources to own homes were now constructing houses.

The chief minister maintained that public money belonged to citizens and should be spent on their education, housing, transport, healthcare and development. CM Punjab referred to an assault on a female shop worker. She also referred to an incident involving a female employee at a garment shop, saying she had seen a video in which the woman was allegedly assaulted by a man. She said she had sought information from the police about the incident, which she believed had occurred in Faisalabad.

The chief minister said she had summoned the woman to a police station and instructed her to slap the man accused of assaulting her. She maintained that the provincial government stood with vulnerable and underprivileged people and would not allow influential individuals to mistreat them.

CM Maryam said the dignity of every citizen was equal and that wealth or political influence should not allow anyone to mistreat others.

Development projects in Jhelum

Referring to development work in Jhelum, the chief minister said she was scheduled to inaugurate a newly developed market and visit Pind Dadan Khan. She also mentioned the Lilla-Jhelum Road, saying the project had been completed during the current year.

CM Maryam said the provincial government was working to improve infrastructure and public facilities in smaller cities. She maintained that development projects, improved healthcare, educational facilities, transport services, and housing initiatives were intended to raise living standards throughout Punjab.

article_html:
Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz on Tuesday said political narratives, allegations and slogans could not replace public service, stressing that voters ultimately judged political parties on their performance and the development work carried out for their welfare.

Addressing a Honhaar Scholarship and laptop distribution ceremony at Government Comprehensive High School in Jhelum, Maryam said political parties could not sustain public support through rhetoric alone if they failed to deliver services to the people.

She said political narratives had a limited lifespan and that parties which failed to serve the public eventually lost their relevance.

The chief minister referred to two elections held in Sahiwal and Gujranwala, saying that the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) had secured victories in both despite opposition parties joining forces against it.

She said opposition parties had formed alliances and made efforts to defeat the PML-N but had failed to secure public support.

CM Maryam maintained that the results demonstrated that voters preferred development and public service over political slogans and allegations, adding that the PML-N had repeatedly received public support over the past four decades because people associated the party with development and the resolution of their problems.

The chief minister criticised political opponents for their reliance on political narratives rather than practical measures to address public concerns. She said popularity could be measured through electoral results and public confidence rather than claims made by political parties.

Referring to the opposition's electoral performance, CM Maryam claimed that political opponents had lost elections both while in government and after moving into opposition. She said people voted for political parties when development projects and public services reached their homes. The chief minister also criticised misleading information circulating on social media and urged students to assess political claims critically.

She advised young people to examine whether roads were being constructed, streets were being cleaned, and public services were improving before forming opinions about government performance, further adding that the provincial government had undertaken development projects worth trillions of rupees and claimed that these initiatives were improving the lives of people across Punjab.

She maintained that development work was no longer restricted to major cities and that smaller districts were receiving facilities previously concentrated in larger urban centres. The chief minister said she had visited Sahiwal, Mandi Bahauddin and Attock before arriving in Jhelum and had witnessed development work in these cities.

She claimed that her administration had broken the longstanding practice of concentrating public resources and development projects in major cities. She also criticised the tenure of former Punjab chief minister Usman Buzdar, questioning why students had not received scholarships, laptops and other educational facilities during his administration. The chief minister said the provincial government was providing facilities that should have been made available to citizens in previous years.

Responds to corruption allegations

Responding to allegations of corruption, the chief minister said her government had launched development projects worth trillions of rupees during its tenure. She maintained that she had not misappropriated public funds and was accountable to the people and God for the use of public resources.

CM Maryam said she would not spare any minister found involved in bribery or corruption if credible evidence was presented against them. She acknowledged that corruption had not been completely eliminated from Punjab but claimed that her administration was actively pursuing corruption cases and taking action against those responsible.

The chief minister also referred to alleged corruption in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa and questioned the performance of previous provincial administrations. She said the governments of other provinces should answer to their own people, while she remained responsible for the use of public funds in Punjab.

CM Maryam pledged that every rupee collected through taxes would be spent on public welfare, development and improving citizens' lives. She also questioned why individuals who criticised the government continued to hold ministerial positions instead of resigning.

Punjab to distribute 100,000 scooties to students

Turning to education and student welfare, CM Maryam announced that the Punjab government would distribute 100,000 scooties to students, with the first phase expected to begin in December. She said the programme had initially been scheduled for inauguration on November 5 but had been delayed because of the large number of scooties being manufactured.

The chief minister advised students who had applied for scooties to undergo proper driving training and wear helmets to ensure their safety. She congratulated students receiving Honhaar Scholarships and laptops, saying their achievements reflected their hard work and the sacrifices made by their parents.

CM Maryam said the scholarships, laptops and other facilities were not personal favours from the government but the students' rights, earned through merit and dedication. She pledged to establish a system in which educational and employment opportunities would be determined by merit rather than political influence, recommendations or the influence of wealthy individuals.

The chief minister said students from underprivileged families would not be deprived of employment opportunities after completing their education because of influential individuals. She encouraged students to participate in public service, politics and national development.

CM Maryam also praised Rana Sikandar for his efforts in the education sector and said the provincial government was responsible for approximately 50,000 schools across Punjab.

The chief minister said the provincial government was establishing nearly 300 Nawaz Sharif Schools of Eminence (NSSE) across Punjab. She said these institutions would provide air-conditioned classrooms, computer laboratories, artificial intelligence laboratories, science laboratories and qualified teaching staff, further adding that the facilities available at these institutions were comparable to, or better than, those provided by expensive private schools.

She said the government intended to extend similar educational facilities to children attending public schools throughout the province. The chief minister also referred to plans concerning an NSSE in Jhelum on December 15. She claimed that students who previously attended private schools were increasingly moving towards government institutions because of improvements in educational facilities.

CM Maryam said the provincial government was committed to ensuring that students received opportunities based on their abilities and academic performance.

Green bus services expanded to smaller cities

Highlighting transport initiatives, CM Maryam said green bus services operating in Lahore were also being provided in Rawalpindi, Jhelum, Khushab, Layyah, Bhakkar, Rahim Yar Khan, Bahawalpur and Multan. She said similar bus facilities and infrastructure were being developed in other districts, including Kasur, Rajanpur, Mandi Bahauddin and Pakpattan.

The chief minister said students were being allowed to travel free of charge on green buses to schools, colleges and universities. She stated that the government had been advised to introduce a nominal fare but had decided to continue providing free transport to students.

CM Maryam said the initiative was intended to provide students with comfortable transport and improve access to education. She maintained that smaller cities were receiving facilities similar to those available in Lahore and other major urban centres.

Discussing healthcare initiatives, the chief minister said she had visited the District Headquarters Hospital in Jhelum and inaugurated a catheterisation laboratory established in recent months. She said patients were receiving cardiac procedures, including angiograms, angioplasty, stenting and pacemaker implantation, free of charge.

CM Maryam said catheterisation laboratories and cardiac centres were being established in 25 smaller cities where such facilities had previously been unavailable. She added that cancer hospitals were being established at divisional headquarters, while a government cancer hospital was also being developed in Lahore.

The chief minister recounted meeting a patient who had travelled from Faisalabad to Jhelum for cardiac treatment after facing a longer waiting period in his home city. She said the patient had undergone a procedure the day after arriving in Jhelum.

Maryam described the case as an example of improved healthcare access in smaller cities, saying patients were now travelling from larger cities to smaller districts for treatment.

Housing scheme benefits low-income families

The chief minister also highlighted the provincial government's Apni Chhat, Apna Ghar housing programme, saying approximately 250,000 to 275,000 homes were being constructed for low-income families. She said she had visited a family in Jhelum that had previously lived in rented accommodation for 25 to 30 years.

According to her, the family had previously paid Rs15,000 in monthly rent and was now paying Rs14,000 a month towards its own home. She said hundreds of similar cases existed in Jhelum, where families who previously lacked the resources to own homes were now constructing houses.

The chief minister maintained that public money belonged to citizens and should be spent on their education, housing, transport, healthcare and development. CM Punjab referred to an assault on a female shop worker. She also referred to an incident involving a female employee at a garment shop, saying she had seen a video in which the woman was allegedly assaulted by a man. She said she had sought information from the police about the incident, which she believed had occurred in Faisalabad.

The chief minister said she had summoned the woman to a police station and instructed her to slap the man accused of assaulting her. She maintained that the provincial government stood with vulnerable and underprivileged people and would not allow influential individuals to mistreat them.

CM Maryam said the dignity of every citizen was equal and that wealth or political influence should not allow anyone to mistreat others.

Development projects in Jhelum

Referring to development work in Jhelum, the chief minister said she was scheduled to inaugurate a newly developed market and visit Pind Dadan Khan. She also mentioned the Lilla-Jhelum Road, saying the project had been completed during the current year.

CM Maryam said the provincial government was working to improve infrastructure and public facilities in smaller cities. She maintained that development projects, improved healthcare, educational facilities, transport services, and housing initiatives were intended to raise living standards throughout Punjab.

Responding to allegations of corruption, the chief minister said her government had launched development projects worth trillions of rupees during its tenure. She maintained that she had not misappropriated public funds and was accountable to the people and God for the use of public resources.

CM Maryam said she would not spare any minister found involved in bribery or corruption if credible evidence was presented against them. She acknowledged that corruption had not been completely eliminated from Punjab but claimed that her administration was actively pursuing corruption cases and taking action against those responsible.

The chief minister also referred to alleged corruption in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa and questioned the performance of previous provincial administrations. She said the governments of other provinces should answer to their own people, while she remained responsible for the use of public funds in Punjab.

CM Maryam pledged that every rupee collected through taxes would be spent on public welfare, development and improving citizens' lives. She also questioned why individuals who criticised the government continued to hold ministerial positions instead of resigning.
Punjab to distribute 100,000 scooties to students

Turning to education and student welfare, CM Maryam announced that the Punjab government would distribute 100,000 scooties to students, with the first phase expected to begin in December. She said the programme had initially been scheduled for inauguration on November 5 but had been delayed because of the large number of scooties being manufactured.

The chief minister advised students who had applied for scooties to undergo proper driving training and wear helmets to ensure their safety. She congratulated students receiving Honhaar Scholarships and laptops, saying their achievements reflected their hard work and the sacrifices made by their parents.

CM Maryam said the scholarships, laptops and other facilities were not personal favours from the government but the students' rights, earned through merit and dedication. She pledged to establish a system in which educational and employment opportunities would be determined by merit rather than political influence, recommendations or the influence of wealthy individuals.

The chief minister said students from underprivileged families would not be deprived of employment opportunities after completing their education because of influential individuals. She encouraged students to participate in public service, politics and national development.
CM Maryam also praised Rana Sikandar for his efforts in the education sector and said the provincial government was responsible for approximately 50,000 schools across Punjab.

The chief minister said the provincial government was establishing nearly 300 Nawaz Sharif Schools of Eminence (NSSE) across Punjab. She said these institutions would provide air-conditioned classrooms, computer laboratories, artificial intelligence laboratories, science laboratories and qualified teaching staff, further adding that the facilities available at these institutions were comparable to, or better than, those provided by expensive private schools.

She said the government intended to extend similar educational facilities to children attending public schools throughout the province. The chief minister also referred to plans concerning an NSSE in Jhelum on December 15. She claimed that students who previously attended private schools were increasingly moving towards government institutions because of improvements in educational facilities.
CM Maryam said the provincial government was committed to ensuring that students received opportunities based on their abilities and academic performance.
Green bus services expanded to smaller cities

Highlighting transport initiatives, CM Maryam said green bus services operating in Lahore were also being provided in Rawalpindi, Jhelum, Khushab, Layyah, Bhakkar, Rahim Yar Khan, Bahawalpur and Multan. She said similar bus facilities and infrastructure were being developed in other districts, including Kasur, Rajanpur, Mandi Bahauddin and Pakpattan.

The chief minister said students were being allowed to travel free of charge on green buses to schools, colleges and universities. She stated that the government had been advised to introduce a nominal fare but had decided to continue providing free transport to students.

CM Maryam said the initiative was intended to provide students with comfortable transport and improve access to education. She maintained that smaller cities were receiving facilities similar to those available in Lahore and other major urban centres.

Discussing healthcare initiatives, the chief minister said she had visited the District Headquarters Hospital in Jhelum and inaugurated a catheterisation laboratory established in recent months. She said patients were receiving cardiac procedures, including angiograms, angioplasty, stenting and pacemaker implantation, free of charge.

CM Maryam said catheterisation laboratories and cardiac centres were being established in 25 smaller cities where such facilities had previously been unavailable. She added that cancer hospitals were being established at divisional headquarters, while a government cancer hospital was also being developed in Lahore.

The chief minister recounted meeting a patient who had travelled from Faisalabad to Jhelum for cardiac treatment after facing a longer waiting period in his home city. She said the patient had undergone a procedure the day after arriving in Jhelum.
Maryam described the case as an example of improved healthcare access in smaller cities, saying patients were now travelling from larger cities to smaller districts for treatment.
Housing scheme benefits low-income families

The chief minister also highlighted the provincial government's Apni Chhat, Apna Ghar housing programme, saying approximately 250,000 to 275,000 homes were being constructed for low-income families. She said she had visited a family in Jhelum that had previously lived in rented accommodation for 25 to 30 years.

According to her, the family had previously paid Rs15,000 in monthly rent and was now paying Rs14,000 a month towards its own home. She said hundreds of similar cases existed in Jhelum, where families who previously lacked the resources to own homes were now constructing houses.

The chief minister maintained that public money belonged to citizens and should be spent on their education, housing, transport, healthcare and development. CM Punjab referred to an assault on a female shop worker. She also referred to an incident involving a female employee at a garment shop, saying she had seen a video in which the woman was allegedly assaulted by a man. She said she had sought information from the police about the incident, which she believed had occurred in Faisalabad.

The chief minister said she had summoned the woman to a police station and instructed her to slap the man accused of assaulting her. She maintained that the provincial government stood with vulnerable and underprivileged people and would not allow influential individuals to mistreat them.
CM Maryam said the dignity of every citizen was equal and that wealth or political influence should not allow anyone to mistreat others.
Development projects in Jhelum

Referring to development work in Jhelum, the chief minister said she was scheduled to inaugurate a newly developed market and visit Pind Dadan Khan. She also mentioned the Lilla-Jhelum Road, saying the project had been completed during the current year.

CM Maryam said the provincial government was working to improve infrastructure and public facilities in smaller cities. She maintained that development projects, improved healthcare, educational facilities, transport services, and housing initiatives were intended to raise living standards throughout Punjab.

headline: Vanishing vessels and missing sailors: The Iran war's human cost at sea
description: UN confirms 130 'incidents', mainly attacks, in region since US-Iran conflict began, with at least 25 seafarers killed
author: Reuters
article_text:
V Pandiselvi, the mother of Indian sailor Naveen Kumar, has not heard from her son for more than six months yet she still clings to hope he will return, crying as she replays old voice notes.

Kumar was one of six crew members assigned to work on two Iran-linked cargo vessels last seen in Iranian waters in May before disappearing. The vessels' fate is still unclear.

Commercial ships have come under fire since the United States-Israeli war on Iran began on February 28. Tehran attacked ships to assert control over the Strait of Hormuz and the US in turn struck Iran-linked ships to impose a blockade on Iranian ports.

The United Nations' International Maritime Organisation has confirmed 130 "incidents" – mainly attacks – in the region since the conflict began, with at least 25 seafarers killed.

"We cannot bear this pain," Pandiselvi, 45, told Reuters from her one-bedroom house in the city of Dindigul in southern India's Tamil Nadu state, struggling to keep her composure. "You don't need anyone to tell you what a parent would go through if they were to lose their child. We appeal to everyone involved to please come forward and help us."

Reuters spoke to shipping sources, Iraqi officials and the families of missing sailors in Iraq's Basra and India's Tamil Nadu state to reveal the human cost of Hormuz attacks.

The 23-year-old Kumar's family took on considerable debt for him to complete a marine course and pursue his dream of working as a sailor, after which he left for a six-month crew contract he was told was based in Dubai. A week in, he found himself in Iran, to the consternation of his family.

'Every minute is agony'

Even before war broke out three months later, Kumar's family was desperately trying to repatriate him. Then came radio silence.

"My mental condition had deteriorated into madness, I sent desperate messages," Pandiselvi said, adding she was sending him voice notes without any replies to a number she had saved as "Naveen Mariner" with an anchor emoji.

The family keeps the line active in hope their son picks up. A neighbour described her as listening to messages over and over, in tears.

"A terrifying question mark hangs over his fate: Is he still on that ship, or has something terrible happened to him? It's causing a lot of confusion. Every passing minute is agony," Pandiselvi said.

Kumar had been deployed to the vessels Bridge 1 and Bridge 2, which disappeared around May 9. The two ships were not on the IMO's list of incidents.

Iraq said in May it was monitoring the disappearance of the two vessels, which flew the Bolivian flag. No distress signals were received. Gulf ports requested information after communications with the crew were lost.

Khaled Saad al-Thaalibi, who heads the Iraqi maritime foundation in Basra, told Reuters the latest available information indicated the vessels' Automatic Identification System (AIS) transmitted their last known position approximately 8 nautical miles from Iran's Kish Island on May 9 at 4:50pm.

"We called the agent in Iran but he told us that he knew nothing about the incident and on the following day the Iranian search and rescue tried to look for the vessels but they found nothing," Thaalibi told Reuters from his office in Basra. "We don't know if the vessels sunk or were confiscated by a country."

The other Bridge 1 and 2 crew members missing are three Iraqis, one Pakistani and another Indian. Sources familiar with the matter said the vessels were involved in Iranian trade and carrying steel.

No answers

Haider Rahman al-Mayahi, a 22-year-old Iraqi sailor, was on the crew, his brother Youssef Rahman said. "He left behind a one-year-old daughter and a father who suffered a stroke from the grief of his disappearance," he told Reuters, breaking down in tears.

Al-Mayahi's family travelled to Iran seeking answers. They located the vessels' owner, whom they identified only as an Iranian who told them he had no information on the vessels.

The family received conflicting theories about the vessels. Some shipping sources said they may have been struck by the US and sunk immediately while others speculated the crew had been detained by a Gulf state or Iran.

The Iranian agent who hired the Iraqi sailors did not respond to phone calls from Reuters.

Kumar's family took out around 1.5 million Indian rupees ($16,000) in loans for him to complete his maritime training course and is now struggling with the financial burden.

They contacted the local agency that hired Kumar, Mumbai-based firm Lascar Marine, initially receiving assurances he would return soon. People from the agency later told the family they had no information. After that, calls went unanswered, the family said.

The agency did not reply to repeated calls from Reuters.

An order dated May 22, published on a government website, showed India's Seamen's Employment Office withdrew the recruitment license of Lascar Marine Services and barred its past and present directors from maritime business for five years, citing repeated failures to repatriate seafarers — including Kumar — or pay their wages.

The director of Seamen's Employment Office did not respond to a Reuters request for comment.

Crew working aboard ships are usually contracted by agents like Lascar Marine and hired on six-month contracts. Since the Iran war, costs of hiring sailors have tripled with many working just one journey as risks mount.

One Dubai-based shipper told Reuters a crew member may make what they used to make in seven months in only two and then opt to go home. A captain, the highest paid crew member on a vessel, could make around $8,000 to $13,000 a month before the conflict. Now they can earn three times that. "They ask for three months' pay per month but after seeing what a journey entails they sometimes quit after one trip," the shipper said.

For Pandiselvi, Kumar's mother, the allure of good pay is now meaningless. "We worked tirelessly to secure our children's careers and future," she said. "Now, seeing everything that has happened, we are left wondering what our lives have come to."

The director of Seamen's Employment Office did not respond to a Reuters request for comment.

Crew working aboard ships are usually contracted by agents like Lascar Marine and hired on six-month contracts. Since the Iran war, costs of hiring sailors have tripled with many working just one journey as risks mount.

One Dubai-based shipper told Reuters a crew member may make what they used to make in seven months in only two and then opt to go home. A captain, the highest paid crew member on a vessel, could make around $8,000 to $13,000 a month before the conflict. Now they can earn three times that. "They ask for three months' pay per month but after seeing what a journey entails they sometimes quit after one trip," the shipper said.

For Pandiselvi, Kumar's mother, the allure of good pay is now meaningless. "We worked tirelessly to secure our children's careers and future," she said. "Now, seeing everything that has happened, we are left wondering what our lives have come to."

headline: BHC overturns ex-MPA Achakzai's acquittal, hands him 10 years in traffic officer's death case
description: Court also orders him to pay blood money to the legal heirs of the deceased
author: Sardar Hameed Khan
article_text:
The Balochistan High Court on Tuesday accepted the provincial government's appeal against the acquittal of Pashtunkhwa Milli Awami Party (PMAP) leader, former provincial lawmaker and Public Accounts Committee chairman Abdul Majeed Achakzai, sentencing him to 10 years of rigorous imprisonment in the case involving the death of traffic sub-inspector Haji Ataullah.

The court also ordered him to pay blood money to the legal heirs of the deceased.

According to the Balochistan High Court, a division bench comprising Justice Muhammad Aamir Nawaz Rana and Justice Abdul Qayyum Lehri heard the government's appeal against Achakzai's acquittal. The court accepted the appeal and set aside the acquittal verdict announced on September 4, 2020, by the Additional Sessions Judge-VI and Model Criminal Trial Court-II, Quetta.

The high court convicted Achakzai under Section 320 of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC) for causing the death of traffic sub-inspector Haji Ataullah, who was on duty, by running him over while driving recklessly and negligently at high speed.

The court sentenced Achakzai to 10 years of rigorous imprisonment and ordered him to pay blood money to the deceased's legal heirs.

The high court directed the Additional Sessions Judge-VI, Quetta, to issue non-bailable arrest warrants for Achakzai, who is currently out on bail, for his immediate arrest and the implementation of the sentence.

The court also directed the relevant authorities to ensure prompt execution of the arrest warrants in accordance with the law so that Achakzai could be transferred to prison to serve his sentence.

The case

The incident took place on June 20, 2017, at GPO Chowk on Zarghoon Road in Quetta, where a speeding official Land Cruiser belonging to Achakzai hit traffic sergeant Haji Ataullah Dashti, who was on duty. Dashti sustained serious injuries and later died, while a cyclist, Abdul Ghafoor Baloch, was also injured.

Achakzai allegedly ran over the traffic sergeant after the latter signalled him to stop. The incident, initially treated as a traffic accident, came under scrutiny after CCTV footage emerged showing the vehicle hitting the officer following an exchange of words between the two. The footage went viral on social media and prompted protests by the Balochistan press. There were also reports that Achakzai was driving recklessly and was intoxicated at the time.

Police initially registered a case against unidentified persons. Following the emergence of the footage, they registered a case against Achakzai on charges of terrorism, murder, and attempted murder. He was arrested from his residence in Quetta's Satellite Town area on June 25, 2017.

Civil Lines police subsequently submitted a challan before the Anti-Terrorism Court, but the terrorism charge was later withdrawn after police failed to establish it.

Achakzai, who was elected to the Balochistan Assembly from PB-13 Qila Abdullah in the 2013 general elections, admitted that he had been driving his official vehicle when the incident occurred. He said he would compensate the deceased traffic sergeant's family and the injured passerby. He also intended to travel to Dera Ghazi Khan with tribal elders to meet Dashti's family.

The case was later transferred to the Model Criminal Trial Court in Quetta, where it remained under trial for around three years.

On September 4, 2020, the Model Criminal Trial Court acquitted Achakzai, ruling that the prosecution had failed to establish that he was driving the vehicle when the incident occurred.

In its 29-page written judgment, Judge Dost Muhammad Mandokhail noted that none of the 20 prosecution witnesses, including eyewitnesses and the deceased's brother, had identified Achakzai as the driver of the vehicle.

The judgment said the police had initially registered the FIR against unidentified persons but did not conduct an identification parade after nominating Achakzai as an accused.

The court observed that the CCTV footage did not establish who was driving the vehicle. It also noted contradictions and omissions in prosecution witnesses' statements and said the case had not been proved beyond reasonable doubt.

Achakzai had denied the allegations in his statement recorded under Section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, claiming that his driver had been behind the wheel and that he was not in the vehicle.

The trial court consequently acquitted him of the charges under sections 302, 324, 279, 337 and 427 of the PPC. The provincial government later challenged the acquittal before the Balochistan High Court.

Achakzai, who was elected to the Balochistan Assembly from PB-13 Qila Abdullah in the 2013 general elections, admitted that he had been driving his official vehicle when the incident occurred. He said he would compensate the deceased traffic sergeant's family and the injured passerby. He also intended to travel to Dera Ghazi Khan with tribal elders to meet Dashti's family.
The case was later transferred to the Model Criminal Trial Court in Quetta, where it remained under trial for around three years.
On September 4, 2020, the Model Criminal Trial Court acquitted Achakzai, ruling that the prosecution had failed to establish that he was driving the vehicle when the incident occurred.

In its 29-page written judgment, Judge Dost Muhammad Mandokhail noted that none of the 20 prosecution witnesses, including eyewitnesses and the deceased's brother, had identified Achakzai as the driver of the vehicle.
The judgment said the police had initially registered the FIR against unidentified persons but did not conduct an identification parade after nominating Achakzai as an accused.

The court observed that the CCTV footage did not establish who was driving the vehicle. It also noted contradictions and omissions in prosecution witnesses' statements and said the case had not been proved beyond reasonable doubt.

Achakzai had denied the allegations in his statement recorded under Section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, claiming that his driver had been behind the wheel and that he was not in the vehicle.

The trial court consequently acquitted him of the charges under sections 302, 324, 279, 337 and 427 of the PPC. The provincial government later challenged the acquittal before the Balochistan High Court.

headline: Pakistan-Sri Lanka second test may shift to Rawalpindi
description: Rising smog in Lahore raises concerns over match scheduled to begin on November 17
author: Mohammad Yousuf Anjum
article_text:
Rising smog in Lahore raises concerns over match scheduled to begin on November 17

Pakistan's second test against Sri Lanka, scheduled to begin in Lahore on November 17, could be moved to Rawalpindi because of worsening smog. According to sources the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) officials are concerned about deteriorating air quality in Lahore and have discussed the possibility of shifting the match. Sources said that the consultations remain at an early stage. If the proposal is approved, Rawalpindi would host both tests of the series, with the opening match currently under way at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium. Sri Lanka are in Pakistan for the last one month, having already played three-match T20I series and ODI tri-series. Pakistan defeated them 2-1 in the T20I series and Pakistan also downed them in the ODI tri-series final at Lahore to win the vital event also including England who failed to deliver. The ODI tri-series initial three matches had been held in Pindi before Lahore hosted the remaining four encounters including the final.

headline: Bangladesh prosecutor says ex-PM Hasina will be executed if she returns
description: Prosecutor says Hasina missed deadline to appeal conviction, leaving her with no further legal recourse
author: AFP
article_text:
The Bangladeshi prosecutor who secured the death sentence against ousted leader Sheikh Hasina said on Tuesday she will be executed if she returns home.

Hasina, whose 15-year rule was ended by a mass uprising she tried to crush, has vowed to return in December to Bangladesh, where she was sentenced to death for crimes against humanity over the 2024 crackdown on protesters.

"Sheikh Hasina has no option but to face the execution of the verdict," Md Aminul Islam told reporters, responding to reports she planned to return from self-imposed exile in India.

He added that she missed the deadline to appeal her conviction, leaving her with no further legal recourse. "The statute says that an appeal must be filed within 30 days of the delivery of the judgement," he said.

Hasina, 79, fled to neighbouring India by helicopter in August 2024 as angry crowds stormed her palace. She has remained there ever since, hidden from public view. Only occasionally has she addressed news conferences by telephone, her voice sounding frail.

Hasina has repeatedly said she intends to return to Bangladesh in December, telling AFP she is "fully aware" she faces being hanged if she returns. She said "fear cannot decide" her "duty to the people".

Critics have accused Hasina of jailing political rivals, enacting harsh anti-press laws and overseeing widespread human rights abuses, including the killing of opposition activists.

Her 2024 crackdown left up to 1,400 people dead, according to the United Nations.

Hasina defied orders from the court to return to Bangladesh to attend her trial last year on whether she bore command responsibility for the bloody crackdown on the student-led uprising. Witnesses included a man whose face was ripped apart by a gunshot. Hasina, who was assigned a state-appointed lawyer, called the trial a "jurisprudential joke".

In November 2025, a court in Dhaka sentenced her to death in absentia after finding her guilty on three counts of crimes against humanity, including incitement, ordering killings and failing to prevent atrocities.

Bangladesh's foreign ministry has sought her extradition from India, which says the request is under legal review. Her continued presence there has strained relations between the neighbouring countries.

She also faces a string of other cases, including corruption charges.

headline: Israel's parliament sworn in as president urges lawmakers to avoid repeat elections
description: Newly elected lawmakers took office as former general Eisenkot began efforts to form a coalition
author: AFP
article_text:
Israel's parliament was sworn in on Tuesday without a new ​government, after a deadlocked general election stripped Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of his parliamentary majority but left his main rivals with no clear path ‌to power.

Lawmakers elected in the October 27 vote took their oaths of office as Gadi Eisenkot, a former general, sought to forge a coalition after Israel's president tasked him on Sunday with forming a government.

Eisenkot and his allies also lack a majority and he has yet to strike deals with parties that could bring him to power. If both Eisenkot and Netanyahu fail to form coalitions, another ​election could follow.

Presiding over the swearing-in ceremony, President Isaac Herzog told lawmakers: "You must do everything to avoid a repeat election."

Reach out a hand for compromise, ​even between rivals ... Look upon one another with generosity. There is much work to be done here, and it requires the ability ⁠and experience found in every part of this House."

Parliament could try to set up October 7 inquiry

Netanyahu remains caretaker prime minister until a new candidate manages to ​form a coalition. His right-wing Likud party's alliance with far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties outperformed election expectations but still lost its majority, now holding 53 of the Knesset's 120 seats.

Eisenkot's ​centre-right Yashar party and patchwork partner factions hold just 48 seats. But they have potential allies in Israel's Arab-led parties, which hold 19 seats and are aligned with Eisenkot in their vehement opposition to Netanyahu.

This means that the newly sworn-in parliament could still deliver on some of Eisenkot's campaign promises, such as potentially setting up a commission of inquiry into the October 7, 2023 Hamas ​attacks, something backed by the Arab parties but largely opposed by Netanyahu.

It also could allow Eisenkot to replace the current Knesset speaker, a Likud member.

Herzog told Knesset members ​that parliament was "duty bound to leave no stone unturned" in investigating and understanding the "catastrophe" of October 7, while Israel continues to face threats from Iran and its proxies.

Eisenkot initially has until December ‌6 to ⁠form a government but he can seek a two-week extension to December 20. He has acknowledged his path to power is "extraordinarily complex".

His options include trying to form a minority government with Arab party support, bringing ultra-Orthodox parties into his camp despite years of mutual hostility, or forging a unity government with Netanyahu. All three paths face formidable obstacles.

Ultra-Orthodox parties have so far said they would not join an Eisenkot-led government.

For his part, Netanyahu has cast doubt on the election results by baselessly alleging voter fraud by Arabs, who ​make up a fifth of the population. ​Election officials have said they are ⁠probing potential misconduct, but that they have seen no evidence of fraud that could have influenced the vote's outcome.

Speaking after parliament was sworn in, Netanyahu called for a unity government, warning that Iran was seeking to revive its nuclear programme and that Israel ​could come under growing international pressure to accept a nuclear-armed Iran.

"Only such a [unity] government will be capable of confronting challenges ​of this magnitude," he ⁠said.

If Eisenkot fails to form a government, Herzog would likely ask Netanyahu to try to build a coalition. If he also fails, another candidate would get a chance before Israel would be forced into another election.

Moments after the official opening of parliament, Eisenkot and his allies submitted a series of bills, including legislation to establish a state commission of inquiry into ⁠the October ​7 attacks and to impose term limits on the prime minister. They also proposed repealing a controversial ​judicial overhaul and other laws enacted under Netanyahu's government over the past four years.

Among those sworn in on Tuesday was Elisha Madan, a military reservist who lost both legs fighting in Gaza. He received a ​standing ovation from lawmakers as he rose on his prosthetic legs to take the oath of office.

headline: Journalist Rabia Ahsan's husband sent for polygraph test
description: Court grants four-day physical remand of accused, directs police to complete investigation & produce suspect on Nov 13
author: Imran Asghar
article_text:
A Rawalpindi court on Tuesday granted four-day physical remand of Ahsan Tahir, husband of slain anchorperson and journalist Rabia Ahsan, as police prepared to conduct his polygraph test in Lahore to verify his account of the fatal shooting.

Rabia, a 41-year-old anchorperson associated with 92 News, was found shot dead at her home in Rawalpindi on Sunday. Her husband was taken into custody in connection with the incident, which prompted an outpouring of grief from colleagues and members of the journalist community. The court on Monday had granted police a one-day physical remand of the suspect.

Senior Civil Judge Muhammad Nasrullah Wattoo handed over the suspect to Saddar Beruni police for further investigation and directed them to produce him before the court again on November 13, along with a detailed investigation report and the post-mortem report.

During the hearing, police told the court that the suspect's statement had been recorded under Section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC), in which he acknowledged that the shooting had occurred but maintained that it was accidental rather than intentional.

According to police sources, Ahsan told investigators that he and Rabia had been taking winter clothes for themselves and their children out of a cupboard at their Gulshanabad home on Adiala Road on Sunday when a pistol fell out of the clothes and discharged accidentally.

He reportedly expressed deep remorse over the incident and maintained that there had been no premeditation or conspiracy to kill his wife. He also claimed that his daughters were present at home and could corroborate his account. The suspect also voluntarily handed over the pistol to police.

During Tuesday's hearing, police sought a seven-day physical remand, telling the court that the suspect's polygraph test would be conducted at a forensic laboratory in Lahore. Investigators also sought to establish through forensic examination whether the bullet had been fired from the pistol recovered from the suspect.

The court granted a four-day remand instead. Police said the polygraph examination would help assess the suspect's account and that its findings would be included in the investigation report.

A polygraph test records physiological responses, including changes in heart rate, blood pressure, breathing and sweating. However, it cannot independently establish whether a statement is true or false.

Meanwhile, preliminary post-mortem findings confirmed that Rabia had sustained a single gunshot wound below the neck, with the bullet exiting through her back. No signs of physical violence were found on her body.

Samples collected during the post-mortem examination have been sent to a forensic laboratory in Lahore. The pistol and bullet casing have also been forwarded for forensic analysis to determine whether the recovered weapon was used in the shooting.

Khurram Ahmed has also dismissed reports that the family intends to withdraw the murder case, maintaining that no such decision has been taken.

Police sources further said that a 15-year-old domestic worker, who had been hired around two weeks before the incident, had been sent back to his home.

The case was registered at the police station on the complaint of Rabia's brother, Khurram Ahmed, who accused Ahsan of shooting his sister at their home in Gulshanabad Sector II, on Adiala Road, on Sunday.

According to the FIR, Rabia's mother and sister were in the lawn at around 2:30pm when they heard a gunshot from the bedroom. Her sister rushed inside and found Rabia lying on the floor in a pool of blood, while Ahsan was holding a pistol.

The FIR stated that Ahsan told police he had fired at his wife with the same weapon. Police said he had failed to produce a licence or permit for the pistol. The case was registered under Section 302 of the Pakistan Penal Code and Section 13(2)(a) of the Punjab Arms Amendment Ordinance.

Rabia had presented her last programme on a mainstream television channel on Saturday night. Police sources said her mother and sisters had also been at the house when the incident occurred.

The suspect was a grade-18 officer at the Overseas Pakistanis Foundation, according to police sources. Rabia was survived by two daughters and also ran a private salon in Islamabad.

A team from the Punjab Forensic Science Agency collected evidence from the crime scene. Her body was shifted to a hospital for a post-mortem examination.
