The court on Monday had granted police a one-day physical remand of the suspect.

Senior Civil Judge Muhammad Nasrullah Wattoo handed over the suspect to Saddar Beruni police for further investigation and directed them to produce him before the court again on November 13, along with a detailed investigation report and the post-mortem report.

During the hearing, police told the court that the suspect's statement had been recorded under Section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC), in which he acknowledged that the shooting had occurred but maintained that it was accidental rather than intentional.

According to police sources, Ahsan told investigators that he and Rabia had been taking winter clothes for themselves and their children out of a cupboard at their Gulshanabad home on Adiala Road on Sunday when a pistol fell out of the clothes and discharged accidentally.

He reportedly expressed deep remorse over the incident and maintained that there had been no premeditation or conspiracy to kill his wife. He also claimed that his daughters were present at home and could corroborate his account. The suspect also voluntarily handed over the pistol to police.

During Tuesday's hearing, police sought a seven-day physical remand, telling the court that the suspect's polygraph test would be conducted at a forensic laboratory in Lahore. Investigators also sought to establish through forensic examination whether the bullet had been fired from the pistol recovered from the suspect.
The court granted a four-day remand instead. Police said the polygraph examination would help assess the suspect's account and that its findings would be included in the investigation report.

A polygraph test records physiological responses, including changes in heart rate, blood pressure, breathing and sweating. However, it cannot independently establish whether a statement is true or false.

Meanwhile, preliminary post-mortem findings confirmed that Rabia had sustained a single gunshot wound below the neck, with the bullet exiting through her back. No signs of physical violence were found on her body.

Samples collected during the post-mortem examination have been sent to a forensic laboratory in Lahore. The pistol and bullet casing have also been forwarded for forensic analysis to determine whether the recovered weapon was used in the shooting.
Khurram Ahmed has also dismissed reports that the family intends to withdraw the murder case, maintaining that no such decision has been taken.
Police sources further said that a 15-year-old domestic worker, who had been hired around two weeks before the incident, had been sent back to his home.

The case was registered at the police station on the complaint of Rabia's brother, Khurram Ahmed, who accused Ahsan of shooting his sister at their home in Gulshanabad Sector II, on Adiala Road, on Sunday.

According to the FIR, Rabia's mother and sister were in the lawn at around 2:30pm when they heard a gunshot from the bedroom. Her sister rushed inside and found Rabia lying on the floor in a pool of blood, while Ahsan was holding a pistol.

The FIR stated that Ahsan told police he had fired at his wife with the same weapon. Police said he had failed to produce a licence or permit for the pistol. The case was registered under Section 302 of the Pakistan Penal Code and Section 13(2)(a) of the Punjab Arms Amendment Ordinance.
Rabia had presented her last programme on a mainstream television channel on Saturday night. Police sources said her mother and sisters had also been at the house when the incident occurred.
The suspect was a grade-18 officer at the Overseas Pakistanis Foundation, according to police sources. Rabia was survived by two daughters and also ran a private salon in Islamabad.
A team from the Punjab Forensic Science Agency collected evidence from the crime scene. Her body was shifted to a hospital for a post-mortem examination.

headline: James Gunn breaks silence on four-year run at DC Studios
description: The filmmaker says he is eager to return to making films without studio responsibilities
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
James Gunn has opened up about the personal and professional challenges of leading DC Studios, describing his four-year tenure as a rewarding but demanding experience.

The filmmaker addressed his departure in a lengthy statement after Skydance replaced him and Peter Safran with Jeremy Latcham as president and chief creative officer of DC Studios on Monday. The decision brought an end to Gunn and Safran's four-year leadership of the studio.

View this post on Instagram

During their tenure, the pair oversaw a reboot of the DC superhero universe, with projects including Superman, Supergirl, Clayface and the HBO series Lanterns.

Although Gunn celebrated several achievements, he admitted that the responsibilities of running a major studio had taken a personal toll.

"What only the closest people to me have known over the past four years is my time at DC Studios has been trying, to say the least," he wrote, explaining that he disliked the corporate aspects of the position.

He also revealed that the demanding schedule had left him with little time to unwind or spend with loved ones. Gunn said balancing projects he felt passionate about with the administrative responsibilities of being a studio head had been particularly difficult.

However, his statement was not entirely focused on the struggles. He described working with the DC Studios team, collaborators, cast members and fans as among the greatest highlights of his time in the role.

He also praised Safran, calling him the smartest and most competent person he knew and thanking him for being an exceptional professional partner and friend.

Despite stepping away from leadership, Gunn confirmed that his association with DC was not necessarily over. He revealed that he and Safran had been involved in another DC project that he was writing, although its future remained uncertain.

Gunn also expressed excitement about returning to filmmaking, describing Man of Tomorrow as the best filmmaking experience of his life so far.

In his closing remarks, he thanked audiences for embracing the characters and stories they had brought to the screen, signing off with a message of love and gratitude.

The filmmaker's departure marks a significant change for DC Studios, although projects developed during his leadership are expected to continue.

headline: 63 students hospitalised after fire at religious school in Bangladesh
description: Four children in critical condition as authorities suspect electrical short circuit as reason for blaze
author: Anadolu Agency
article_text:
Four children in critical condition as authorities suspect electrical short circuit as reason for blaze

At least 63 students were hospitalised after a fire broke out at an Islamic religious school in Bangladesh's central Narayanganj district early Tuesday, a fire official told Anadolu.

The blaze erupted on the second floor of a five-story building in Narayanganj, about 16 kilometres (10 miles) southeast of the capital Dhaka, said Abdullah Al Arefin, deputy assistant director of the Narayanganj Fire Service and Civil Defence.

Four firefighting units were dispatched and brought the blaze under control, he said, adding that most students escaped without burns, although several suffered from smoke inhalation.

The fire originated in the library and office rooms of Jamiatul Ashrafia Madrasa, which has about 1,300 students, most of them boarders.

All 63 affected students were taken to the National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery in Dhaka. Four were admitted to the intensive care unit in critical condition, including one placed on life support, resident surgeon Sultan Mahmud Sikdar told local newspaper The Daily Star.

The doctor said none of the students had suffered burns, but all were experiencing respiratory problems believed to have been caused by smoke inhalation.

A preliminary assessment by the Fire Service indicated that an electrical short circuit may have sparked the blaze.

headline: Paul McCartney reaches historic financial milestone joining elite billionaire club
description: His publishing business, Beatles royalties and worldwide tours have helped build his fortune
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Paul McCartney has reached billionaire status, with an estimated net worth of $1.4 billion, placing him among the wealthiest musicians in the world.

According to Forbes, the former Beatles member ranks as the world's third-richest musician, behind Jay-Z, whose estimated fortune stands at $2.8 billion, and Taylor Swift, with $2 billion.

The financial publication attributed McCartney's wealth to several income streams, including music publishing, songwriting royalties, touring, business interests and his extensive art collection.

A significant part of his fortune comes from MPL Communications, the publishing company he established in 1969. The business manages his own musical catalogue alongside copyrights belonging to other artists. Its holdings also include works by Buddy Holly, Broadway musical scores and Christmas standards.

McCartney also benefits from the continuing commercial success of the Beatles. Through Apple Corps, the band's holding company, he receives a share of earnings generated by streaming, vinyl sales and merchandise. It is estimated that the company generates approximately $50 million annually.

His songwriting catalogue provides another substantial source of income. The musician reportedly earns around $10 million annually from his share of Beatles songwriting copyrights, which he spent years fighting to reclaim.

Touring has also contributed considerably to his wealth. His GOT BACK tour included 79 performances between 2022 and 2025, adding to decades of earnings from live performances.

Despite his extraordinary financial success, McCartney remains active in music. He released his 20th solo album, The Boys of Dungeon Lane, in May 2026.

He is also the subject of Man on the Run, a documentary directed by Morgan Neville that explores his life after the Beatles and the formation of Wings.

His latest financial milestone reflects a career spanning decades, with music publishing and the enduring popularity of his work continuing to generate substantial returns.

According to Forbes, the former Beatles member ranks as the world's third-richest musician, behind Jay-Z, whose estimated fortune stands at $2.8 billion, and Taylor Swift, with $2 billion.
The financial publication attributed McCartney's wealth to several income streams, including music publishing, songwriting royalties, touring, business interests and his extensive art collection.

A significant part of his fortune comes from MPL Communications, the publishing company he established in 1969. The business manages his own musical catalogue alongside copyrights belonging to other artists. Its holdings also include works by Buddy Holly, Broadway musical scores and Christmas standards.

McCartney also benefits from the continuing commercial success of the Beatles. Through Apple Corps, the band's holding company, he receives a share of earnings generated by streaming, vinyl sales and merchandise. It is estimated that the company generates approximately $50 million annually.

His songwriting catalogue provides another substantial source of income. The musician reportedly earns around $10 million annually from his share of Beatles songwriting copyrights, which he spent years fighting to reclaim.
Touring has also contributed considerably to his wealth. His GOT BACK tour included 79 performances between 2022 and 2025, adding to decades of earnings from live performances.

headline: Bilawal calls for ‘system reset’ through unity
description: Says political parties need to work together rather than fight one another
author: Muhammad Saleem Jhandeer
article_text:
Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari on Tuesday again advised the PML-N-led federal government to adopt reconciliation rather than engaging in confrontation with the opposition, emphasising the need for the government to also take its coalition partners into confidence on key issues.

Bilawal, whose party supports the ruling coalition without becoming part of the government at the Centre, expressed these views on Tuesday while addressing a function organized at the completion of one million housing units for people affected by the 2021 floods in Sindh.

According to the PPP chief, people do not expect their governments to divide the nation and pit people against each other. “People expect their government to work to make their lives easier,” he said.

The federal government has been at odds not only with the opposition, including Imran Khan’s PTI—whose Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) government was suspended after the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in K-P last month—but also with Maulana Fazlur Rehman’s JUI-F.

After Fazl’s scathing criticism of the federal government and the powers that be following the K-P emergency, a number of federal ministers attacked the JUI-F chief as government authorities started issuing notices to Fazl-linked businesses and people for alleged rule violations.

Speaking at the groundbreaking ceremony of a hospital in Larkana earlier on November 7, Bilawal urged the federal government and political parties to set aside their differences and engage all political, social and provincial stakeholders to tackle the economic crisis.

The PPP chief then warned that the fallout from the Iran war was placing an unprecedented burden on ordinary Pakistanis, saying that the economic consequences of the conflict were being felt across the world, from America to Larkana.

He described the situation as a major test for governments, stressing that public welfare must take precedence over political confrontation. He urged the federal government to engage stakeholders rather than continue fighting political opponents.

"If we remain engaged in fighting one another, with Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf [PTI], with Maulana [Fazlur Rehman], with terrorists, with India and Afghanistan, then we will not be able to alleviate the suffering of the Pakistani people," Bilawal said.

The PPP chief maintained that political differences must take a back seat to efforts to address public hardships, adding that governments would be judged by their ability to support citizens through the economic difficulties.

In his Tuesday address, Bilawal also obliquely hit out at both Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi and the PML-N, saying that there was indeed a need to “reset” the system, but by allowing the country to be run by people “instead of traders and businessmen” and through unity.

Mohsin Naqvi on July 31 claimed that the country’s systems needed a “reset” through the creation of new provinces. The Sindh Assembly, where the PPP is in the majority, later passed a resolution against any possible division of Sindh.

Naqvi and some other ministers, however, have continually advocated for the creation of new administrative units with an alleged proposal to divide Sindh into two provinces.

Bilawal reiterated that Pakistan, along with the rest of the world, was facing an economic crisis and that the country’s politics did indeed need to be reset to deal with it.

“[However, for this reset] all political parties should work together instead of fighting one another. The people no longer wanted to hear calls for confrontation and do not want the country’s system turned upside down at the wishes of business groups in Islamabad or Lahore.”

He urged the prime minister to take his coalition partners into confidence first and engage with the opposition through dialogue rather than opening new fronts of confrontation. “Public relief would remain impossible unless the government and opposition worked together,” he added.

Bilawal rejects corruption allegations in Sindh housing project

The PPP chairman rejected corruption allegations in the Sindh People's Housing Scheme and accused political opponents of running a smear campaign against the provincial government, while calling for an international audit of the project to address the allegations.

Bilawal said Sindh had repeatedly faced criticism, while political opponents had attempted to create an impression of widespread corruption in the province. He said political opponents had accused the PPP of raising funds for the housing project to misappropriate money.

He urged Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah to write to international organisations and invite them to audit the project. “I can confidently say that no corruption has taken place in this project,” he said.

He urged political opponents to stop criticising and maligning the Sindh government and instead learn from its efforts to serve underprivileged communities. Bilawal said 50 per cent of educational institutions had been destroyed in 2023.

One million homes completed for flood victims

Highlighting the Sindh People's Housing Scheme, Bilawal described it as the world's largest housing project and said the provincial government had completed one million homes for flood-affected families. He said the PPP had launched the historic initiative at a time when the world was facing an economic crisis.

The PPP chairman said the programme aimed to construct two million homes, while he also referred to a target of five million houses for flood-affected families. Bilawal said the Sindh government had undertaken the project with the support of international partners.

He stated that the provincial government had not only constructed permanent houses for flood victims but had also provided them with ownership rights to the land. He said the ownership of houses had been registered in women's names, giving affected families greater security.

The PPP chairman maintained that families who previously had no homes had been provided permanent housing. He said the government's responsibility was to provide citizens with healthcare and medical treatment facilities while taking measures to reduce the financial burden on ordinary people.

Recalling the floods, Bilawal said he had been in Larkana when the heavy rains began and had never witnessed a natural disaster of such magnitude. He said he had travelled by helicopter with the prime minister and that the floodwaters had made the landscape appear like a sea.

The PPP chairman recalled promising women affected by the disaster that he would help build homes for them. He said that promise had now resulted in the completion of one million houses.

Bilawal said the federal government at the time had told international financial institutions that provincial governments were corrupt and that funds should therefore be provided to the Centre. He claimed that those making such statements did not even visit Sindh.

The PPP chairman said the World Bank had expressed confidence in the Sindh government and released funds for the housing project. He recalled that, while serving as foreign minister, he had also raised funds for Balochistan.

Bilawal said the federal government had taken responsibility for reconstruction in Balochistan, but only 30,000 houses had been built there over three years. He contrasted that figure with the one million homes he said had been completed in Sindh.

The PPP chairman rejected corruption allegations in the Sindh People's Housing Scheme and accused political opponents of running a smear campaign against the provincial government, while calling for an international audit of the project to address the allegations.

Bilawal said Sindh had repeatedly faced criticism, while political opponents had attempted to create an impression of widespread corruption in the province. He said political opponents had accused the PPP of raising funds for the housing project to misappropriate money.

He urged Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah to write to international organisations and invite them to audit the project. “I can confidently say that no corruption has taken place in this project,” he said.

He urged political opponents to stop criticising and maligning the Sindh government and instead learn from its efforts to serve underprivileged communities. Bilawal said 50 per cent of educational institutions had been destroyed in 2023.

Highlighting the Sindh People's Housing Scheme, Bilawal described it as the world's largest housing project and said the provincial government had completed one million homes for flood-affected families. He said the PPP had launched the historic initiative at a time when the world was facing an economic crisis.

The PPP chairman said the programme aimed to construct two million homes, while he also referred to a target of five million houses for flood-affected families. Bilawal said the Sindh government had undertaken the project with the support of international partners.

He stated that the provincial government had not only constructed permanent houses for flood victims but had also provided them with ownership rights to the land. He said the ownership of houses had been registered in women's names, giving affected families greater security.

The PPP chairman maintained that families who previously had no homes had been provided permanent housing. He said the government's responsibility was to provide citizens with healthcare and medical treatment facilities while taking measures to reduce the financial burden on ordinary people.

Recalling the floods, Bilawal said he had been in Larkana when the heavy rains began and had never witnessed a natural disaster of such magnitude. He said he had travelled by helicopter with the prime minister and that the floodwaters had made the landscape appear like a sea.

The PPP chairman recalled promising women affected by the disaster that he would help build homes for them. He said that promise had now resulted in the completion of one million houses.

Bilawal said the federal government at the time had told international financial institutions that provincial governments were corrupt and that funds should therefore be provided to the Centre. He claimed that those making such statements did not even visit Sindh.

The PPP chairman said the World Bank had expressed confidence in the Sindh government and released funds for the housing project. He recalled that, while serving as foreign minister, he had also raised funds for Balochistan.

Bilawal said the federal government had taken responsibility for reconstruction in Balochistan, but only 30,000 houses had been built there over three years. He contrasted that figure with the one million homes he said had been completed in Sindh.

headline: Dax Shepard speaks out against rumours portraying him as an abusive husband
description: Dax Shepard says public criticism has taken a personal toll on his family
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Dax Shepard has spoken out against rumours portraying him as an abusive husband, saying the claims have been particularly painful for both him and his wife, Kristen Bell.

The actor addressed the controversy during Monday's episode of his Armchair Expert podcast, explaining that the speculation intensified after Bell's recent comments about his unusual approach to flirting.

Shepard described the accusations as deeply insulting and rejected suggestions that he was controlling or abusive towards his family.

He also explained why the allegations affected him so strongly, revealing that he grew up around abusive men and had dedicated much of his life to becoming the opposite.

"I literally dedicated my whole life to being the opposite of all that," he said, adding that he did not yell at his children or use swear words towards them.

Shepard shares two daughters, Lincoln, 13, and Delta, 11, with Bell. He also insisted that he did not yell at his wife, describing the allegations as particularly offensive because they suggested Bell was raising their children in an abusive household.

The actor also addressed the comments that initially triggered the online discussion. During her October 26 appearance on the podcast, Bell explained that Shepard sometimes compliments restaurant staff during their dinners together.

Shepard clarified that his compliments were not directed towards young female waitresses, as some interpretations suggested. Instead, he said he often complimented men whose appearance or clothing caught his attention, hoping to make their day.

He explained that this behaviour was his way of flirting with Bell, rather than attempting to attract other people.

The couple have previously faced criticism over their candid discussions about marriage and parenting. In October 2025, Bell received backlash for an anniversary post joking about Shepard promising never to kill her.

The latest controversy has prompted Shepard to question whether public criticism will continue to define his reputation, despite his efforts to explain his intentions.

headline: Andrew Garfield appears to question Sam Altman’s public image after past admiration
description: The actor also reveals he never actually met Altman despite filming scenes outside his home
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Andrew Garfield has offered a revealing account of how his perception of Sam Altman evolved, recalling a time when he considered the OpenAI chief executive an inspiring figure before expressing uncertainty about his public image.

Speaking during a question-and-answer session at the Academy Museum in Los Angeles on Monday, the actor discussed his preparation for Artificial, Luca Guadagnino’s upcoming film about the founding of OpenAI and the controversy surrounding Altman’s departure and subsequent return.

Garfield recalled first becoming interested in Altman after watching him testify before Congress. He was particularly impressed by the technology executive’s comments about transparency, artificial intelligence risks and his stated commitment to helping humanity.

The actor also admired Altman’s apparent willingness to defend his position in a challenging political environment.

Garfield said he had initially viewed him as someone whose values and priorities were in the right place. He even joked that Altman could become his future best friend.

However, his comments suggested that his earlier admiration had become considerably more complicated.

"He convinced me that he was nothing but purely altruistic, which, I mean, it’s all playing out. I’m not gonna comment on those things," Garfield said, adding that people could form their own opinions about what was happening.

The actor also expressed concern about the future of artificial intelligence, warning that society needed artists and influential people to participate in conversations about regulation and protecting human autonomy.

Meanwhile, Garfield addressed an unusual detail involving Altman’s account of the film’s production. The technology executive had previously suggested that the pair exchanged waves while the production filmed outside his San Francisco home.

Garfield disputed the story, insisting that he never saw Altman in person and had no interaction with him during filming.

He said the production had been told Altman was not home that day, leaving open the possibility that the executive had mistaken someone else for him.

headline: Steven Tyler faces renewed legal battle as court prepares for 2027 proceedings
description: A new judge will review earlier court decisions after his predecessor withdrew from the case
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Steven Tyler is scheduled to face trial in May 2027 over allegations made by a woman who claims the Aerosmith frontman sexually abused her when she was a minor during the 1970s.

The trial date was confirmed as May 3, 2027, by Judge Lawrence Riff during a hearing in Los Angeles on November 9. He has taken over the proceedings after the previous judge, Patricia Young, disqualified herself from the case.

The change in judges follows an unexpected development in September, when Young withdrew after discovering that a fellow judge involved in discussions about the matter had previously been dismissed from the trial. She disclosed the issue to both legal teams before stepping aside.

Riff has agreed to reconsider decisions made by Young from the beginning of her assignment if either legal team requests a review. According to Rolling Stone, the new judge wants both sides to have confidence that the proceedings have been conducted properly.

The lawsuit was filed by Julie Misley, who first brought her allegations against Tyler in 2022. She claims their relationship began in 1973, when she was 16 and the musician was 25, and continued for approximately three years.

Misley has also alleged that Tyler pressured her into having an abortion when she was 17. Her lawsuit describes the relationship as one in which she was allegedly persuaded to believe that the situation was a romantic affair.

In April, Young dismissed several claims because of statute of limitations issues involving Massachusetts, Oregon and Washington. However, one claim relating to California was allowed to proceed.

Tyler has denied wrongdoing, while his legal representatives have previously argued that the relationship was consensual and that Massachusetts law applied because the pair primarily lived in Boston.

With the trial approaching, further pretrial hearings are expected as both sides prepare for the proceedings.

article_html:
Steven Tyler is scheduled to face trial in May 2027 over allegations made by a woman who claims the Aerosmith frontman sexually abused her when she was a minor during the 1970s.

The trial date was confirmed as May 3, 2027, by Judge Lawrence Riff during a hearing in Los Angeles on November 9. He has taken over the proceedings after the previous judge, Patricia Young, disqualified herself from the case.

The change in judges follows an unexpected development in September, when Young withdrew after discovering that a fellow judge involved in discussions about the matter had previously been dismissed from the trial. She disclosed the issue to both legal teams before stepping aside.

Riff has agreed to reconsider decisions made by Young from the beginning of her assignment if either legal team requests a review. According to Rolling Stone, the new judge wants both sides to have confidence that the proceedings have been conducted properly.

The lawsuit was filed by Julie Misley, who first brought her allegations against Tyler in 2022. She claims their relationship began in 1973, when she was 16 and the musician was 25, and continued for approximately three years.

Misley has also alleged that Tyler pressured her into having an abortion when she was 17. Her lawsuit describes the relationship as one in which she was allegedly persuaded to believe that the situation was a romantic affair.

In April, Young dismissed several claims because of statute of limitations issues involving Massachusetts, Oregon and Washington. However, one claim relating to California was allowed to proceed.

Tyler has denied wrongdoing, while his legal representatives have previously argued that the relationship was consensual and that Massachusetts law applied because the pair primarily lived in Boston.

With the trial approaching, further pretrial hearings are expected as both sides prepare for the proceedings.

headline: Amanda Seyfried reveals unexpected involvement in Elizabeth Holmes documentary
description: The actress says taking creative risks has become an important part of her career
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Amanda Seyfried has opened up about taking on an unusual acting assignment that brought her back to one of the most recognisable roles of her career.

The actress secretly participated in You Can See Everything, a documentary about disgraced Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes, directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim. Now that her involvement has been revealed, Seyfried says she feels both relieved and excited.

Speaking exclusively to PEOPLE at the New York premiere of Netflix’s Steps on November 8, the actress discussed her decision to reprise her portrayal of Holmes for the documentary.

Seyfried previously played the former technology executive in Hulu’s The Dropout, earning an Emmy and a Golden Globe for her performance.

Her latest appearance involved recreating conversations and encounters that Fielder and his team had been unable to capture during their documentary filming. The project follows Holmes in the weeks leading up to her imprisonment for fraud.

Seyfried explained that accepting unfamiliar assignments was important to her development as an actor and artist.

She said she wanted to pursue projects that challenged her and pushed her outside her comfort zone. She also described the satisfaction of taking a creative risk and discovering that the finished work could have a positive impact.

The documentary features an unusual combination of real footage and staged reenactments. One particularly revealing moment involves Holmes watching Seyfried portray her in The Dropout.

After Holmes entered prison, the filmmakers invited Seyfried to view much of the footage they had collected, eventually bringing her into the project.

The actress’s involvement had been kept out of the promotional material and trailers released before the documentary’s theatrical debut on October 16.

Meanwhile, Seyfried continues to explore different projects. She also voices Cinderella in Netflix’s upcoming film Steps, scheduled to arrive on November 20.

Her return to Holmes’ story demonstrates her continued interest in complex characters and unconventional storytelling.

headline: Pakistan demolish Nepal in Asia Cup
description: In semi-finals on Thursday Green-shirts face Bangladesh, India lock horns with Afghanistan
author: Sports Desk
article_text:
Pakistan maintained their unbeaten run in the ACC Men’s Under-19 Asia Cup with a huge 101-run victory over Nepal in their final Group A match on Tuesday at the Al Amerat Cricket Ground in Oman.

The defending champions posted 275-7 in their allotted 50 overs before bowling Nepal out for 174 in 43.4 overs to register a comprehensive win. Pakistan had already secured their place in the semi-finals.

Ahmed Hussain starred with both bat and ball, scoring a brilliant 89 before claiming four wickets for 35 runs. Mohammad Sayyam and Mohammad Huzaifa picked up two wickets apiece to complete the victory.

Chasing 276, Nepal struggled to establish partnerships. Rohit Chand top-scored 37 off 54 balls, while opener Niraj Kumar Yadav contributed 29 from 59 deliveries. Suryanshu Koirala added 22, but Nepal failed to keep pace with the required run rate.

Abhay Yadav offered some late resistance with a quick-fire 23 off 16 balls, including three fours and a six, but the target remained beyond Nepal's reach.

Earlier, Pakistan recovered from early setback through a match-defining 135-run partnership between captain Farhan Yousaf and Ahmed Hussain.

After openers Usman Khan (19) and Jahangir Bilal (22) provided a 45-run start, Nepal fought back through Bipin Sharma and Sachin Bhatt, reducing Pakistan to 57-2. Bipin then dismissed Abdul Qadir for six, leaving the defending champions under pressure.

Farhan and Ahmed steadied the innings before accelerating to put Pakistan in control. Farhan scored 74 off 95 balls, hitting six fours and three sixes, while Ahmed produced an impressive 89 off 73 deliveries, including seven fours and two sixes.

Hasnain Abbas Dar added a useful 25 off 23 balls, helping Pakistan push their total to 275-7. Bipin was Nepal's leading bowler with three wickets for 58 runs.

With an unbeaten group-stage record and a semi-final place secured, Pakistan will now focus on defending their continental title.

Meanwhile in the same group India Under-19 secured a convincing 70-run victory over the United Arab Emirates to qualify for the last four.

Batting first, India posted 309-7, powered by Aaryavir Sehwag’s brilliant 160 off 168 balls and VK Vineeth’s 67. In reply, UAE managed 239 in 50 overs, with Ahmed Khudadad scoring 74. Ishan Sood starred with four wickets for India.

Semi-finals (Nov12)

Pakistan v Bangladesh, India v Afghanistan

headline: Fact check: Viral video does not show a man kicking and damaging Tarbela Dam; it’s old and unrelated
description: Viral video falsely claims man damaged Tarbela Dam; footage is from Kohistan in August 2026
author: Fact Check By iVerify
article_text:
Several people were sharing a clip on social media platforms X and Facebook since November 9, 2026, allegedly showing the crumbling state of Tarbela Dam with a man kicking and damaging its structure. However, the video is from August 2026 and was filmed in Kohistan.

A rock mass collapsed at the Tarbela Dam 5th Extension Project (T-5) construction site on November 9, 2026, causing water to surge into nearby work areas.

An emergency was declared following the collapse; construction work was suspended and workers were directed to move to safer areas. However, no loss of life was reported in the incident.

How it starting

On Nov 9, an Afghan propaganda account, based on its past posts, shared a video on X, allegedly showing a man standing at the edge of the Tarbela Dam’s wall and kicking it, highlighting the poor condition.

The caption of the post read, “Pakistan Army Corruption | Tarbela Dam T-5. The protective structure of the dam breaks with a kick, resulting in today’s incident. T-4 Project. Former WAPDA Chairman (R) Lt Gen Muzammil Hussain faced an NAB case over a financial loss of $753.7 million approximately PKR 100 billion. Corruption runs deep among Pakistan’s top generals.”

The video gained 186,797 views.

The same video was reposted a few hours later by TV anchor and media personality Moeed Pirzada with the following caption, “Wow! This young man kicked open the back door of a Wapda vehicle—now he must be arrested and punished!”

His post garnered a total of 91,369 views.

Similarly, other accounts also shared the same video in a similar context on X and Facebook, here, here, and here.

Methodology

A fact-check was initiated to verify the viral claim due to its high virality and keen public interest surrounding the safety and structural integrity of the Tarbela Dam.

A keyword search was conducted to verify whether any credible media outlets in Pakistan had recently reported on a viral video of a man kicking the walls of the Tarbela Dam and breaking them easily, but it yielded no results.

A reverse image search was conducted to trace the source of the viral video, which yielded the same visual shared by Pakistan Connect, a digital news outlet, dated August 3, 2026.

The caption of the clip read: “The KP government claims widespread development across the province, but the situation on the ground tells a different story. A video from Kohistan exposes the current condition of a road and its safety walls, raising serious concerns about the quality of construction.”

A further keyword search yeilded the same video shared on Facebook on August 20, 2026, by Nazar Buneri, a former provincial social media member of the Awami National Party.

The video’s caption read: “The standard of development work carried out by the Tabdeeli government in Kohistan district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.”

As per the description, the clip is from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Kohistan district.

Fact-check status: False

The claim that a viral video shows a man kicking and damaging Tarbela Dam is false.

The video is from August 2026 and was filmed in Kohistan.

This fact check was originally published by iVerify Pakistan— a project of CEJ-IBA and UNDP.

headline: Wapda chairman orders inquiry into Tarbela project incident
description: Wapda chairman Lt Gen Muhammad Saeed orders a departmental inquiry to probe the incident holistically
author: APP
article_text:
Water and Power Development Authority (WAPDA) Chairman Lt Gen (retd) Muhammad Saeed on Tuesday ordered a departmental inquiry into an incident inside the tunnel of the Tarbela Fifth Extension Hydropower Project and directed the immediate implementation of rehabilitation measures to minimise potential delays in the project's completion.

The breach on Monday had prompted the indefinite suspension of construction work on Tarbela Dam and also caused an increased flow of water in the River Indus, with authorities issuing an alert for the areas adjoining the river.

The chairman visited the project a day ago and today to review the situation following the incident. WAPDA Member (Water) Engineer Asim Rauf Khan, other senior WAPDA officials, contractors and consultants were also present.

During the visit, the chairman inspected the under-construction project's intake structure, tunnel, powerhouse and other key construction sites. The consultants, contractor and WAPDA's project management team briefed him on the prevailing situation and the measures taken so far.

Later, he chaired a meeting at the project office to review the possible causes of the incident and short-, medium- and long-term measures to address the situation.

The meeting finalised immediate measures, implementation of which has already begun. The consultants, contractor and WAPDA team also agreed that neither the main Tarbela Dam nor any other major structure faced any threat.

The WAPDA chairman directed the consultants to submit a comprehensive report on all aspects of the incident at the earliest. He also instructed the consultants, contractor and WAPDA's project team to immediately implement rehabilitation measures and finalise an emergency response plan to minimise any potential delays in the overall completion of the project.

The Ministry of Water Resources has also sought an initial assessment report from WAPDA, which was submitted today. Federal Minister for Water Resources Mian Muhammad Moeen Wattoo is also reviewing the incident. The WAPDA chairman personally briefed him on the details.

With an installed generation capacity of 1,530 megawatts, the Tarbela Fifth Extension Hydropower Project is being constructed on Tunnel No. 5 of the Tarbela Dam. The World Bank and the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank are providing financial assistance for the project.

WAPDA had awarded a $354.6 million contract for the project's civil works to China's Power Construction Corporation of China Limited in May 2021. The project had an approved cost of $807 million, with the World Bank providing $390 million and the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank contributing $300 million.

Once completed, it is expected to generate an average of 1.347 billion units of electricity annually and increase Tarbela Dam's installed capacity from 4,888MW to 6,418MW.

The project, however, has faced repeated delays, pushing its completion deadline back from the original five-year schedule to September 2027. In September 2024, a project director told a Senate committee that delays had been caused, among other factors, by difficulties in obtaining an NOC from the Indus River System Authority for the closure of Tunnel 5.

The project had also faced a temporary suspension in August 2025 after rising reservoir levels and increased water inflows led to water entering the construction site.

headline: Keira Knightley admits her iconic Christmas film has almost faded from her memory
description: Actress was only 17 when she filmed her part in the 2003 Christmas hit
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Keira Knightley has revealed that her connection to Love Actually is rather different from that of the millions of fans who revisit the Christmas film every year. Despite starring in the 2003 romantic comedy, the actress has not watched it since its premiere.

Speaking to Heart, Knightley explained that she was 18 when the film premiered and has little recollection of the experience. As a result, fans who approach her with familiar lines from the film often leave her unable to respond in the way they might expect.

“I have not watched Love Actually since the premiere, which was when I was 18,” she said. “So, I think I am the person that knows it the least of anybody.”

Knightley added that she recognises when people are quoting the film because of their expressions, but does not necessarily understand the references. “It means nothing to me,” she admitted.

The actress also explained that her limited time on set contributed to her lack of memories. She was 17 during filming and worked on the production for only a week.

“I do not remember it really,” she said, while acknowledging that she likes seeing the film continue to have such a significant life with audiences.

Knightley played Juliet, a newly married woman whose husband’s best friend, Mark, secretly loves her. The character is at the centre of one of the film’s most recognisable moments, when Mark, played by Andrew Lincoln, declares his feelings through a series of cue cards at her door.

However, Knightley has previously expressed reservations about the scene. In a 2024 interview with the Los Angeles Times, she described its romantic gesture as “quite creepy” and recalled questioning the way it was presented while filming.

She also pointed out that she was only 17 at the time, a detail she felt audiences had not fully appreciated when discussing the scene

headline: Who is Alice Huang, the Chinese businesswoman tied to Nvidia's CEO?
description: Known as Huang Le, the Chinese businesswoman led a Shanghai firm before controlling Singapore's Megaspeed
author: Reuters
article_text:
Alice Huang built a career in Chinese finance before emerging in a very different arena: the global race for artificial-intelligence chips.

Known also as Huang Le, the Chinese businesswoman held senior roles ​at a Shanghai investment firm before becoming the controlling shareholder of Singapore-based cloud-computing company Megaspeed International, according to more than 30 publicly available financial records, corporate filings and company materials reviewed by Reuters.

Nvidia ‌lists Megaspeed as an official cloud partner on its directory. Megaspeed attracted public attention in October 2025, when the New York Times reported the company was under US investigation over whether it was helping Chinese customers obtain advanced Nvidia chips subject to Washington's export controls.

Alice Huang has since been thrust into the spotlight because of her links with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. The two are not related.

The New York Times reported last month that US authorities had concluded she was a Chinese intelligence asset who passed information to Beijing while developing a close ​relationship with the Nvidia CEO.

Reuters could not independently verify the intelligence allegation, which China has denied. Reuters could not determine Alice Huang's whereabouts to seek comment.

Nvidia's board has launched an independent investigation into reports that its CEO ​was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation, but said it had no reason to believe national security information or company trade secrets had been compromised.

US President Donald Trump said on ⁠Monday that the FBI was also looking into the matter, but he did not provide further details.

Without commenting directly on Alice Huang, Jensen Huang acknowledged on Sunday being unfaithful to his wife, but said he was committed to supporting ​US national security.

From Shanghai finance to Nvidia chips

Alice Huang, reported by Chinese financial publication Caixin to be about 42 years old, previously worked in banking and investment management, according to Chinese fund-industry records and an indexed profile on private-fund database ​Simuwang, which also listed an earlier career in television journalism.

Before her involvement with Megaspeed, she held senior positions at Shanghai Hexi Investment Management, a Chinese investment firm.

Several posts on Hexi's official WeChat account between 2016 and 2017 identified her as the firm's deputy general manager, executive director and a member of its investment decision committee and said she had previously worked at HSBC's private bank in Hong Kong and at CITIC Securities. HSBC and CITIC did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

A Hexi business card reviewed by Reuters identified Alice Huang ​as a partner and general manager, with an office in Shanghai's Lujiazui financial district. At the Aurora Plaza address listed on the card, Reuters found offices undergoing extensive renovation, with no Hexi signage or staff present. Calls to a ​number on the card went unanswered, and an email address could not receive messages.

Huang became Megaspeed's controlling shareholder in March 2023, according to Washington-based research group C4ADS, which reviewed corporate records. Incorporated in Singapore in 2015 as 7Road International, Megaspeed provides cloud-computing services and ‌describes itself ⁠on its company website as an Nvidia business partner in the Asia-Pacific region.

Huang also served as a director and managing director of Megaspeed's Indonesian subsidiary from March to November 2023, C4ADS said. Megaspeed did not respond to a request for comment.

At a party hosted by Taiwanese server manufacturer Gigabyte during the 2024 Computex technology trade show, Alice Huang and Jensen Huang were both present, according to a person who attended. A photograph posted on LinkedIn showed them seated next to each other.

Gigabyte, which makes AI servers using Nvidia chips, did not respond to a request for comment.

Business ties under scrutiny

Megaspeed has drawn scrutiny from US authorities over suspicions that it helped Chinese companies obtain advanced Nvidia chips subject to Washington's export restrictions, ​but there has been no public finding that it violated ​the rules.

Shipping records from trade-data provider ImportGenius reviewed by ⁠Reuters show Megaspeed's Indonesian subsidiary imported Nvidia hardware between 2024 and 2026, including H100 processors and related components, in shipments from suppliers including Gigabyte subsidiary Giga Computing.

The H100 is among the advanced Nvidia processors restricted from export to China, although the shipments to Indonesia do not themselves establish any violation of US export controls.

Megaspeed's shares were transferred in late 2023 ​to Singapore-based SwiftData, which holds all 10 million of its ordinary shares, according to C4ADS. Reuters could not immediately contact SwiftData.

C4ADS said it could not determine who ultimately ​controls SwiftData, but assessed that Alice ⁠Huang may have continued to exercise influence over Megaspeed after the transfer, citing appearances in which she was identified as its chair.

Seeking answers

The reports of ties between Alice Huang and Jensen Huang have prompted US lawmakers to seek answers from the Nvidia CEO.

Central questions include whether he knew of any alleged intelligence activity and whether sensitive information was compromised, said George Chen, a partner at consultancy The Asia Group.

"In many respects, Jensen may also be viewed as a potential victim if he was deliberately ⁠targeted or manipulated ​without knowledge of the individual's true identity or intentions," Chen said.

The US chipmaker has said its CEO meets with thousands of customer executives ​each year, and that its cloud customers in Asia receive ordinary business information rather than trade secrets or information related to US national security.

Trump said on Monday he "was amazed" by allegations involving Jensen Huang, among the president's closest allies in Silicon Valley. Trump said he had spoken to the CEO, ​who told him that he had no idea that the woman was a spy.

article_html:
Alice Huang built a career in Chinese finance before emerging in a very different arena: the global race for artificial-intelligence chips.

Known also as Huang Le, the Chinese businesswoman held senior roles ​at a Shanghai investment firm before becoming the controlling shareholder of Singapore-based cloud-computing company Megaspeed International, according to more than 30 publicly available financial records, corporate filings and company materials reviewed by Reuters.

Nvidia ‌lists Megaspeed as an official cloud partner on its directory. Megaspeed attracted public attention in October 2025, when the New York Times reported the company was under US investigation over whether it was helping Chinese customers obtain advanced Nvidia chips subject to Washington's export controls.

Alice Huang has since been thrust into the spotlight because of her links with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. The two are not related.

The New York Times reported last month that US authorities had concluded she was a Chinese intelligence asset who passed information to Beijing while developing a close ​relationship with the Nvidia CEO.

Reuters could not independently verify the intelligence allegation, which China has denied. Reuters could not determine Alice Huang's whereabouts to seek comment.

Nvidia's board has launched an independent investigation into reports that its CEO ​was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation, but said it had no reason to believe national security information or company trade secrets had been compromised.

US President Donald Trump said on ⁠Monday that the FBI was also looking into the matter, but he did not provide further details.

Without commenting directly on Alice Huang, Jensen Huang acknowledged on Sunday being unfaithful to his wife, but said he was committed to supporting ​US national security.

From Shanghai finance to Nvidia chips

Alice Huang, reported by Chinese financial publication Caixin to be about 42 years old, previously worked in banking and investment management, according to Chinese fund-industry records and an indexed profile on private-fund database ​Simuwang, which also listed an earlier career in television journalism.

Before her involvement with Megaspeed, she held senior positions at Shanghai Hexi Investment Management, a Chinese investment firm.

Several posts on Hexi's official WeChat account between 2016 and 2017 identified her as the firm's deputy general manager, executive director and a member of its investment decision committee and said she had previously worked at HSBC's private bank in Hong Kong and at CITIC Securities. HSBC and CITIC did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

A Hexi business card reviewed by Reuters identified Alice Huang ​as a partner and general manager, with an office in Shanghai's Lujiazui financial district. At the Aurora Plaza address listed on the card, Reuters found offices undergoing extensive renovation, with no Hexi signage or staff present. Calls to a ​number on the card went unanswered, and an email address could not receive messages.

Huang became Megaspeed's controlling shareholder in March 2023, according to Washington-based research group C4ADS, which reviewed corporate records. Incorporated in Singapore in 2015 as 7Road International, Megaspeed provides cloud-computing services and ‌describes itself ⁠on its company website as an Nvidia business partner in the Asia-Pacific region.

Huang also served as a director and managing director of Megaspeed's Indonesian subsidiary from March to November 2023, C4ADS said. Megaspeed did not respond to a request for comment.

At a party hosted by Taiwanese server manufacturer Gigabyte during the 2024 Computex technology trade show, Alice Huang and Jensen Huang were both present, according to a person who attended. A photograph posted on LinkedIn showed them seated next to each other.

Gigabyte, which makes AI servers using Nvidia chips, did not respond to a request for comment.

Business ties under scrutiny

Megaspeed has drawn scrutiny from US authorities over suspicions that it helped Chinese companies obtain advanced Nvidia chips subject to Washington's export restrictions, ​but there has been no public finding that it violated ​the rules.

Shipping records from trade-data provider ImportGenius reviewed by ⁠Reuters show Megaspeed's Indonesian subsidiary imported Nvidia hardware between 2024 and 2026, including H100 processors and related components, in shipments from suppliers including Gigabyte subsidiary Giga Computing.

The H100 is among the advanced Nvidia processors restricted from export to China, although the shipments to Indonesia do not themselves establish any violation of US export controls.

Megaspeed's shares were transferred in late 2023 ​to Singapore-based SwiftData, which holds all 10 million of its ordinary shares, according to C4ADS. Reuters could not immediately contact SwiftData.

Read More: Nvidia CEO becomes subject of memes as social media reacts to alleged affair with chinese spy

C4ADS said it could not determine who ultimately ​controls SwiftData, but assessed that Alice ⁠Huang may have continued to exercise influence over Megaspeed after the transfer, citing appearances in which she was identified as its chair.

Seeking answers

The reports of ties between Alice Huang and Jensen Huang have prompted US lawmakers to seek answers from the Nvidia CEO.

Central questions include whether he knew of any alleged intelligence activity and whether sensitive information was compromised, said George Chen, a partner at consultancy The Asia Group.

"In many respects, Jensen may also be viewed as a potential victim if he was deliberately ⁠targeted or manipulated ​without knowledge of the individual's true identity or intentions," Chen said.

The US chipmaker has said its CEO meets with thousands of customer executives ​each year, and that its cloud customers in Asia receive ordinary business information rather than trade secrets or information related to US national security.

Trump said on Monday he "was amazed" by allegations involving Jensen Huang, among the president's closest allies in Silicon Valley. Trump said he had spoken to the CEO, ​who told him that he had no idea that the woman was a spy.

headline: Tariq Fazal defends Imran's medical treatment amid renewed concerns
description: Says government will maintain emergency in K-P until the required objectives are accomplished
author: Naeem Asghar
article_text:
Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry on Tuesday defended the medical treatment being provided to Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) founder Imran Khan, insisting that the government had neither "neglected" his healthcare needs in the past nor would it allow any negligence in the future.

The remarks come amid renewed concerns about Imran’s health following a meeting with his lawyer at Adiala jail on November 2, during which Imran disclosed that his blood pressure had surged to 192, putting him at risk of a brain haemorrhage.

Speaking to reporters at the Parliament House, Chaudhry said that Barrister Salman Safdar had himself acknowledged that medical check-up facilities were "available" to Imran during a media talk outside Islamabad High Court earlier in the day.

"The government was neither previously negligent about his medical treatment nor will any negligence be tolerated in the future in this regard."

Chaudhry maintained that the government would continue to ensure adequate medical care for Imran, adding that the PTI founder had been taken to hospital six times for medical examinations even before the Supreme Court had issued its order.

The Supreme Court on August 18 had ordered that the PTI founder be shifted to Islamabad's Shifa International Hospital within two days for medical examination and treatment.

He noted: "Whenever the need arose in connection with his blood pressure, a doctor was called from London, and his treatment was carried out according to the standards that I believe were necessary for his healthcare."

Taking a swipe at Safdar, the minister said the lawyer appeared to have assumed the role of a "medical specialist" rather than focusing on his legal responsibilities.

"There is no deal or dheel (relaxation) on the table for Imran," he remarked, stating that the only route to his release was through legal proceedings.

While speaking about the situation in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (K-P), Chaudhry strongly criticised the performance of the PTI's provincial government, further accusing the party of failing to deliver development in the province.

He said that an emergency was imposed in K-P as a "measure of last resort" and resulted from the party's "political suicide", owing to its decision not to cooperate with the federal government and security institutions in the fight against terrorism.

Chaudhry added that the government would maintain the emergency in K-P until the required objectives were accomplished.

He further accused the PTI of fomenting "political unrest and confrontation", further stating that K-P was now moving towards peace, development and prosperity.

The government has also previously rejected claims that Imran was being denied proper medical care. Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political and Public Affairs Rana Sanaullah told the Senate on August 25 that Imran was receiving the best available treatment from specialists and that his medical care and jail meetings were being conducted in accordance with the law and relevant court orders.

In February, it was revealed by a report prepared by Barrister Salman Safdar on the SC’s direction that Imran had informed officials that his right eye was functioning at only 15% capacity. Safdar submitted the report to a two-member bench. As a result, the SC ordered that Imran be granted access to his personal physicians in Adiala Jail.

Imran and Bushra Bibi remain incarcerated in Rawalpindi's Adiala Jail. They were sentenced on December 20, 2025, to 17 years in prison in the Toshakhana-II case, which pertains to allegations that the couple unlawfully retained a Bulgari jewellery set gifted by the Saudi crown prince during an official visit to Saudi Arabia.

Taking a swipe at Safdar, the minister said the lawyer appeared to have assumed the role of a "medical specialist" rather than focusing on his legal responsibilities.

"There is no deal or dheel (relaxation) on the table for Imran," he remarked, stating that the only route to his release was through legal proceedings.

While speaking about the situation in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (K-P), Chaudhry strongly criticised the performance of the PTI's provincial government, further accusing the party of failing to deliver development in the province.

He said that an emergency was imposed in K-P as a "measure of last resort" and resulted from the party's "political suicide", owing to its decision not to cooperate with the federal government and security institutions in the fight against terrorism.

Chaudhry added that the government would maintain the emergency in K-P until the required objectives were accomplished.

He further accused the PTI of fomenting "political unrest and confrontation", further stating that K-P was now moving towards peace, development and prosperity.

The government has also previously rejected claims that Imran was being denied proper medical care. Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political and Public Affairs Rana Sanaullah told the Senate on August 25 that Imran was receiving the best available treatment from specialists and that his medical care and jail meetings were being conducted in accordance with the law and relevant court orders.

In February, it was revealed by a report prepared by Barrister Salman Safdar on the SC’s direction that Imran had informed officials that his right eye was functioning at only 15% capacity. Safdar submitted the report to a two-member bench. As a result, the SC ordered that Imran be granted access to his personal physicians in Adiala Jail.

Imran and Bushra Bibi remain incarcerated in Rawalpindi's Adiala Jail. They were sentenced on December 20, 2025, to 17 years in prison in the Toshakhana-II case, which pertains to allegations that the couple unlawfully retained a Bulgari jewellery set gifted by the Saudi crown prince during an official visit to Saudi Arabia.

headline: PM Shehbaz performs dome placement ceremony at Chashma-5 nuclear plant
description: PM Shehbaz calls dome placement at Chashma nuclear plant a historic milestone, praises Pakistan-China cooperation
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday led the dome-placement ceremony at the Chashma-5 (C-5) Nuclear Power Plant in Mianwali.

PM Shehbaz had inaugurated the 1200 MW Chashma Nuclear Power Plant Unit 5 in July 2023. Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir was also present at the ceremony, along with Chinese and other senior officials and representatives of relevant organisations.

Addressing the ceremony, the prime minister described the dome placement as a historic occasion at Pakistan's largest nuclear power plant, which was built in close collaboration with China.

He said that three and a half years after the power plant's inauguration, its dome had been put in place ahead of schedule, calling it a proud moment for Pakistan. He also praised the engineers, technicians and workers from both Pakistan and China for their contributions.

“China's dedication and hard work have helped achieve this milestone, and I am confident that, with the same commitment, we will see this project commissioned ahead of time,” he said.

The prime minister said the project would provide clean, reliable and affordable electricity, describing it as a source of power that would not go off.

“Power that does not rise or fall with the price of imported fuel, power that does not depend on whether the sun shines or the wind blows, power that runs through the night for the factory that must not stop, the hospital that must not go dark and the studies by its light,” he said.

He added that this was what energy security meant for Pakistan, its people and its economy.

Calling Pakistan a climate-vulnerable country, he said the country had a responsibility to pursue energy solutions that supported its economic objectives while protecting the environment.

“This project will turn dreams into hope and hope into reality one day soon,” he said, adding that no nation could build a prosperous future unless it first safeguarded its future.

PM Shehbaz also praised CDF Munir for his leadership during Marka-e-Haq, saying the country had witnessed the courage, professionalism and unwavering commitment of its armed forces under his stewardship.

He also appreciated the CDF Munir proactive and steadfast support for joint efforts to revive the economy and advance Pakistan's socioeconomic development, adding that such resolve could help Pakistan pursue its economic ambitions, attract investment and accelerate development with confidence.

The prime minister thanked China for its support in building the power plant, saying Chashma-5 was the seventh nuclear power unit Beijing had helped construct in Pakistan. He described each unit as a living testament to the friendship between the two countries.

He also thanked Chinese President Xi Jinping, the Chinese government and the China National Nuclear Corporation for their continued support, saying Chinese engineers had worked shoulder to shoulder with their Pakistani counterparts as one team.

With Pakistan and China entering the second phase of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor, he said, Chashma-5 reflected the strength of their partnership by creating economic opportunities and helping build a brighter future for their people.

The prime minister called on the people of Pakistan to harness every resource, technology and citizen's potential to build the country envisioned by its founder, Quaid-e-Azam Mohammad Ali Jinnah.

“A Pakistan that is economically dominant, energy independent and environmentally resilient,” he said.

He prayed that Chashma-5 would stand as a lasting symbol of Pakistan-China friendship and their shared determination to build a prosperous, peaceful and stronger Pakistan.

The prime minister, while congratulating the Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission (PAEC), China Atomic Energy Authority, contractors, engineers, financial institutions and other stakeholders, also acknowledged the people of Mianwali for hosting the landmark project.

Earlier, the PAEC chairman highlighted nuclear energy’s growing contribution to Pakistan’s electricity mix and national energy security. He said the country’s nuclear power plants were safely and efficiently generating 3,530 megawatts of electricity, helping avoid approximately 15 million tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions annually.

Unit 5 of the Chashma Nuclear Power Plant will have a gross capacity of 1,200 MW(e). The pressurised water reactor is expected to become operational by 2030. Upon completion, the unit will provide a substantial source of low-carbon electricity to Pakistan's national grid.

Pakistan currently operates six nuclear power plants with a combined installed capacity of 3,530 MW(e).

The prime minister thanked China for its support in building the power plant, saying Chashma-5 was the seventh nuclear power unit Beijing had helped construct in Pakistan. He described each unit as a living testament to the friendship between the two countries.

He also thanked Chinese President Xi Jinping, the Chinese government and the China National Nuclear Corporation for their continued support, saying Chinese engineers had worked shoulder to shoulder with their Pakistani counterparts as one team.

With Pakistan and China entering the second phase of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor, he said, Chashma-5 reflected the strength of their partnership by creating economic opportunities and helping build a brighter future for their people.
The prime minister called on the people of Pakistan to harness every resource, technology and citizen's potential to build the country envisioned by its founder, Quaid-e-Azam Mohammad Ali Jinnah.
“A Pakistan that is economically dominant, energy independent and environmentally resilient,” he said.
He prayed that Chashma-5 would stand as a lasting symbol of Pakistan-China friendship and their shared determination to build a prosperous, peaceful and stronger Pakistan.

The prime minister, while congratulating the Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission (PAEC), China Atomic Energy Authority, contractors, engineers, financial institutions and other stakeholders, also acknowledged the people of Mianwali for hosting the landmark project.

Earlier, the PAEC chairman highlighted nuclear energy’s growing contribution to Pakistan’s electricity mix and national energy security. He said the country’s nuclear power plants were safely and efficiently generating 3,530 megawatts of electricity, helping avoid approximately 15 million tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions annually.

Unit 5 of the Chashma Nuclear Power Plant will have a gross capacity of 1,200 MW(e). The pressurised water reactor is expected to become operational by 2030. Upon completion, the unit will provide a substantial source of low-carbon electricity to Pakistan's national grid.
Pakistan currently operates six nuclear power plants with a combined installed capacity of 3,530 MW(e).

headline: Australia to mandate AI breach reporting, create regulator after OpenAI breach
description: OpenAI's agent accessed Australia's Medicare medical spending portal without authorisation, from government
author: Reuters
article_text:
Australia will require artificial intelligence companies to report breaches ‌and consider changes to criminal law to address "serious misconduct", Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said on Tuesday, after an OpenAI agent broke into a government website.

The OpenAI agent gained unauthorised access to the medical statistics portal ​of Medicare, Australia's universal health insurance programme, while conducting research on public medical ​spending, the government said in September. The breach triggered a rapid ⁠government review into the incident.

Albanese said his government had accepted all recommendations of the ​review.

"(The recommendations) include mandatory AI company reporting when it comes to misaligned behaviour or cyber ​incidents, and consideration of reforming criminal law in cases of serious misconduct," Albanese told reporters.

"The law needs to get ahead of, and in some cases, make sure that it catches up with what is ​a very fast-changing world."

OpenAI has said it learned of the breach only in August ​and that the incident was unintentional. Its review found no evidence that patient records were accessed by ‌the ⁠agent.

The breach has added to friction between Australia and US technology companies, after Canberra refused ChatGPT maker OpenAI and rival Anthropic exemptions from copyright laws for model training, instead requiring them to negotiate licensing agreements with Australian rights holders.

However, both companies told Australian parliament last ​month that they would welcome ​laws requiring them to ⁠report data breaches carried out by their AI agents, acknowledging the decision to notify was currently at their discretion.

Albanese said his centre-left ​Labor government would set up an AI regulator to oversee security ​controls throughout ⁠the development and deployment of AI systems, identify serious risks and conduct independent evaluations of AI models.

"The AI safety regulator will be able to enforce significant penalties for AI companies ⁠doing the ​wrong thing," he said.

The mandatory AI safety and ​security protections will form part of the government's proposed AI legislation, Albanese said, which it plans to introduce in ​Parliament next year.

headline: School bus overturns near Murree, killing driver, injuring 30
description: It was returning to Gujranwala after a recreational trip with 40 people, including students and school staff on board
author: Aurangzeb Abbasi
article_text:
It was returning to Gujranwala after a recreational trip with 40 people, including students and school staff on board

A school bus carrying students and staff overturned near Shawala on the Expressway Link Road near Murree, killing the driver and injuring 30 students and staff members. Three of the injured were reported to be in critical condition.

The bus belonged to Al-Hamd Public Model School in Chadiyala Khurd, near Aimenabad in Gujranwala, and was returning to the city after a recreational trip to Murree. A total of 40 people, including students and school staff, were on board.

The bus reportedly went out of control and overturned near Shawala, triggering panic among the passengers. The driver died on the spot.

Teams from Rescue 1122 Murree rushed to the scene after receiving information about the accident and launched a rescue operation.

Rescuers pulled the injured passengers from the wreckage, provided them with first aid and shifted 30 students and staff members to the Tehsil Headquarters Hospital in Murree.

Local residents also joined the rescue efforts and helped the injured.

Murree Deputy Commissioner Agha Zaheer Abbas Shirazi and other district administration officials reached the site and supervised the rescue operation, which was completed under the supervision of Incident Commander Engineer Kamran Rashid.

Police also reached the scene and launched an investigation to determine the cause of the accident.

headline: Nvidia's clubby board faces a sticky 'honey pot' test
description: Its advanced chips fuel the AI race, while China dismissed spying claims as baseless slander.
author: Reuters
article_text:
Revelations that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had an affair with a businesswoman suspected of being a Chinese spy have forced the chipmaker's board to confront more than ordinary executive misconduct, raising ​existential questions for the company and concerns about the board's ability to investigate its CEO independently.

Among corporate leaders, "There have definitely been ‌affair scandals and sexual-harassment scandals. But honey-pot scandals? No," said Ann Lipton, a University of Colorado law professor who follows boardroom issues.

She was using a term for an espionage ploy in which an operative entraps a target by feigning romantic interest. Historical examples include the Profumo Affair in the early 1960s and tend to involve diplomatic or political consequences.

US President Donald Trump ​said on Monday the FBI was probing Huang's relationship, a day after Nvidia's board launched an internal investigation "regarding the national security concerns raised in news ​reports, ," according to an email Huang sent to Nvidia employees and released by the company.

The company's advanced semiconductors are at the ⁠heart of a global race for AI superiority. China's Foreign Ministry said the spying claim was "a groundless accusation, slander, and a smear."

Nvidia co-founder Huang, 63, has ​no obvious successor and close ties to Trump. He owns 3.6% of its stock and has dozens of direct reports, suggesting a tight grip on the company.

Shares ​in Nvidia fell Monday as Huang's future came under scrutiny. But the stock later trimmed its decline to close 4% lower as some investors bet that the CEO could survive the crisis.

Board's credibility

Unusually among its peers, Nvidia operates without a board chair among its 11 directors. While the company considers all but Huang independent, three independent directors have served since the 1990s ​and a fourth, Mark Stevens, for most of that time. Only two have joined the board since 2021.

The clubby roster may not be so unusual ​by the standards of charismatic Silicon Valley company founders like Apple's Steve Jobs, who died in 2011.

But the US probe has heightened scrutiny of whether directors who have worked alongside ‌Huang for ⁠decades are sufficiently independent to investigate his conduct.

"If you have a figure like Steve Jobs, I think people on Wall Street as well as in Silicon Valley would say they're entitled to some leeway or deference," said Marc Goldstein, head of US research for proxy adviser Institutional Shareholder Services.

Such deference could now raise questions about whether the board provided sufficient oversight of a CEO whose own judgment has come under scrutiny.

Nvidia said on Sunday that while its board had no ​reason to believe that either US national ​security or Nvidia secrets were ⁠compromised, its inquiry would examine all available information. The board said it had confidence in the CEO and his leadership team.

Goldstein said board members running that investigation should be given the latitude to hire their own legal advisers to bolster their ​credibility.

The company also might consider keeping long-serving directors away from the probe, he added, to avoid legal challenges from ​shareholders claiming it wasn't ⁠sufficiently independent.

Political economy

Yale University management professor Jeffrey Sonnenfeld said the company faces additional national-security questions because of the ties between Huang and Trump. Trump, who has praised Huang, said on Monday that he had spoken to the executive and thought he would "be in good shape."

Washington has imposed restrictions on exports of advanced AI chips to China since 2022. Last ⁠year the ​Trump administration allowed Nvidia to resume certain China shipments under arrangements in which the US ​government receives a cut of the company's China chip sales.

The deal makes any suggestion of foreign espionage more sensitive for both executives and US government officials, Sonnenfeld said. "That's why you don't want state ​capitalism arrangements. You don't want the US government to be so involved in private companies," he said.
