headline: PPP Punjab demands devolution of power to local govts
description: Faryal Talpur is scheduled to hold direct meetings with party workers, office-bearers during her visit to province
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Central Punjab General Secretary Syed Hassan Murtaza has called for the devolution of administrative and financial powers to the grassroots level through local government elections, arguing that the creation of new provinces would not resolve people's problems unless the existing governance structure was reformed.

Addressing a press conference at the Punjab Secretariat, Murtaza said that instead of drawing the country into debates over new provinces and administrative units, the government should focus on providing relief from inflation, unemployment and rising electricity and petroleum prices.

He maintained that administrative shortcomings could not be addressed without empowering local governments and transferring authority to the grassroots.

Murtaza said the PPP believed in the Constitution and democracy, and that decisions concerning the country's future must be taken through constitutional, legal and democratic procedures rather than according to the wishes of an individual or a particular group.

He also announced that the party would intensify its organisational activities across Punjab, with senior PPP leader Faryal Talpur scheduled to hold direct meetings with party workers and office-bearers during her five-day visit to the province.

She would hear their concerns, suggestions and organisational complaints, while consultations would also be held to strengthen the party structure and improve its prospects in future elections. He said several political personalities were also expected to join the PPP during the visit.

Murtaza said Talpur's meetings would not be confined to Lahore but would extend to different districts and, wherever possible, tehsil-level organisations.

The party was also considering allocating two to three days every month for her visits to Punjab, with each visit focusing on a particular division.

Representatives of the People's Lawyers Forum, People's Youth, Pakistan People's Students Federation, labour wing and women's wing would also participate in the consultations.

He clarified that the initiative was not intended to establish a parallel organisational structure, adding that any recommendations for organisational changes would be submitted to the party chairman for approval in accordance with the party's constitution.

New provinces debate

Commenting on the debate over the creation of new provinces, Murtaza said the PPP had already presented its position, backed by arguments, and proposed alternative solutions rather than merely opposing the idea.

He questioned why the government was discussing new provinces when it had failed to address administrative shortcomings in the existing system.

He said the 18th Constitutional Amendment had envisaged the transfer of powers from the federation to the provinces, but the process had not been completed at the grassroots level.

While authority had been devolved from the federal government to provincial governments, the latter had further concentrated powers instead of transferring them to districts and local governments through Provincial Finance Commission awards.

He questioned whether smaller districts were receiving their legitimate financial and administrative resources, saying development funds were frequently distributed on political considerations.

According to him, even basic development schemes, including the construction of streets and drainage systems, had become subject to discretionary political decisions.

Murtaza said holding local government elections and devolving powers to the grassroots had been among the fundamental commitments contained in the written agreement between the PPP and the government. However, despite repeated demands, meaningful progress had not been made.

He maintained that local governments, student unions and labour unions were essential institutions for producing new political leadership, particularly among young people and working-class communities.

Questioning the practical benefits of creating new provinces, he asked how such a move would reduce petroleum and electricity prices, eliminate unemployment, control inflation or improve law and order.

Referring to Islamabad, he said that despite the concentration of the country's top political leadership, bureaucracy and administrative resources in the federal capital, serious shortcomings persisted in its healthcare system.

He questioned whether creating additional administrative units would achieve anything beyond increasing public expenditure.

article_html:
LAHORE:

Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Central Punjab General Secretary Syed Hassan Murtaza has called for the devolution of administrative and financial powers to the grassroots level through local government elections, arguing that the creation of new provinces would not resolve people's problems unless the existing governance structure was reformed.

Addressing a press conference at the Punjab Secretariat, Murtaza said that instead of drawing the country into debates over new provinces and administrative units, the government should focus on providing relief from inflation, unemployment and rising electricity and petroleum prices.

He maintained that administrative shortcomings could not be addressed without empowering local governments and transferring authority to the grassroots.

Murtaza said the PPP believed in the Constitution and democracy, and that decisions concerning the country's future must be taken through constitutional, legal and democratic procedures rather than according to the wishes of an individual or a particular group.

He also announced that the party would intensify its organisational activities across Punjab, with senior PPP leader Faryal Talpur scheduled to hold direct meetings with party workers and office-bearers during her five-day visit to the province.

She would hear their concerns, suggestions and organisational complaints, while consultations would also be held to strengthen the party structure and improve its prospects in future elections. He said several political personalities were also expected to join the PPP during the visit.

Murtaza said Talpur's meetings would not be confined to Lahore but would extend to different districts and, wherever possible, tehsil-level organisations.

The party was also considering allocating two to three days every month for her visits to Punjab, with each visit focusing on a particular division.

Representatives of the People's Lawyers Forum, People's Youth, Pakistan People's Students Federation, labour wing and women's wing would also participate in the consultations.

He clarified that the initiative was not intended to establish a parallel organisational structure, adding that any recommendations for organisational changes would be submitted to the party chairman for approval in accordance with the party's constitution.

New provinces debate

Commenting on the debate over the creation of new provinces, Murtaza said the PPP had already presented its position, backed by arguments, and proposed alternative solutions rather than merely opposing the idea.

He questioned why the government was discussing new provinces when it had failed to address administrative shortcomings in the existing system.

He said the 18th Constitutional Amendment had envisaged the transfer of powers from the federation to the provinces, but the process had not been completed at the grassroots level.

While authority had been devolved from the federal government to provincial governments, the latter had further concentrated powers instead of transferring them to districts and local governments through Provincial Finance Commission awards.

He questioned whether smaller districts were receiving their legitimate financial and administrative resources, saying development funds were frequently distributed on political considerations.

According to him, even basic development schemes, including the construction of streets and drainage systems, had become subject to discretionary political decisions.

Murtaza said holding local government elections and devolving powers to the grassroots had been among the fundamental commitments contained in the written agreement between the PPP and the government. However, despite repeated demands, meaningful progress had not been made.

He maintained that local governments, student unions and labour unions were essential institutions for producing new political leadership, particularly among young people and working-class communities.

Questioning the practical benefits of creating new provinces, he asked how such a move would reduce petroleum and electricity prices, eliminate unemployment, control inflation or improve law and order.

Referring to Islamabad, he said that despite the concentration of the country's top political leadership, bureaucracy and administrative resources in the federal capital, serious shortcomings persisted in its healthcare system.

He questioned whether creating additional administrative units would achieve anything beyond increasing public expenditure.

headline: Pakistan, US seek more academic exchanges
description: Pakistan, US seek more academic exchanges
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
.

Pakistan and the United States on Tuesday agreed to promote closer exchanges between think tanks and academic institutions to deepen mutual understanding and encourage dialogue on regional and international issues.

The understanding was reached during a meeting between FM Ishaq Dar and former US assistant secretary of state for South Asian affairs Ambassador Robin Raphel. A statement said the two sides discussed matters of mutual interest.

Dar appreciated the positive trajectory of Pakistan-US relations and underscored the importance of sustained engagement to further strengthen bilateral cooperation.

headline: Forces seize 700kg explosives in Waziristan
description: Forces seize 700kg explosives in Waziristan
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
.

Security forces on Tuesday recovered 700kg of locally made explosives, a missile and other equipment during a search and clearance operation in different areas of North Waziristan.

The operation was underway in several areas, where security forces searched 62 more houses and several compounds.

The sources said searches were completed at 17 compounds between Api village and Haider Khel, 28 in Maski and 17 in other areas. Fourteen targeted locations were also cleared in Hassu Khel.

During an operation in Mosaki, security forces recovered 700 kilogrammes of locally made explosives.

headline: Maryam dares PML-Q ministers to resign
description: Maryam dares PML-Q ministers to resign
author: rameez.khan
article_text:
Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif on Tuesday challenged PML-Q ministers to resign if they had reservations about her government, taking a fresh swipe at Federal Minister Chaudhary Salik Hussain amid an escalating war of words between the two coalition partners.

She also linked the criticism of her government to preparations for the upcoming general elections, insisting that political opponents were increasingly active as the electoral contest drew closer.

The federal government, led by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, appears either unwilling to intervene or indifferent to the growing confrontation between a member of his cabinet and the Punjab chief minister, who belongs to his own party.

Salik Hussain has remained firm in his allegations of corruption against the Punjab government, while his party, the PML-Q, an ally of the PML-N, has repeatedly taken aim at Maryam Nawaz.

Asked why the PML-N should not remove Federal Minister Salik Hussain and his younger brother, Punjab Minister Shafy Hussain, if it believed the Chaudhary family was part of a wider political conspiracy against the provincial government, Punjab Information Minister Azma Bukhari said there was no reason to dismiss either minister.

"Why should we boot out any minister when our government has no issue with them?" she said, adding that those who had reservations about the government should resign themselves.

Her response effectively placed the responsibility for any possible departure on the PML-Q ministers rather than the PML-N leadership. It also lent weight to recent remarks by the PML-Q information secretary that the PML-N had neither given his party any ministries nor did it have the authority to take them away.

Maryam Nawaz was speaking at a ceremony in Jhelum for the distribution of Honhaar scholarships and laptops among students. She said opposition parties were stepping up their political activities as the next general elections approached, but maintained that meaningful development work, rather than rhetoric, would ultimately win votes.

She said those unfamiliar with public issues were trying to act smart and distract her from serving the people of Punjab.

"I swear I will not spare any minister if evidence of corruption emerges against them," she said.

In an apparent reference to Moonis Elahi, son of former Punjab chief minister Chaudhary Parvez Elahi and a cousin of Salik Hussain, Maryam said those associated with corruption and bribery had earned notoriety but were still living outside the country.

"I am not claiming that corruption has been completely eliminated. But whenever I come across corruption in Punjab, I pursue the matter relentlessly," she said.

Meanwhile, the Punjab government has withdrawn Elite Force security provided to Federal Minister Chaudhary Salik Hussain, according to PML-Q Information Secretary Mustafa Malik, who criticised the move as an attempt to silence even constructive criticism of the provincial government.

"The information about the withdrawal of Elite Force security from Federal Minister Chaudhary Salik Hussain is correct," Malik said, confirming the development on behalf of the party.

Reacting to the decision, Malik urged Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz to take notice, saying the provincial government was unable to tolerate even positive criticism.\",RAMEEZ KHAN,National

headline: JI, govt agree on outline for levy relief
description: JI, govt agree on outline for levy relief
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
The JI on Tuesday said it had agreed with the government on the broad outlines of an agreement to extend petroleum-related relief to consumers, but warned it could resume its long march if the negotiations failed to produce a concrete outcome on its demand for abolishing the petroleum levy.

The government and JI held a 10th round of talks on the petroleum levy, with both sides agreeing on the need to provide relief to consumers, particularly low-income households, while discussions on a phased reduction of the levy also came under discussion.

Speaking at a press conference after the 10th round of talks with the government committee, JI deputy chief Liaquat Baloch said the two sides had agreed on the need to expand the existing relief measures, while the government would consult the IMF on continuing the relief.

He said providing relief to the public remained the foremost concern during the negotiations and that the government had acknowledged difficulties in the supply of petroleum products due to the global situation.

Baloch said JI had proposed including vehicles with engines of up to 1,000cc and the agricultural sector in the relief scheme. He said the government had also acknowledged that JI's demand for abolishing the petroleum levy was legitimate.

"Our demand is that the levy should be abolished immediately and the public should be given clear relief," he said, criticising the government for being unwilling to cut its luxuries and putting the burden of the Federal Board of Revenue's (FBR) failures on consumers.

Baloch said the two sides had agreed on the broad outlines of a draft agreement during Tuesday's meeting, with the government expected to share further details in the coming days.

He said that the government had informed the JI delegation that it had started working on a plan to address its revenue requirements and would share a framework for gradually reducing the levy after consultations with the IMF.

He said another meeting was expected on Wednesday or Thursday, while the final decision on the proposed agreement would be taken during a possible meeting between Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and JI chief Hafiz Naeemur Rehman.

Following that meeting, the party would decide whether to proceed with its planned long march, he added. The JI leader claimed that the party's protest had helped halt increases in petroleum prices and secured relief of Rs146 per litre on diesel and Rs120 per litre on petrol. "The process has now reached the stage of final decisions," he said.

He said JI remained committed to peaceful political engagement but would withdraw from the negotiations if it found that the government was unwilling to move forward.

"Our only goal is that the people should get relief, that there should be a reduction in production costs, that the economy should run and that people should get employment," he said.

Baloch said JI had proposed including vehicles with engines of up to 1,000cc and the agricultural sector in the relief scheme. He said the government had also acknowledged that JI's demand for abolishing the petroleum levy was legitimate.

"Our demand is that the levy should be abolished immediately and the public should be given clear relief," he said, criticising the government for being unwilling to cut its luxuries and putting the burden of the Federal Board of Revenue's (FBR) failures on consumers.
Baloch said the two sides had agreed on the broad outlines of a draft agreement during Tuesday's meeting, with the government expected to share further details in the coming days.

He said that the government had informed the JI delegation that it had started working on a plan to address its revenue requirements and would share a framework for gradually reducing the levy after consultations with the IMF.

He said another meeting was expected on Wednesday or Thursday, while the final decision on the proposed agreement would be taken during a possible meeting between Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and JI chief Hafiz Naeemur Rehman.

Following that meeting, the party would decide whether to proceed with its planned long march, he added. The JI leader claimed that the party's protest had helped halt increases in petroleum prices and secured relief of Rs146 per litre on diesel and Rs120 per litre on petrol. "The process has now reached the stage of final decisions," he said.
He said JI remained committed to peaceful political engagement but would withdraw from the negotiations if it found that the government was unwilling to move forward.
"Our only goal is that the people should get relief, that there should be a reduction in production costs, that the economy should run and that people should get employment," he said.

headline: Virtual Assets Alliance of Pakistan launched
description: Hunza Asif, founder of Asia Web3 Alliance Japan, has been appointed the alliance's first chairperson
author: Irshad Ansari
article_text:
The Virtual Assets Alliance of Pakistan (Vaap) has been formally launched to improve the protection of cryptocurrency users, raise investor awareness and promote transparency and responsible practices in the country's digital assets industry.

The announcement was made at a press conference, where HTX Country Manager Syed Ehtesham Hamdani said the platform aimed to bring cryptocurrency users and businesses together.

Hunza Asif, founder of Asia Web3 Alliance Japan, has been appointed the alliance's first chairperson, while Hamdani has been named its senior vice-chairman.

Hamdani said Pakistan ranked third globally in cryptocurrency adoption, according to a global adoption index. However, he cautioned that estimates suggesting the country had 20 million cryptocurrency users were unverified, adding that no independently verified figures were available on the number of users.

He said the alliance would work to collect reliable data on cryptocurrency users, raise investor awareness and promote cybersecurity education.

The platform also brings together industry experts and prominent stakeholders and aims to encourage responsible market activities, evidence-based policy discussions, independent research and cooperation with local institutions, he added.

According to Hamdani, the alliance would work to make Pakistan's virtual assets industry more organised and effective while promoting transparency and responsible practices in the cryptocurrency market.

headline: Encroachments on 1,258 acres of railways land in Karachi
description: Encroachments on 1,258 acres of railways land in Karachi
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
.

Around 951 acres of Pakistan Railways' land in Karachi Division are under private encroachment, while another 307 acres have been encroached upon by government departments, a parliamentary panel was informed on Tuesday.

The National Assembly Standing Committee on Railways was informed that out of 19,594 acres of railway land in the division, 1,258.28 acres were under encroachment.

Briefing the committee, the Ministry of Railways said 363.907 acres had been retrieved over the past four years. Between Jul and Oct 2026, the department removed encroachments from approximately 8.992 acres, with an estimated value of Rs305.67 million. The ministry also shared a schedule for removing further encroachments in November.

The committee, which met at Parliament House under the acting chairmanship of MNA Ramesh Lal, stressed the need to protect railway land, improve coordination with provincial and local administrations and expedite retrieval operations.

headline: Trump elevates Baker as US ambassador
description: Trump elevates Baker as US ambassador
author: Kamran Yousaf
article_text:
US President Donald Trump has nominated career diplomat and current charge d'affaires Natalie Baker as the next US ambassador to Pakistan, a move that could end nearly two years of vacancy in one of Washington's most important diplomatic posts in South Asia and provide fresh momentum to improving bilateral relations.

In a statement issued on Tuesday, the White House announced that Baker, a career member of the Senior Foreign Service with the rank of Minister-Counselor, had been nominated as "Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of the United States of America to the Islamic Republic of Pakistan".

Her nomination has been sent to the US Senate for consideration and will require confirmation before she can formally assume the ambassadorial position.

Baker has been heading the US diplomatic mission as charge d'affaires since January 2025, following the departure of then ambassador Donald Blome. She arrived in Islamabad in August 2024 as deputy chief of mission and continued to lead the embassy after completing her tenure in that position in September 2026.

If confirmed, she will become the first full-time US ambassador to Pakistan since Blome left the country, ending a gap of almost two years during which the embassy was headed by a charge d'affaires.

Blome had assumed office in May 2022 after a gap of nearly four years during which Washington did not have a full-time ambassador in Islamabad. He was the first permanent US envoy to Pakistan since David Hale completed his tenure in August 2018.

Baker's nomination comes at a significant moment in Pakistan-US relations, with both countries having intensified diplomatic engagement over the past year, particularly on trade, investment, counterterrorism and regional security.

She has played an active role in this renewed engagement and is among the most visible American diplomats to have served in Pakistan in recent years.

Unlike many diplomats who maintain a relatively low public profile, Baker has been particularly outgoing, making frequent public appearances, engaging with students, business communities and civil society, and participating in cultural and social events across Pakistan.

Her communication style and visible presence have earned her considerable recognition in the country. She has also been actively involved in promoting American investment opportunities and expanding economic cooperation.

Several Pakistani officials have publicly acknowledged her contribution to improving bilateral ties. In September, Board of Investment Minister Qaiser Ahmed Sheikh praised her diplomatic role and contribution towards strengthening relations, while expressing hope that her responsibilities could be elevated.

During her tenure, Baker has also been involved in high-level discussions on trade, energy, minerals and security cooperation. She accompanied a US business delegation during engagements with Pakistani officials and has repeatedly highlighted Washington's interest in expanding commercial ties.

Her tenure has coincided with a major diplomatic development in the region, with Pakistan emerging as a key mediator during the Iran-US conflict and hosting landmark direct talks between Tehran and Washington. Baker has been involved in the diplomatic engagement between the two countries during this period.

Before arriving in Islamabad in August 2024, Baker served as deputy chief of mission at the US Embassy in Doha, Qatar. Her previous diplomatic assignments included Libya, Kuwait and the US Consulate in Dubai, where she served as deputy director of the Iran Regional Presence Office.

She had also previously served as a consular officer in Islamabad, giving her familiarity with Pakistan and its diplomatic environment.

The nomination comes against the backdrop of a major political shift in Washington. The Democratic Party won control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate in the November 3 midterm elections, dealing a significant setback to Trump's Republican Party.

The new Congress will assume office in January 2027. Until then, Republicans retain control of the outgoing Senate, which could consider Baker's nomination before the transition. If her nomination remains pending when the new Congress convenes, it will have to be considered by a Senate under Democratic control.

Under the US constitutional system, the president nominates ambassadors, but their appointments require the advice and consent of the Senate. The nomination is normally examined by the Senate Foreign Relations Committee before being put to a vote in the full chamber.

The timing of Baker's nomination, shortly after the midterm elections, is significant as it signals the Trump administration's intention to maintain diplomatic engagement with Pakistan despite the changing political balance in Washington.

While the Democratic victory will give the opposition party greater oversight of Trump's foreign policy and appointments, the nomination of a seasoned career diplomat who is already familiar with Pakistan also suggests an emphasis on continuity in bilateral relations.

For Islamabad, Baker's confirmation would provide an opportunity to work with a full-time American ambassador who has already developed working relationships with Pakistan's political, military and diplomatic leadership.

Her nomination has been sent to the US Senate for consideration and will require confirmation before she can formally assume the ambassadorial position.

Baker has been heading the US diplomatic mission as charge d'affaires since January 2025, following the departure of then ambassador Donald Blome. She arrived in Islamabad in August 2024 as deputy chief of mission and continued to lead the embassy after completing her tenure in that position in September 2026.

If confirmed, she will become the first full-time US ambassador to Pakistan since Blome left the country, ending a gap of almost two years during which the embassy was headed by a charge d'affaires.

Blome had assumed office in May 2022 after a gap of nearly four years during which Washington did not have a full-time ambassador in Islamabad. He was the first permanent US envoy to Pakistan since David Hale completed his tenure in August 2018.

Baker's nomination comes at a significant moment in Pakistan-US relations, with both countries having intensified diplomatic engagement over the past year, particularly on trade, investment, counterterrorism and regional security.

She has played an active role in this renewed engagement and is among the most visible American diplomats to have served in Pakistan in recent years.

Unlike many diplomats who maintain a relatively low public profile, Baker has been particularly outgoing, making frequent public appearances, engaging with students, business communities and civil society, and participating in cultural and social events across Pakistan.

Her communication style and visible presence have earned her considerable recognition in the country. She has also been actively involved in promoting American investment opportunities and expanding economic cooperation.

Several Pakistani officials have publicly acknowledged her contribution to improving bilateral ties. In September, Board of Investment Minister Qaiser Ahmed Sheikh praised her diplomatic role and contribution towards strengthening relations, while expressing hope that her responsibilities could be elevated.

During her tenure, Baker has also been involved in high-level discussions on trade, energy, minerals and security cooperation. She accompanied a US business delegation during engagements with Pakistani officials and has repeatedly highlighted Washington's interest in expanding commercial ties.

Her tenure has coincided with a major diplomatic development in the region, with Pakistan emerging as a key mediator during the Iran-US conflict and hosting landmark direct talks between Tehran and Washington. Baker has been involved in the diplomatic engagement between the two countries during this period.

Before arriving in Islamabad in August 2024, Baker served as deputy chief of mission at the US Embassy in Doha, Qatar. Her previous diplomatic assignments included Libya, Kuwait and the US Consulate in Dubai, where she served as deputy director of the Iran Regional Presence Office.

She had also previously served as a consular officer in Islamabad, giving her familiarity with Pakistan and its diplomatic environment.

The nomination comes against the backdrop of a major political shift in Washington. The Democratic Party won control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate in the November 3 midterm elections, dealing a significant setback to Trump's Republican Party.

The new Congress will assume office in January 2027. Until then, Republicans retain control of the outgoing Senate, which could consider Baker's nomination before the transition. If her nomination remains pending when the new Congress convenes, it will have to be considered by a Senate under Democratic control.

Under the US constitutional system, the president nominates ambassadors, but their appointments require the advice and consent of the Senate. The nomination is normally examined by the Senate Foreign Relations Committee before being put to a vote in the full chamber.

The timing of Baker's nomination, shortly after the midterm elections, is significant as it signals the Trump administration's intention to maintain diplomatic engagement with Pakistan despite the changing political balance in Washington.

While the Democratic victory will give the opposition party greater oversight of Trump's foreign policy and appointments, the nomination of a seasoned career diplomat who is already familiar with Pakistan also suggests an emphasis on continuity in bilateral relations.

For Islamabad, Baker's confirmation would provide an opportunity to work with a full-time American ambassador who has already developed working relationships with Pakistan's political, military and diplomatic leadership.

headline: Chashma-5 takes shape with reactor dome placement
description: Chashma-5 takes shape with reactor dome placement
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday called for greater utilisation of the country's resources and human capital to build a Pakistan that was economically stronger, energy-secure and environmentally responsible, according to a statement issued by the Prime Minister's Office Media Wing.

Shehbaz attended a ceremony marking a major milestone for the Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission (PAEC), with the successful placement of the dome of the Chashma-5 (C-5) Nuclear Power Plant at the Chashma Nuclear Power Generating Station.

The ceremony was also attended by Chief of Army Staff and Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Asim Munir, Chinese engineers, senior officials and representatives of relevant organisations. Shehbaz appreciated the dedication of engineers, technicians and workers from Pakistan and China.

"We must increasingly harness our resources and human capital to build a Pakistan that is economically stronger, energy-secure and environmentally responsible," he said.

Highlighting the importance of clean energy, he said the C-5 project was a manifestation of the country's commitment to clean and emissions-free electricity generation.

The prime minister also commended the Chinese partners, saying the milestone reaffirmed the "all-weather friendship" between Pakistan and China and their unwavering commitment to expanding strategic cooperation in economic, security and development sectors.

The C-5 project will have a generation capacity of 1,200 megawatts and is expected to commence electricity generation in September 2030.

In his opening remarks, the PAEC chairman said nuclear power continued to play an important role in Pakistan's energy security by providing reliable and low-carbon electricity.

"Pakistan's nuclear power plants are safely and efficiently generating 3,530 MW of electricity and helping avoid approximately 15 million tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions annually," he said.

He added that nuclear energy accounted for around 16.6% of the country's electricity generation despite representing only 8.6% of its installed capacity. Its share of electricity generation rises to 26% during winter.

headline: IHC orders lawyers' meeting with Imran
description: IHC orders lawyers' meeting with Imran
author: Fiaz Mahmood
article_text:
Sardar Latif Khosa and Salman Safdar, lead counsels of former prime minister Imran Khan and his spouse Bushra Bibi are scheduled to meet their clients in Rawalpindi's Adiala Jail today (Wednesday) at 3pm. The meeting is likely to last one hour.

A division bench of the Islamabad High Court (IHC) comprising Chief Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar and Justice Muhammad Asif on Tuesday directed authorities to facilitate the meeting while hearing Imran and Bushra's appeals against their January 2026 conviction in £190m case.

During the hearing of the case, Safdar told the court that on November 3, he was allowed to meet PTI founder Imran Khan after seven months and his wife, Bushra Bibi, after 11 months.

He said Bushra asked him where he had been for the past 11 months. "It is a difficult situation for a professional lawyer. Lawyers should be allowed to meet their clients in jail regularly," he said.

Presenting arguments about the health of Imran and Bushra, Safdar said the condition of the PTI founder's eyes had improved, but his blood pressure remained uncontrolled. Imran told him that uncontrolled blood pressure could put him at risk of a brain haemorrhage, he added.

Safdar said Bushra Bibi's eyesight was in a very poor condition. She had been taken for surgery six months ago and was scheduled to undergo another operation on November 15, he added.

He argued that Bushra Bibi could not receive proper treatment in jail, saying that the female prisoner was returned to her cell on the very day she underwent surgery. Doctors had performed the operation in an emergency, and sending her back to jail immediately afterwards was not appropriate, he said.

"It is not right that I keep arguing the appeals while my client loses her eyesight," Safdar told the court.

He said if the court could not grant her bail, it could grant her bail for four to six weeks to receive medical treatment. He also requested the formation of a medical board and called for complete medical records to be obtained from Adiala Jail.

Islamabad Advocate General Naveed Malik told the court that Bushra Bibi was being treated in jail and had been provided all necessary medical facilities. He also submitted a record of the treatment provided to her, saying that a medical board visited her for a check-up even on November 8.

Chief Justice Dogar said he had heard Safdar patiently and in detail, but the matter concerning the health of the two prisoners was pending before the Federal Constitutional Court (FCC). Safdar responded that no matter concerning Bushra was pending before the FCC.

Safdar also requested the court to provide paper books for preparing the appeals and grant him time to prepare his arguments. He said the paper books had not yet been prepared or provided to the defence.

The chief justice said the lawyers would be given the paper books and time to prepare their cases.

Sardar Latif Khosa told the court that he had earlier requested a meeting with Imran Khan and had assured it that he would not seek another adjournment if the meeting was arranged. However, he was still waiting to meet his client, he said.

The CJ asked Khosa how long he wanted the meeting to last. Khosa requested at least one hour. Justice Dogar said Khosa could present arguments on the appeals next week after meeting his client.

Safdar also requested another jail meeting with Imran Khan, saying that although he had met him and received instructions, the meeting had not been sufficient. The chief justice observed that Safdar had already been allowed to meet his client and said he was issuing an order only for Khosa's meeting.

The Islamabad advocate general said meetings could be arranged for both lawyers if they assured the court that arguments would begin at the next hearing.

The court directed that both lawyers be allowed to meet their clients in jail and adjourned the hearing.

According to sources, the state law officer and the lawyers later agreed that a one-hour meeting between the lawyers and the jailed couple would take place today (Wednesday) at 3pm.

headline: Wapda under scrutiny over 'Tarbela flaws'
description: Wapda under scrutiny over 'Tarbela flaws'
author: Shahbaz Rana
article_text:
Pakistan's two highest project sanctioning bodies had ordered review of lapses on part of the Water and Power Development Authority (Wapda) in selection of consultants and "weaker design" of the Rs316 billion worth Tarbela 5th Extension Project, official documents revealed on Tuesday.

The documents showed that the Central Development Working Party (CDWP) and the Executive Committee of the National Economic Council (Ecnec) had instructed for establishing a committee, led by the water resources minister, to review all the procedural lapses and delays in project design and execution.

The CDWP - the first administrative tier for approval of the development projects – gave these instructions in May this year, while the ECNEC followed in August at the time of approval of the project, according to the official documents.

In light of the CDWP instructions, the Planning Commission had written to the Water Resources Ministry, which is the sponsoring ministry of the scheme, in June this year to establish the committee. So far, no committee has been established, according to an official of the Planning Commission.

The spokesman for Wapda did not respond to a query whether any remedial measures were taken in the light of the federal government's instructions. The Ministry of Water Resources also did not comment on the matter.

A breach in a protective embankment at the Tarbela dam's T-5 Hydropower Project on Monday caused a large volume of water to flood its tunnel-5, prompting the suspension of construction work indefinitely, according to a report that appeared in The Express Tribune.

The report, while referring to the Wapda's statement, said that during the tunnel excavation of the second bench connecting the tunnel, a weak rock mass collapsed, causing water from the Intake Pit to enter the tunnel and the powerhouse area.

"The water from the Intake Pit has been completely drained, and no further water is entering the downstream work sites," the statement said, adding that dewatering from the under-construction powerhouse had started," it added.

The statement also said that "there is no damage to the main tunnel, under-construction powerhouse, and tailrace culvert or switch yard. Reports of tunnel collapse are incorrect".

Wapda is executing the project to convert the 5th irrigation tunnel of the Tarbela Dam for hydropower generation. The project involves the scaling up of power generation capacity by adding 1,410 MW to an existing Tunnel-5 of Tarbela Dam.

The tunnel is presently being used to release water for irrigation only when the reservoir level is below the minimum spillway operating level and water releases from the existing power units is not adequate.

With the powerhouse installed, the tunnel would continue to carry out the same function and in addition water released from spillway would be diverted through Tunnel-5 and only remaining water would be passed over the spillway.

The official record showed that while chairing the CDWP meeting in May this year, Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal "observed that there are serious lapses on part of Wapda regarding selection of consultants, delay in implementation, weaker design and increase in the cost of the project".

As happens in most of the cases, the CDWP decided that "in view of strategic importance of the project for the safety and operation of Tarbela Reservoir and availing World Bank additional financing, the project may be submitted for consideration of ECNEC with the recommendation that a high-level Committee may be constituted by ECNEC under Federal Minister Water Resources".

The committee's task was "to review all the gaps on part of WAPDA regarding hiring of consultant, enhancing scope of work due to change in design, variation orders (VOs) of the project and rationalisation of cost of the revised PC-1 of the project to ensure transparency and avoid mismanagement in implementation of the Tarbela 5th Extension Project".

Officials said that the Ecnec, which is headed by Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar, also upheld the decision of the CDWP. While considering the project for final approval in August this year, "the ECNEC approved the proposal contained at para-18 of the summary with directions to execute the project in accordance with timelines and to ensure that no further cost escalation takes place."

The para 18 of the Ecnec summary underlined that the revised PC-I was approved at a total cost of Rs 316.4 billion including foreign loan of Rs180.7 billion.

But Ecnec also directed that a high-level committee may be constituted under the federal minister for water resources and planning, member infrastructure and the member monitoring and evaluation section as members to review all the procedural lapses and delays on part of Wapda regarding selection of consultants, enhancing scope of work due to change in design/variation orders (VOs) of the project and rationalisation of cost of the revised PC-I of the project to ensure transparency and avoid mismanagement in implementation of the Tarbela 5th Extension Project.

In the first week of this month, the Planning Ministry issued the authorisation orders and asked the Water Resources Ministry to issue administrative approval in accordance with the Ecnec decision. Ecnec had also allowed the implementation period of the project till June 2028.

The documents showed that the Central Development Working Party (CDWP) and the Executive Committee of the National Economic Council (Ecnec) had instructed for establishing a committee, led by the water resources minister, to review all the procedural lapses and delays in project design and execution.

The CDWP - the first administrative tier for approval of the development projects – gave these instructions in May this year, while the ECNEC followed in August at the time of approval of the project, according to the official documents.

In light of the CDWP instructions, the Planning Commission had written to the Water Resources Ministry, which is the sponsoring ministry of the scheme, in June this year to establish the committee. So far, no committee has been established, according to an official of the Planning Commission.

The spokesman for Wapda did not respond to a query whether any remedial measures were taken in the light of the federal government's instructions. The Ministry of Water Resources also did not comment on the matter.

A breach in a protective embankment at the Tarbela dam's T-5 Hydropower Project on Monday caused a large volume of water to flood its tunnel-5, prompting the suspension of construction work indefinitely, according to a report that appeared in The Express Tribune.

The report, while referring to the Wapda's statement, said that during the tunnel excavation of the second bench connecting the tunnel, a weak rock mass collapsed, causing water from the Intake Pit to enter the tunnel and the powerhouse area.

"The water from the Intake Pit has been completely drained, and no further water is entering the downstream work sites," the statement said, adding that dewatering from the under-construction powerhouse had started," it added.
The statement also said that "there is no damage to the main tunnel, under-construction powerhouse, and tailrace culvert or switch yard. Reports of tunnel collapse are incorrect".

Wapda is executing the project to convert the 5th irrigation tunnel of the Tarbela Dam for hydropower generation. The project involves the scaling up of power generation capacity by adding 1,410 MW to an existing Tunnel-5 of Tarbela Dam.

The tunnel is presently being used to release water for irrigation only when the reservoir level is below the minimum spillway operating level and water releases from the existing power units is not adequate.

With the powerhouse installed, the tunnel would continue to carry out the same function and in addition water released from spillway would be diverted through Tunnel-5 and only remaining water would be passed over the spillway.

headline: Tunnel incident inquiry ordered
description: Tunnel incident inquiry ordered
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Water and Power Development Authority (WAPDA) Chairman Lt Gen (retd) Muhammad Saeed on Tuesday ordered a departmental inquiry into an incident inside the tunnel of the Tarbela Fifth Extension Hydropower Project and directed the immediate implementation of rehabilitation measures to minimise potential delays in the project's completion.

The breach on Monday had prompted the indefinite suspension of construction work on Tarbela Dam and also caused an increased flow of water in the River Indus, with authorities issuing an alert for the areas adjoining the river.

The chairman visited the project a day ago and on Tuesday to review the situation following the incident. WAPDA Member (Water) Engineer Asim Rauf Khan, other senior WAPDA officials, contractors and consultants were also present.

During the visit, the chairman inspected the under-construction project's intake structure, tunnel, powerhouse and other key construction sites. The consultants, contractor and WAPDA's project management team briefed him on the prevailing situation and the measures taken so far.

Later, he chaired a meeting at the project office to review the possible causes of the incident and short-, medium- and long-term measures to address the situation.

The meeting finalised immediate measures, implementation of which has already begun. The consultants, contractor and WAPDA team also agreed that neither the main Tarbela Dam nor any other major structure faced any threat.

The WAPDA chairman directed the consultants to submit a comprehensive report on all aspects of the incident at the earliest. He also instructed the consultants, contractor and WAPDA's project team to immediately implement rehabilitation measures and finalise an emergency response plan to minimise any potential delays in the overall completion of the project.

The Ministry of Water Resources has also sought an initial assessment report from WAPDA, which was submitted today. Federal Minister for Water Resources Mian Muhammad Moeen Wattoo is also reviewing the incident. The WAPDA chairman personally briefed him on the details.

With an installed generation capacity of 1,530 megawatts, the Tarbela Fifth Extension Hydropower Project is being constructed on Tunnel No. 5 of the Tarbela Dam. The World Bank and the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank are providing financial assistance for the project.

WAPDA had awarded a $354.6 million contract for the project's civil works to China's Power Construction Corporation of China Limited in May 2021. The project had an approved cost of $807 million, with the World Bank providing $390 million and the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank contributing $300 million.

Once completed, it is expected to generate an average of 1.347 billion units of electricity annually and increase Tarbela Dam's installed capacity from 4,888MW to 6,418MW.

The project, however, has faced repeated delays, pushing its completion deadline back from the original five-year schedule to September 2027. In September 2024, a project director told a Senate committee that delays had been caused, among other factors, by difficulties in obtaining an NOC from the Indus River System Authority for the closure of Tunnel 5.

The project had also faced a temporary suspension in August 2025 after rising reservoir levels and increased water inflows led to water entering the construction site.

headline: Bilawal urges system reset through democratic unity
description: Bilawal urges system reset through democratic unity
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari has again advised the PML-N-led federal government to adopt reconciliation rather than engaging in confrontation with the opposition, emphasising the need for the government to also take its coalition partners into confidence on key issues.

Bilawal, whose party supports the ruling coalition without becoming part of the government at the Centre, expressed these views on Tuesday while addressing a function organized at the completion of one million housing units for people affected by the 2021 floods in Sindh.

According to the PPP chief, people do not expect their governments to divide the nation and pit people against each other. "People expect their government to work to make their lives easier," he said.

The federal government has been at odds not only with the opposition including Imran Khan's PTIwhose Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) government was suspended after the imposition of emergency and governor's rule in K-P last monthbut also with Maulana Fazlur Rehman's JUI-F.

After Fazl's scathing criticism of the federal government and the powers that be following the K-P emergency, a number of federal ministers attacked the JUI-F chief as government authorities started issuing notices to Fazl-linked businesses and people for alleged rule violations.

Speaking at the groundbreaking ceremony of a hospital in Larkana earlier on November 7, Bilawal urged the federal government and political parties to set aside their differences and engage all political, social and provincial stakeholders to tackle the economic crisis.

The PPP chief then warned that the fallout from the Iran war was placing an unprecedented burden on ordinary Pakistanis, saying that the economic consequences of the conflict were being felt across the world, from America to Larkana.

He described the situation as a major test for governments, stressing that public welfare must take precedence over political confrontation. He urged the federal government to engage stakeholders rather than continue fighting political opponents.

"If we remain engaged in fighting one another, with Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf [PTI], with Maulana [Fazlur Rehman], with terrorists, with India and Afghanistan, then we will not be able to alleviate the suffering of the Pakistani people," Bilawal said.

The PPP chief maintained that political differences must take a back seat to efforts to address public hardships, adding that governments would be judged by their ability to support citizens through the economic difficulties.

In his Tuesday address, Bilawal also obliquely hit out at both Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi and the PML-N, saying that there was indeed a need to "reset" the system, but by allowing the country to be run by people "instead of traders and businessmen" and through unity.

Mohsin Naqvi on July 31 claimed that the country's systems needed a "reset" through the creation of new provinces. The Sindh Assembly, where the PPP is in majority, later passed a resolution against any possible division of Sindh.

Naqvi and some other ministers, however, have continually advocated for the creation of new administrative units with an alleged proposal to divide Sindh into two provinces.

Bilawal reiterated that Pakistan, along with the rest of the world, was facing an economic crisis and that the country's politics did indeed need to be reset to deal with it.

"[However, for this reset] all political parties should work together instead of fighting one another. The people no longer wanted to hear calls for confrontation and do not want the country's system turned upside down at the wishes of business groups in Islamabad or Lahore."

He urged the prime minister to take his coalition partners into confidence first and engage with the opposition through dialogue rather than opening new fronts of confrontation. "Public relief would remain impossible unless the government and opposition worked together," he added.

The PPP chief also commended Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah for the successful completion of the housing project, urging him to have the project audited by an international firm to show their critics that it has been executed in a completely transparent manner.

KARACHI:

PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari has again advised the PML-N-led federal government to adopt reconciliation rather than engaging in confrontation with the opposition, emphasising the need for the government to also take its coalition partners into confidence on key issues.

Bilawal, whose party supports the ruling coalition without becoming part of the government at the Centre, expressed these views on Tuesday while addressing a function organized at the completion of one million housing units for people affected by the 2021 floods in Sindh.

According to the PPP chief, people do not expect their governments to divide the nation and pit people against each other. "People expect their government to work to make their lives easier," he said.

The federal government has been at odds not only with the opposition including Imran Khan's PTIwhose Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) government was suspended after the imposition of emergency and governor's rule in K-P last monthbut also with Maulana Fazlur Rehman's JUI-F.

After Fazl's scathing criticism of the federal government and the powers that be following the K-P emergency, a number of federal ministers attacked the JUI-F chief as government authorities started issuing notices to Fazl-linked businesses and people for alleged rule violations.

Speaking at the groundbreaking ceremony of a hospital in Larkana earlier on November 7, Bilawal urged the federal government and political parties to set aside their differences and engage all political, social and provincial stakeholders to tackle the economic crisis.

The PPP chief then warned that the fallout from the Iran war was placing an unprecedented burden on ordinary Pakistanis, saying that the economic consequences of the conflict were being felt across the world, from America to Larkana.

He described the situation as a major test for governments, stressing that public welfare must take precedence over political confrontation. He urged the federal government to engage stakeholders rather than continue fighting political opponents.

"If we remain engaged in fighting one another, with Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf [PTI], with Maulana [Fazlur Rehman], with terrorists, with India and Afghanistan, then we will not be able to alleviate the suffering of the Pakistani people," Bilawal said.

The PPP chief maintained that political differences must take a back seat to efforts to address public hardships, adding that governments would be judged by their ability to support citizens through the economic difficulties.

In his Tuesday address, Bilawal also obliquely hit out at both Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi and the PML-N, saying that there was indeed a need to "reset" the system, but by allowing the country to be run by people "instead of traders and businessmen" and through unity.

Mohsin Naqvi on July 31 claimed that the country's systems needed a "reset" through the creation of new provinces. The Sindh Assembly, where the PPP is in majority, later passed a resolution against any possible division of Sindh.

Naqvi and some other ministers, however, have continually advocated for the creation of new administrative units with an alleged proposal to divide Sindh into two provinces.

Bilawal reiterated that Pakistan, along with the rest of the world, was facing an economic crisis and that the country's politics did indeed need to be reset to deal with it.

"[However, for this reset] all political parties should work together instead of fighting one another. The people no longer wanted to hear calls for confrontation and do not want the country's system turned upside down at the wishes of business groups in Islamabad or Lahore."

He urged the prime minister to take his coalition partners into confidence first and engage with the opposition through dialogue rather than opening new fronts of confrontation. "Public relief would remain impossible unless the government and opposition worked together," he added.

The PPP chief also commended Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah for the successful completion of the housing project, urging him to have the project audited by an international firm to show their critics that it has been executed in a completely transparent manner.

headline: Makkah Pact targets no country, says Dar
description: Makkah Pact targets no country, says Dar
author: Naeem Asghar
article_text:
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister (DPM/FM) Ishaq Dar on Tuesday said the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement (MJDA) with Saudi Arabia and Turkiye was a defensive arrangement directed against no country and aimed at promoting regional peace and stability.

Addressing the inaugural session of Margalla Dialogue 2026 in Islamabad, DPM/FM said the agreement reflected Pakistan's commitment to collective security and credible deterrence.

The agreement is "directed against no country" and "intended to contribute to regional peace and stability," he added.

Turning to South Asia, the DPM/FM said unresolved disputes, military asymmetries and unilateral actions continued to undermine strategic stability.

He said these conditions required restraint and responsible statecraft, adding that strategic uncertainty should not become a justification for strategic adventurism.

"Pakistan's decisive and calibrated response to India's unprovoked aggression in May 2025 through Operation Bunyanun-Marsoos demonstrated a resolve and capability to defend our sovereignty," Dar said.

"I pay tribute to our armed forces for their professionalism and resolve in their defence of Pakistan. Our position is very clear," Dar said, adding that "We will defend our sovereignty with determination and pursue peace with equal commitment".

The DPM/FM also reiterated Pakistan's position on the IWT.

"Regional stability also depends on respect for treaty obligations. Pakistan will firmly safeguard its legitimate rights under the IWT and oppose any attempt to weaponise water," he said.

"Where millions depend on the shared resource, honouring agreements is essential to both human security and confidence between the states," the foreign minister said.

Dar said rivalry among major powers had reached its peak, while international institutions such as the United Nations were facing political divisions.

He said the changing global order posed significant challenges for Pakistan, requiring "strength at home" and "effective diplomacy abroad" to safeguard national security and ensure prosperity.

He noted that the shape of the emerging world order remained uncertain, but the choices countries made during the transition would determine whether it resulted in greater cooperation or deeper confrontation.

Dar identified three major developments that required particular attention, including mounting pressure on the international security architecture, growing links between geopolitics and economics, and rapid technological advances.

He said intensifying rivalries among major powers, prolonged conflicts and the erosion of arms control agreements were increasing the risks of confrontation and miscalculation.

He stated that growing reliance on military instruments was narrowing the space for diplomacy at a time when diplomatic engagement needed to expand.

"Multilateral institutions, particularly the United Nations, were constrained by political divisions, while the selective application of international law further weakened confidence in institutions established to uphold international principles," Dar said.

He observed that the inconsistent application of agreed principles undermined their authority and made countries less secure.

"Geopolitics, economics and finance were becoming increasingly interconnected, with trade, technology, energy and access to capital being shaped by strategic competition."

He said instability in the "Gulf and the Red Sea demonstrated how quickly regional crises could disrupt trade and energy supplies and send shockwaves through the global economy".

The DPM/FM also highlighted the implications of rapid technological developments, saying "artificial intelligence, cyber capabilities, biotechnology and space technologies were changing how states competed and how conflicts could unfold."

He said these developments raised "difficult questions about accountability and the rules governing their use."

Dar warned that security crises could quickly turn into "economic shocks, increasing food and fuel prices, threatening livelihoods and placing additional pressure on public services."

He stressed that "policymakers needed to recognise how crises in one sector could spread into others."

Discussing the emerging international system, Dar said a more representative multipolar order could provide a wider range of countries with a meaningful voice in international affairs.

However, he cautioned that a wider distribution of power would not automatically produce a fairer or more peaceful world.

"Effective multilateralism, representative institutions and respect for agreed rules were essential to preventing multipolarity from becoming another source of rivalry and fragmentation," he said.

Dar reaffirmed Pakistan's commitment to an equitable international order based on the United Nations Charter, sovereign equality, territorial integrity and the peaceful settlement of disputes.

The DPM/FM said the theme of this year's Margalla Dialogue, "Changing Global Order - How to Navigate Strategic Uncertainty", reflected the challenges facing Pakistan.

Referring to Palestine, the foreign minister said the notion that might was right was gaining ground as the use of force increasingly displaced respect for international law.

He said the suffering in Gaza, continued occupation and expansion of illegal settlements demonstrated the human cost of impunity.

Dar said Pakistan had used its 2025-26 membership of the United Nations Security Council to promote the peaceful settlement of disputes.

He stated that during Pakistan's presidency of the Security Council in July 2025, the council had unanimously adopted Pakistan-initiated Resolution 2788 on strengthening mechanisms for the peaceful settlement of disputes.

He added that the council had adopted another Pakistan-initiated presidential statement by consensus on November 5, reaffirming the importance of sustained diplomacy, mediation and dialogue even during active hostilities.

The DPM/FM said the international community needed reliable mechanisms to prevent disputes from escalating and bring conflicts towards peaceful resolution during periods of strategic uncertainty.

Referring to Pakistan's regional diplomacy, Dar said the country's "facilitation of talks between the United States and Iran in Islamabad" in April 2026 reflected its commitment to peaceful dialogue.

He recalled that the subsequent Islamabad memorandum of understanding, signed on June 18, provided an important foundation for further negotiations and diplomatic efforts.

Dar said, "Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir and the Foreign Office had remained closely engaged in these efforts".

He stated that their sustained engagement had played an important role in Pakistan's efforts to facilitate dialogue and advance regional peace.

He also referred to Pakistan's diplomatic coordination with China.

"Pakistan and China had jointly issued a five-point initiative in Beijing on March 31, 2026, aimed at restoring peace and stability in the Gulf and Middle East through dialogue and diplomacy," he said.

Dar observed that the initiative also called for the free movement of vessels through maritime routes without restrictions, permits or charges.

He stated that "he had remained actively engaged with regional partners, including Qatar and the foreign ministers of Saudi Arabia, Türkiye and Egypt, through the Regional Four (R4) framework."

He said the "R4 had also held a joint meeting on October 23 with the European Four (E4), comprising the United Kingdom, France, Germany and Italy."

The DPM/FM said, "Pakistan continued to pursue diplomatic engagement with regional partners and other parties to restore dialogue and facilitate a return to the negotiating table."

He stressed that communication channels needed to remain open even during serious confrontations, warning that closing them would make future crises more difficult to manage and peace harder to achieve.

Addressing the situation in Afghanistan, Dar said terrorism emanating from Afghan territory remained a security challenge for Pakistan.

He stated that "Pakistan would continue protecting its people while supporting efforts towards a peaceful, stable and economically integrated Afghanistan..

The DPM/FM said progress towards that objective required effective action to ensure Afghan territory was not used for terrorism against other countries, particularly Pakistan.

He added that "these challenges tested Pakistan's ability to protect national security while maintaining prospects for a more stable neighbourhood."

Turning to economic diplomacy, the DPM/FM said Pakistan's ability to navigate global uncertainty depended on the strength it developed domestically.

He stressed that a resilient economy and technological capabilities provided the country with greater freedom to pursue its priorities and withstand external shocks.

"Economic diplomacy was central to his responsibilities as foreign minister."

He stated that he was working with international partners to expand markets for Pakistani products, attract productive investment and strengthen technological cooperation.

"These efforts were intended to help Pakistani businesses grow, create employment opportunities and improve livelihoods."

He added that opportunities secured abroad could produce lasting benefits when domestic institutions delivered, businesses had confidence to invest and people possessed the necessary skills.

Dar also called for greater international attention to the development needs of developing countries.

He said, "Domestic efforts needed to be supported by an international system that provided developing countries with fair opportunities for progress."

The DPM/FM stressed that the emerging global order must address the legitimate development needs of the Global South.

He said equitable access to finance, support for climate adaptation and access to emerging technologies would determine whether developing countries could participate fully in the next phase of global economic growth.

Dar warned that an "international order which left developing countries unable to create jobs, improve living standards and withstand crises would struggle to deliver lasting stability."

Concluding his address, the DPM/FM said the future international order would be shaped by the decisions countries made today.

He reaffirmed that Pakistan would make those decisions with a clear sense of responsibility towards safeguarding its sovereignty, advancing the well-being of its people and contributing to a more peaceful and equitable world.

Dar thanked the Islamabad Policy Research Institute (IPRI) for organising Margalla Dialogue 2026 and wished participants productive deliberations during the two-day event.
