headline: Nine rare vultures spotted
description: Nine rare vultures spotted
author: Asif Mehmood
article_text:
At least nine rare vultures belonging to two species have been spotted in the tribal area of Rojhan in Rajanpur district, raising hopes of their return to parts of South Punjab.

According to wildlife officials, the birds belong to the Himalayan griffon and cinereous vulture species.

Wildlife rangers have begun monitoring their movement and stay in the area to ensure their safety and assess the conditions of their natural habitat.

The Punjab Wildlife and Parks Department said sightings of different vulture species had been reported intermittently from various parts of the region over the past year.

The latest sighting is significant because of the presence of the birds in the same area.

However, continued monitoring and evidence would be required to establish whether the sightings indicate a permanent return or successful breeding in the region.

According to experts, one of the major reasons behind a sharp decline in the vulture population in Punjab is the use of a drug administered to livestock. Studies have found that vultures feeding on the carcasses of animals treated with the drug suffered kidney failure, resulting in widespread deaths.

The government had banned the veterinary use of diclofenac in 2006, although other toxic drugs, contaminated food sources and habitat loss continue to pose threats.

A vulture breeding centre is operating in the Changa Manga forest to support the conservation. Established by WWF-Pakistan in collaboration with partners, the facility focuses on the captive breeding of white-rumped vultures with the aim of increasing their population and reintroducing them into their habitats.

Vultures play an important role in maintaining ecological balance by feeding on animal carcasses and helping prevent the spread of certain diseases. Their declining population can disrupt natural ecosystems, making habitat protection, access to safe food and the prevention of toxic veterinary drug use essential for their conservation.

headline: Marriage dispute leaves two dead
description: Marriage dispute leaves two dead
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
.

A dispute over a marriage proposal claimed two lives in Lahore after members of two families allegedly exchanged gunfire, prompting police to arrest five suspects.

Police arrested five suspects belonging to both families, while raids were under way to apprehend others allegedly involved in the double murder.

Police said the dispute began when Sarwar approached his brother Saeed with a marriage proposal for his son,

Allah Ditta. However, Saeed allegedly rejected the proposal.

headline: Falak Javed's bail hearing adjourned
description: Falak Javed's bail hearing adjourned
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
.

An anti-terrorism court (ATC) on Tuesday adjourned the bail application of PTI activist Falak Javed in the Jinnah House attack case until November 16 after her counsel failed to appear for arguments.

The prosecution also sought more time to produce the case record.

ATC Judge Manzar Ali Gill directed the prosecution to submit the complete case record at the next hearing and asked the defence counsel to conclude arguments on the bail application.

Falak Javed had filed the bail petition from jail.

Her counsel had argued that she was arrested in the case after a delay of three years, maintaining that she was innocent and deserved to be released on bail.

However, the investigating officer maintained that the accused was involved in the attack on Jinnah House.

The case was registered under an FIR at Sarwar Road Police Station.

It accuses PTI leaders of inciting party workers to commit arson and vandalism.

headline: Smog spikes eye, respiratory ailments
description: Smog spikes eye, respiratory ailments
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Vehicles move on a road shrouded in smog on the morning of Diwali, the Hindu festival of lights, in New Delhi, India, October 20, 2025 Photo: Reuters

Vehari

Smog in Vehari city and its surroundings has made breathing unsafe for residents in the mornings and evenings.

The number of local people suffering from various diseases has also increased.

The intensity of smog is increasing day by day in the city as well as suburban areas, including Khanewal Road, Multan Road, Luddan, Machhiwal, Thingi and Pappi Adda, with the atmosphere polluted to a dangerous level.

A citizen said it was particularly difficult to breathe smoothly outdoors during the morning and evening hours due to smog.

A physician, Dr Abdul Rauf Khalid, said there had been an increase due to the smog in patients suffering from eye irritation, throat problems, cough and breathing difficulties. Children, elderly people and asthma patients are the most affected.

He advised citizens to avoid leaving homes unnecessarily, wear masks outside, wash eyes and face with clean water, and immediately consult a doctor if their condition worsens.

Local residents alleged that the major causes of smog in the area included burning of crop stubble and smoke emitted from brick kilns and rice mills, which were still polluting the atmosphere. They said the situation was worsening.

Vehicles move on a road shrouded in smog on the morning of Diwali, the Hindu festival of lights, in New Delhi, India, October 20, 2025 Photo: Reuters

Vehari

Smog in Vehari city and its surroundings has made breathing unsafe for residents in the mornings and evenings.

The number of local people suffering from various diseases has also increased.

The intensity of smog is increasing day by day in the city as well as suburban areas, including Khanewal Road, Multan Road, Luddan, Machhiwal, Thingi and Pappi Adda, with the atmosphere polluted to a dangerous level.

A citizen said it was particularly difficult to breathe smoothly outdoors during the morning and evening hours due to smog.

A physician, Dr Abdul Rauf Khalid, said there had been an increase due to the smog in patients suffering from eye irritation, throat problems, cough and breathing difficulties. Children, elderly people and asthma patients are the most affected.

He advised citizens to avoid leaving homes unnecessarily, wear masks outside, wash eyes and face with clean water, and immediately consult a doctor if their condition worsens.

Local residents alleged that the major causes of smog in the area included burning of crop stubble and smoke emitted from brick kilns and rice mills, which were still polluting the atmosphere. They said the situation was worsening.

headline: Pregnant woman killed in road accident
description: Pregnant woman killed in road accident
author: APP
article_text:
.

A 35-year-old pregnant woman was killed in a road accident near Adda Matti Tal, Aaray Wala, while her baby was delivered through an emergency surgery at a local hospital.

According to Rescue 1122, an emergency call was received from following a collision between a speeding car and a motorcycle. Eyewitnesses told rescuers that the car rammed into the motorcycle carrying a man and two women. One of the women, iqra Bibi, 35, suffered head injuries and died on the spot.

Rescue officials said the deceased was nine months pregnant. At the request of her family, rescuers performed CPR and shifted her to the Bakhtawar Amin Hospital for emergency medical assistance and delivery. Following an operation at the hospital, the baby was delivered and was on ventilator support, rescue officials said.

headline: Punjab govt rules out schools closure
description: Govt rules out schools closure
author: Afzal Talib
article_text:
The Punjab government has decided against closing schools and colleges or imposing restrictions on market timings across the province amid a reported decline in smog levels and forecasts of rain over the coming days.

The Environment Protection Department has not submitted any proposal to the provincial government for closing educational institutions or imposing a lockdown in markets, according to departmental officials.

The department said smog levels in October this year were 33% lower than those recorded during the same month last year.

A survey also indicated a 27% decline.

Experts said smog levels generally continued to rise until November 15, after which they began to decline.

They attributed the expected improvement partly to the wheat-sowing season and a reduction in the burning of crop residues.

Meanwhile, the transport department and traffic police have been conducting daily operations at Lahore's entry points against vehicles emitting excessive smoke.

The Environment Protection Department has also closed more than 30 factories involved in burning tyres and imposed fines amounting to millions of rupees.

The Water and Sanitation Agency (WASA), Lahore Waste Management Company (LWMC) and Environment Protection Department are using smog guns and washing roads to reduce air pollution.

Deputy Director Environment Lahore Ali Ejaz said, on the directions of Senior Minister Marriyum Aurangzeb, more than 30 factories involved in tyre burning had been shut down and fined.

He said smog levels had improved, with October recording a 33% decline compared with the corresponding period last year.

He expected a further gradual improvement after November 15.

Ejaz said no proposal had so far been submitted by any department this year to close schools and colleges or impose market restrictions as a measure to control smog.

Rain forecast prompts PDMA to issue alert

Meanwhile, the Provincial Disaster Management Authority (PDMA) Punjab has directed relevant departments to remain on alert ahead of forecast rain in several districts over the next two days.

According to a PDMA spokesperson, rain is expected in Rawalpindi, Mianwali, Jhelum, Mandi Bahauddin, Attock, Chakwal, Khushab, Bhakkar, Sargodha, Murree and adjoining areas.

Lahore, Kasur, Sialkot, Narowal, Gujrat, Gujranwala, Hafizabad, Wazirabad and Sheikhupura are also likely to receive rain.

Strong winds and rain are forecast in Dera Ghazi Khan, Layyah, Bhakkar, Multan and surrounding areas, with hailstorms possible at isolated locations.

description: Teen held for murder
author: APP
article_text:
.

Police arrested a 15-year-old suspect for allegedly murdering a minor boy.

Police said Adeel, resident of 73-B,15-L, Khanewal, allegedly lured the seven-year-old child to agricultural fields, attempted to sexually assault him and subsequently murdered him. A team under the supervision of DSP Mian Channu Mahmood Akbar traced and arrested the suspect.

headline: Denmark eyes energy partnership
description: Denmark eyes energy partnership
author: Khawar Randhawa
article_text:
Danish Ambassador to Pakistan Maja Derrous Mortensen has expressed Denmark's interest in expanding cooperation with Pakistan in water management, sanitation, energy, environment and civil infrastructure.

During a visit to Faisalabad, she inspected the Eastern Wastewater Treatment Plant project being implemented by the Water and Sanitation Agency (WASA) Faisalabad with Danish support.

The ambassador said Denmark and Pakistan had considerable common ground for cooperation, not only in water and drainage but also in other economic sectors.

She said collaboration across Punjab's 41 water and sanitation agencies could help translate the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals into reality.

The Danish delegation, WASA Managing Director Saqib Raza, Project Director Hafiz Owais Jamal and other officials were also present.

Mortensen reviewed the progress of construction work and expressed satisfaction with its pace.

She described the project as important for Faisalabad, saying its completion would help residents of the city's eastern areas overcome environmental and air pollution and provide them with a cleaner and healthier living environment.

She stressed the need for close coordination between the project team and WASA Faisalabad and expressed Denmark's willingness to support similar development initiatives in the future.

The ambassador said she would also meet the Punjab government, the provincial housing minister and Housing Department officials to discuss the project and related matters.

WASA Managing Director Saqib Raza said progress on the project was satisfactory and that special attention was being given to completing it within the stipulated timeframe.

headline: Leaders demand global intervention on Kashmir
description: Leaders demand global intervention on Kashmir
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Fourth Pillar Media Watchdog President Farooq Mirza and All Parties Hurriyat Conference (APHC) leader Altaf Ahmed Bhat called for intensified international efforts to highlight the Kashmir dispute.

They also urged the United Nations to appoint a special envoy or an independent fact-finding mission to investigate the situation in Indian Illegally Occupied Jammu and Kashmir (IIOJK).

The proposal was discussed during a meeting between Mirza and Bhat, who also chairs the Jammu Kashmir Salvation Movement (JKSM) on Tuesday.

The two leaders expressed concern over alleged human rights violations, continued detention of Kashmiri political leaders, restrictions on press freedom, property-related actions and economic pressures on local families.

They agreed to mobilise overseas Pakistanis and Kashmiris, international media, diplomatic missions and human rights organisations to sustain global attention on the dispute.

Mirza said diaspora communities possess considerable influence and resources that could highlight Kashmir internationally, stressing the need for greater coordination with Pakistani diplomatic missions.

Bhat called for evidence-based advocacy and urged international institutions to take notice of political detentions and restrictions on independent journalism.

Both leaders also agreed to raise the cases of detained Kashmiri political figures before international human rights bodies and legal forums. The meeting was attended by a delegation of journalists and representatives of the Fourth Pillar Media Watchdog.

headline: Climate disasters displace 1,000 G-B families every year: CM
description: Climate disasters displace 1,000 G-B families every year: CM
author: SHABBIR MIR
article_text:
Nearly 1,000 households in Gilgit-Baltistan are affected by glacial floods and other climate-related disasters every year, losing their homes, crops and livelihoods, while the government faces the recurring challenge of rehabilitating and resettling displaced families, Chief Minister Amjad Hussain said on Tuesday.

Addressing the Mountain Women Climate Award 2026 ceremony as chief guest, the chief minister said climate change was no longer a distant warning for Gilgit-Baltistan but an increasingly harsh reality as glacial lake outburst floods (GLOFs) and flash floods repeatedly threaten human settlements, agricultural land and critical infrastructure.

He called for coordinated national and international efforts to protect the region's glaciers, strengthen scientific research and address the growing climate risks.

"The glaciers of Gilgit-Baltistan are a vital water reservoir for the whole of Pakistan, and joint and practical steps at national and international levels are indispensable for their protection," he said.

The chief minister said Gilgit-Baltistan was situated at the confluence of three of the world's great mountain ranges and was home to nearly 8,000 glaciers. Many settlements were located downstream of glaciers, where glacial lake outbursts and sudden floods could cause extensive damage to entire villages.

"Every year, around a thousand households are affected, houses and crops are destroyed, and the government faces the difficult phase of rehabilitating and resettling the affected families. This situation, which has continued for the past several decades, remains a major challenge for the coming years as well," he said.

He said climate-related disasters also inflicted extensive damage on essential infrastructure, including roads, power houses, schools and colleges. Billions of rupees were spent every year on their restoration, placing additional pressure on the region's already limited development resources.

The chief minister said that, until recently, there had been no dedicated institution tasked with protecting glaciers and studying the risks associated with them. In view of this need, the Glacier Protection Authority (GPA) had been established.

He stressed the importance of scientifically assessing the effects of climate change on glaciers situated at different altitudes and developing appropriate protective measures.

headline: Funding woes put 40,000 students at risk
description: Funding woes put 40,000 students at risk
author: Wisal Yousafzai
article_text:
Education programmes run by the Merged Areas Education Foundation (MAEF) in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa's merged districts are facing financial and administrative difficulties, threatening the education of around 40,000 students and leaving hundreds of teachers without salaries.

The foundation runs several programmes, including Literacy for All, Basic Education Community Schools (BECS) and the National Commission for Human Development (NCHD). Sources said four projects had reportedly been dropped from the annual work plan despite approval by the relevant forum, while new admissions under the scholarship programme had been suspended.

Established to improve literacy, enroll out-of-school children and expand access to education in militancy-hit areas, the foundation has implemented various projects over the past two decades. But its operations have been affected by administrative problems and alleged political interference over the past 14 months, sources said.

They alleged that officials from other departments had been appointed to key administrative posts through political influence, including teachers who had left their teaching duties to take up administrative positions. These appointments had affected the foundation's performance and the continuity of its programmes, they added.

The foundation operates around 420 community schools in the merged districts, serving nearly 40,000 children. Disruptions or closures could particularly affect students in remote areas with limited access to government schools.

Sources attributed prolonged salary delays to the expiry of project approval periods and a lack of funds. The original PC-I for the Literacy for All project expired on June 30, 2025, while those for BECS and NCHD ended on June 30, 2026.

Noor Nawaz, a community school teacher, said he and around 200 colleagues had not received salaries for two and a half years but continued to teach despite financial hardship.

He said teachers were increasingly concerned following the imposition of governor's rule and the declaration of an emergency in 12 districts. They remained uncertain about when their outstanding salaries would be paid and whether the education programmes would continue, he added.

Foundation officials said the Literacy for All teachers had been recruited in 2016 under an Annual Development Programme (ADP) project whose original PC-I expired on June 30, 2025.

A revised PC-I had been sent to the Elementary and Secondary Education Department (ESED) for approval and presented to the Pre-Provincial Development Working Party (Pre-PDWP), while the Finance Department had issued revenue clearance, they said.

Approval of the revised PC-I was in its final stages before the Provincial Development Working Party (PDWP), the officials said, adding that outstanding salaries and other dues would be paid once approval was granted and funds released.

They said community school teachers had been paid up to December 2024, but funds for subsequent salaries had not been released despite repeated requests to ESED.

The officials rejected allegations of political interference and appointments against merit, saying all administrative matters were being handled under approved rules and regulations.

headline: Curfew imposed in Mir Ali
description: Curfew imposed in Mir Ali
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
A curfew has been imposed in Mir Ali in connection with an ongoing security operation as au-thorities in North Waziristan have postponed the second-year matriculation examinations at most centres across the district and ordered the closure of the Bannu-Miranshah Road amid a deteriorating security situa-tion.

The Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education (BISE) Bannu announced the postponement in a notifica-tion issued on November 9, following instructions from the North Waziristan deputy commissioner.

The new examination dates will be announced later, the notification said, advising students, parents and edu-cational institutions to await further instructions.

Examinations at Cadet College Razmak and centres in Tehsil Baka Khel along Miranshah Road will, however, proceed as scheduled.

Meanwhile, a curfew has been imposed in Mir Ali in connection with an ongoing security operation. The re-strictions will also extend from Isa to Bobli, according to the administration, which said the Bannu-Miranshah Road would remain closed to all traffic during the curfew.

headline: Gas outage, inflated bills echo in Balochistan PA
description: Gas outage, inflated bills echo in Balochistan PA
author: SHOAIB RAISANI
article_text:
Gas shortages and inflated bills dominated proceedings in the Balochistan Assembly on Tuesday, with government and opposition lawmakers jointly protesting worsening supply disruptions in Quetta as winter sets in.

They said residents were facing prolonged gas outages and low pressure despite receiving exorbitant bills, and lamented that the province's concerns were being ignored.

The speaker summoned the general manager of Sui Southern Gas Company (SSGC) to appear before the assembly next week.

The session, chaired by Speaker Captain (retd) Abdul Khaliq Achakzai, began 50 minutes behind schedule.

Speaking on a point of order, Pakistan Peoples Party lawmaker and Parliamentary Secretary Abdul Samad Khan Gorgage Baloch said gas loadshedding, low pressure and supply disruptions persisted in Quetta. He said the city was also facing prolonged electricity outages and a persistent water shortage.

Deputy Speaker Ghazala Gola said the lack of gas was causing hardship, with women lodging frequent complaints.

National Party chief Dr Abdul Malik Baloch said the crisis had been compounded by disruptions in supplies following the recent war in Iran. He said Balochistan's share of national gas production had fallen from 80 per cent to 15 per cent.

He said LNG supplies from Qatar had stopped, while gas imports from Iran had been suspended in the name of curbing smuggling. The crisis would not ease until border crossings were reopened, he added.

Provincial Minister Bakht Muhammad Kakar said he had recently met Sui Gas officials in Karachi to discuss the shortage. With LNG and LPG supplies disrupted amid the global crisis, he questioned what contingency measures the company had planned.

He said the chief minister had convened a meeting for next week, which would also be attended by Sui Gas officials. The government was making efforts to ensure gas supplies to consumers during winter, he added.

The speaker directed Kakar to include excessive billing on the agenda.

Provincial Minister Mir Sadiq Umrani said inflated bills were as serious a concern as the shortage, citing a case in which a consumer had been charged Rs100,000 for 30 units of gas. He urged the authorities to address the issue, saying the assembly's debate should translate into relief for the public.

He said the SSGC general manager visited the province but failed to address public complaints.

Provincial Minister Ali Madad Jatak said gas supplies to Sariab were almost non-existent, adding that the shortage was not so severe that the provincial capital should be left without supplies. He cited a case in which a person earning Rs15,000 a month ad received a gas bill of Rs20,000.

JUI lawmaker Shahida Rauf said the assembly debated gas and electricity shortages every winter, adding that she had repeatedly raised the issue and government members were now also voicing concern.

National Party lawmaker Rehmat Saleh Baloch described the border region as the province's lifeline and said Balochistan's concerns were being ignored. He said 50 per cent of LNG supplies came from Iran, 15 per cent from Qatar and 15 per cent from Oman, while domestic production accounted for the remaining 20 per cent.

article_html:
QUETTA:

Gas shortages and inflated bills dominated proceedings in the Balochistan Assembly on Tuesday, with government and opposition lawmakers jointly protesting worsening supply disruptions in Quetta as winter sets in.

They said residents were facing prolonged gas outages and low pressure despite receiving exorbitant bills, and lamented that the province's concerns were being ignored.

The speaker summoned the general manager of Sui Southern Gas Company (SSGC) to appear before the assembly next week.

The session, chaired by Speaker Captain (retd) Abdul Khaliq Achakzai, began 50 minutes behind schedule.

Speaking on a point of order, Pakistan Peoples Party lawmaker and Parliamentary Secretary Abdul Samad Khan Gorgage Baloch said gas loadshedding, low pressure and supply disruptions persisted in Quetta. He said the city was also facing prolonged electricity outages and a persistent water shortage.

Deputy Speaker Ghazala Gola said the lack of gas was causing hardship, with women lodging frequent complaints.

National Party chief Dr Abdul Malik Baloch said the crisis had been compounded by disruptions in supplies following the recent war in Iran. He said Balochistan's share of national gas production had fallen from 80 per cent to 15 per cent.

He said LNG supplies from Qatar had stopped, while gas imports from Iran had been suspended in the name of curbing smuggling. The crisis would not ease until border crossings were reopened, he added.

Provincial Minister Bakht Muhammad Kakar said he had recently met Sui Gas officials in Karachi to discuss the shortage. With LNG and LPG supplies disrupted amid the global crisis, he questioned what contingency measures the company had planned.

He said the chief minister had convened a meeting for next week, which would also be attended by Sui Gas officials. The government was making efforts to ensure gas supplies to consumers during winter, he added.

The speaker directed Kakar to include excessive billing on the agenda.

Provincial Minister Mir Sadiq Umrani said inflated bills were as serious a concern as the shortage, citing a case in which a consumer had been charged Rs100,000 for 30 units of gas. He urged the authorities to address the issue, saying the assembly's debate should translate into relief for the public.

He said the SSGC general manager visited the province but failed to address public complaints.

Provincial Minister Ali Madad Jatak said gas supplies to Sariab were almost non-existent, adding that the shortage was not so severe that the provincial capital should be left without supplies. He cited a case in which a person earning Rs15,000 a month ad received a gas bill of Rs20,000.

JUI lawmaker Shahida Rauf said the assembly debated gas and electricity shortages every winter, adding that she had repeatedly raised the issue and government members were now also voicing concern.

National Party lawmaker Rehmat Saleh Baloch described the border region as the province's lifeline and said Balochistan's concerns were being ignored. He said 50 per cent of LNG supplies came from Iran, 15 per cent from Qatar and 15 per cent from Oman, while domestic production accounted for the remaining 20 per cent.

headline: JUI-F announces Nov 15 protests across K-P
description: Decisions were taken at a meeting of the party's provincial executive committee
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Decisions were taken at a meeting of the party's provincial executive committee

Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) on Tuesday announced protests across Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa on November 15 in support of party chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman's position on the province's mineral resources.

The party demanded that details of all agreements with foreign countries on the exploitation of mineral resources be made public and announced an awareness campaign across the province.

The decisions were taken at a meeting of the party's provincial executive committee, chaired by K-P chief Senator Maulana Atta-ur-Rehman at Mufti Mahmood Centre in Peshawar.

The meeting also discussed alleged smear campaigns against party leaders through fabricated videos and photographs, anti-encroachment operations, and the government's mineral policy.

Addressing a news conference after the meeting, Maulana Atta-ur-Rehman said the emergency imposed in the province appeared to be aimed at facilitating anti-encroachment operations rather than combating terrorism.

headline: Tanker involved in incident in Strait of Hormuz: UK maritime agency
description: Iran urges UN, IAEA to condemn US offer of $20m for nuclear information
author: Reuters
article_text:
A tanker was involved in an incident in the Strait of Hormuz, the UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) center said on late Tuesday, citing military authorities.

The status of the crew, the extent of any damage, and possible environmental impact remained unknown, according to a warning posted by the maritime agency on the US social media platform X.

The warning did not identify the tanker or specify the nature of the incident or when it occurred.

Earlier Tuesday, UKMTO said a tanker was struck by an unidentified projectile approximately 19 nautical miles northeast of Limah, Oman, with the crew said to be safe and no environmental damage reported.

Separately, ADNOC Logistics & Services said one of its vessels sustained damage in an attack in the United Arab Emirates’ territorial waters in the Gulf on Tuesday afternoon.

US Treasury chief Bessent moved to military base after Iranian threats, sources say

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has recently moved from his Washington, DC residence to a US military base after Iranian threats against his life, two people familiar with the matter said on Tuesday.

The New York Times first reported the move. A senior intelligence official in the Trump administration warned in a memo seen by Reuters late last month that Iranian plots against US personnel and American citizens had reached an advanced stage.

Bessent has led the US sanctions and economic pressure campaign against Iran, dubbed Operation Economic Outcast, since August to try to push Tehran to end attacks on shipping and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. The crucial waterway has been largely closed since the US and Israel attacked Iran on February 28.

The economic pressure campaign, which coincides with a US naval blockade of Iranian ports, has included sanctions on Middle Eastern bank branches and other financial services firms facilitating transactions with Iran.

"The secretary will not be deterred by the Iranian regime's threats and remains committed to executing Operation Economic Outcast and maintaining the blockade, which together are collapsing Iran's economy," a US Treasury spokesperson said in an emailed statement.

The Times reported the severity of the threats to Bessent was not immediately clear.

Iran urges UN, IAEA to condemn US offer of $20m for nuclear information

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on Tuesday urged the United Nations and the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) to condemn a US offer of up to $20 million for information on Iran’s nuclear program, warning that the move could endanger the country’s nuclear facilities and scientists.

In a letter to UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, the UN Security Council president and IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi, Araghchi described the announcement as "abhorrent" and urged its unequivocal condemnation, according to Iran's official IRNA news agency.

He said the offer, announced through the US State Department's Rewards for Justice program and reposted by the US Central Command (CENTCOM), sought information about nuclear facilities, equipment, scientists and personnel, while also offering possible relocation.

He accused Washington of encouraging espionage against Iran's nuclear program, warning that the initiative could expose nuclear scientists and technical personnel to assassination, sabotage and other security threats.

Araghchi argued that seeking confidential information about nuclear facilities under IAEA safeguards raised serious questions about the credibility and integrity of the agency's monitoring system.

He warned that normal implementation of safeguards obligations could not be expected when nuclear facilities, personnel and sensitive information were exposed to threats of attack and sabotage.

He stressed that Article IV of the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT) recognises countries' right to develop and use nuclear energy for peaceful purposes.

Araghchi called on the UN Security Council to address the potential consequences for international peace and security and hold Washington accountable for unlawful actions.

Araghchi also urged Grossi to safeguard confidential information collected during inspections, prevent its misuse for intelligence purposes and bring the matter before the IAEA Board of Governors.

The US State Department's Rewards for Justice program offers financial incentives for information related to threats to US national security. According to Araghchi's letter, its latest announcement offered up to $20 million and possible relocation in exchange for information concerning Iran's nuclear program.

China can play key role in ending Iran's "neither war nor peace" situation with US: Iranian parliament speaker

China can play a significant role in ending the war and resolving Iran's current situation of "neither war nor peace" with the US, Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said on Tuesday.

In an article published on the website of Iran's Supreme Leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, Ghalibaf, who also serves as Iran's special representative for China affairs and heads Tehran's negotiating delegation with the US, highlighted Beijing's potential role in regional diplomacy.

"China's role in ending the war and the situation of 'neither war nor peace' is significant," he said.

Ghalibaf said China's relations with Iran and Arab countries, along with Beijing's diplomatic initiatives, provide an opportunity to strengthen regional stability and help shape a new regional order.

He said the supreme leader issued detailed instructions concerning relations with China, emphasising specific priorities rather than broad recommendations.

Ghalibaf announced plans to establish a high-level steering and oversight body to coordinate and monitor the implementation of cooperation with Beijing, focusing on strategic coordination, setting priorities, accelerating decisions, and following up on major cross-sectoral issues rather than replacing the responsibilities of government institutions.

He also stressed that cooperation with China should go beyond ceremonial agreements, encouraging concrete projects under a 25-year comprehensive cooperation agreement between the two countries.

Fire breaks out at Iran's South Pars gas platform

A fire broke out at Iran's SPD14D platform in the South Pars gas field on Tuesday, prompting authorities to evacuate all personnel as a precaution, Iranian media reported.

The Pars Oil and Gas Company said operational and safety teams successfully contained the blaze at one of the gas platforms in Phase 14 of South Pars.

The deputy oil minister said earlier that the platform was fully evacuated to ensure the safety of engineers working at the facility, according to the semi-official Fars News Agency.

The official said the situation was under control and that authorities were investigating the cause of the fire, with a gas leak or an operational incident being considered as possible explanations.

The SPD14D platform accounts for 14.5 million cubic meters of South Pars' total gas production of more than 700 million cubic meters, according ot the deputy oil minister.

No casualties were immediately reported.

South Pars, located in the Gulf, is Iran's largest natural gas field and a major source of the domestic gas supply. The field is shared with Qatar, where it is known as the North Field.

Netanyahu, Trump reportedly clash over Iran in tense call: report

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and US President Donald Trump reportedly clashed during a call over the weekend amid disagreements about the possibility of resuming military operations against Iran, media reports said on Tuesday.

The Yedioth Ahronoth newspaper, citing sources familiar with the conversation, said the call focused primarily on Iran and differences between Washington and Tel Aviv about a possible renewal of the war.

Sources described the conversation as particularly difficult and confrontational, with one calling it "a screaming conversation from hell."

Netanyahu's office, however, rejected the account, denying the conversation was contentious. "Fake news, complete nonsense," it said in response.

A senior Israeli official also confirmed that the call had taken place but insisted that it had not been difficult.

article_html:
A tanker was involved in an incident in the Strait of Hormuz, the UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) center said on late Tuesday, citing military authorities.

The status of the crew, the extent of any damage, and possible environmental impact remained unknown, according to a warning posted by the maritime agency on the US social media platform X.

The warning did not identify the tanker or specify the nature of the incident or when it occurred.

Earlier Tuesday, UKMTO said a tanker was struck by an unidentified projectile approximately 19 nautical miles northeast of Limah, Oman, with the crew said to be safe and no environmental damage reported.

Separately, ADNOC Logistics & Services said one of its vessels sustained damage in an attack in the United Arab Emirates’ territorial waters in the Gulf on Tuesday afternoon.

US Treasury chief Bessent moved to military base after Iranian threats, sources say

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has recently moved from his Washington, DC residence to a US military base after Iranian threats against his life, two people familiar with the matter said on Tuesday.

The New York Times first reported the move. A senior intelligence official in the Trump administration warned in a memo seen by Reuters late last month that Iranian plots against US personnel and American citizens had reached an advanced stage.

Bessent has led the US sanctions and economic pressure campaign against Iran, dubbed Operation Economic Outcast, since August to try to push Tehran to end attacks on shipping and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. The crucial waterway has been largely closed since the US and Israel attacked Iran on February 28.

The economic pressure campaign, which coincides with a US naval blockade of Iranian ports, has included sanctions on Middle Eastern bank branches and other financial services firms facilitating transactions with Iran.

"The secretary will not be deterred by the Iranian regime's threats and remains committed to executing Operation Economic Outcast and maintaining the blockade, which together are collapsing Iran's economy," a US Treasury spokesperson said in an emailed statement.

The Times reported the severity of the threats to Bessent was not immediately clear.

Iran urges UN, IAEA to condemn US offer of $20m for nuclear information

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on Tuesday urged the United Nations and the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) to condemn a US offer of up to $20 million for information on Iran’s nuclear program, warning that the move could endanger the country’s nuclear facilities and scientists.

In a letter to UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, the UN Security Council president and IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi, Araghchi described the announcement as "abhorrent" and urged its unequivocal condemnation, according to Iran's official IRNA news agency.

He said the offer, announced through the US State Department's Rewards for Justice program and reposted by the US Central Command (CENTCOM), sought information about nuclear facilities, equipment, scientists and personnel, while also offering possible relocation.

He accused Washington of encouraging espionage against Iran's nuclear program, warning that the initiative could expose nuclear scientists and technical personnel to assassination, sabotage and other security threats.

Araghchi argued that seeking confidential information about nuclear facilities under IAEA safeguards raised serious questions about the credibility and integrity of the agency's monitoring system.

He warned that normal implementation of safeguards obligations could not be expected when nuclear facilities, personnel and sensitive information were exposed to threats of attack and sabotage.

He stressed that Article IV of the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT) recognises countries' right to develop and use nuclear energy for peaceful purposes.

Araghchi called on the UN Security Council to address the potential consequences for international peace and security and hold Washington accountable for unlawful actions.

Araghchi also urged Grossi to safeguard confidential information collected during inspections, prevent its misuse for intelligence purposes and bring the matter before the IAEA Board of Governors.

The US State Department's Rewards for Justice program offers financial incentives for information related to threats to US national security. According to Araghchi's letter, its latest announcement offered up to $20 million and possible relocation in exchange for information concerning Iran's nuclear program.

China can play key role in ending Iran's "neither war nor peace" situation with US: Iranian parliament speaker

China can play a significant role in ending the war and resolving Iran's current situation of "neither war nor peace" with the US, Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said on Tuesday.

In an article published on the website of Iran's Supreme Leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, Ghalibaf, who also serves as Iran's special representative for China affairs and heads Tehran's negotiating delegation with the US, highlighted Beijing's potential role in regional diplomacy.

"China's role in ending the war and the situation of 'neither war nor peace' is significant," he said.

Ghalibaf said China's relations with Iran and Arab countries, along with Beijing's diplomatic initiatives, provide an opportunity to strengthen regional stability and help shape a new regional order.

He said the supreme leader issued detailed instructions concerning relations with China, emphasising specific priorities rather than broad recommendations.

Ghalibaf announced plans to establish a high-level steering and oversight body to coordinate and monitor the implementation of cooperation with Beijing, focusing on strategic coordination, setting priorities, accelerating decisions, and following up on major cross-sectoral issues rather than replacing the responsibilities of government institutions.

He also stressed that cooperation with China should go beyond ceremonial agreements, encouraging concrete projects under a 25-year comprehensive cooperation agreement between the two countries.

Fire breaks out at Iran's South Pars gas platform

A fire broke out at Iran's SPD14D platform in the South Pars gas field on Tuesday, prompting authorities to evacuate all personnel as a precaution, Iranian media reported.

The Pars Oil and Gas Company said operational and safety teams successfully contained the blaze at one of the gas platforms in Phase 14 of South Pars.

The deputy oil minister said earlier that the platform was fully evacuated to ensure the safety of engineers working at the facility, according to the semi-official Fars News Agency.

The official said the situation was under control and that authorities were investigating the cause of the fire, with a gas leak or an operational incident being considered as possible explanations.

The SPD14D platform accounts for 14.5 million cubic meters of South Pars' total gas production of more than 700 million cubic meters, according ot the deputy oil minister.

No casualties were immediately reported.

South Pars, located in the Gulf, is Iran's largest natural gas field and a major source of the domestic gas supply. The field is shared with Qatar, where it is known as the North Field.

Netanyahu, Trump reportedly clash over Iran in tense call: report

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and US President Donald Trump reportedly clashed during a call over the weekend amid disagreements about the possibility of resuming military operations against Iran, media reports said on Tuesday.

The Yedioth Ahronoth newspaper, citing sources familiar with the conversation, said the call focused primarily on Iran and differences between Washington and Tel Aviv about a possible renewal of the war.

Sources described the conversation as particularly difficult and confrontational, with one calling it "a screaming conversation from hell."

Netanyahu's office, however, rejected the account, denying the conversation was contentious. "Fake news, complete nonsense," it said in response.

A senior Israeli official also confirmed that the call had taken place but insisted that it had not been difficult.

headline: Imran Khan undergoes eye treatment at PIMS, receives intravitreal injection
description: Hospital says his vital signs and physical examination were normal, and he remained clinically stable
author: Zaigham Naqvi
article_text:
Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) founder Imran Khan was administered his sixth intravitreal anti-VEGF injection at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) in Islamabad during the early hours of Wednesday, according to a press release issued by PIMS.

“After obtaining informed consent and adopting standard monitoring, precautionary measures and clinical protocols, he was administered an intravitreal anti-VEGF injection by the ophthalmology team,” the statement said.

Imran has received a series of anti-VEGF intravitreal injections in his right eye as part of treatment for right central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO), a condition diagnosed after he reported reduced vision. He received his first injection at the PIMS on January 24. The hospital initially diagnosed him with right central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO), a condition affecting blood flow through the retina, after he reported reduced vision in his right eye.

According to PIMS, Imran was brought from Central Jail Adiala in Rawalpindi to PIMS during the intervening night of November 10 and 11 for a medical check-up and follow-up eye treatment, as advised by his treating ophthalmologist.

“Prior to the procedure, he underwent a medical examination, including ocular assessment. His vital parameters were found to be normal. He was clinically stable, and his general physical examination was normal,” the statement said.

“During his stay at PIMS, he remained vitally stable before, during, and after the procedure," adding that he was discharged at approximately 2:30am, with necessary instructions for further care and follow-up.

The statement said that Imran remained at PIMS for around 40 to 50 minutes before being transferred back to Adiala Jail after his condition was found to be satisfactory.

The development came a day after Imran's sister, Uzma Khan, moved the Supreme Court seeking an early hearing of the case concerning his transfer from Adiala Jail to Shifa International Hospital for medical treatment.

The issue of Imran's transfer dates back to August 18, when the SC ordered authorities to transfer Imran from Adiala Jail to Shifa International Hospital for specialised medical treatment. However, he was taken to PIMS instead and returned to jail after a medical examination. The PTI subsequently filed a contempt petition, alleging that the authorities had failed to implement the court's order.

Imran's treatment so far

In late January, Imran was first taken to the hospital for a minor eye procedure. Five days later, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said that doctors at PIMS had conducted an examination of his eyes and, after obtaining his written consent, carried out a minor medical procedure that lasted around 20 minutes.

Amid controversy surrounding the eye treatment, PIMS confirmed that Imran was administered an anti-VEGF intravitreal injection to treat right central retinal vein occlusion.

The confirmation came as PTI continued to express concern over the founder's health, alleging that jail authorities and the government were obstructing his treatment for a serious eye condition, and demanding immediate medical care that included Imran being treated at Shifa International Hospital.

In February, it was revealed by a report prepared by Barrister Salman Safdar on the Supreme Court’s direction that Imran had informed officials that his right eye was functioning at only 15% capacity. Safdar submitted the report to a two-member bench. As a result, the Supreme Court ordered that Imran be granted access to his personal physicians in Adiala Jail and that he be allowed telephone contact with his sons, Kasim and Sulaiman.

Later, a medical board examining Imran reported an improvement in his eyesight and did not recommend shifting him to a hospital. According to the medical report, Imran’s vision in his right eye improved from 6/36 to 6/9, while his left eye had 6/6 vision with the use of glasses. The assessment was carried out by a board comprising Dr Nadeem Qureshi and Dr Arif, following a detailed examination at Adiala jail.

In March, another medical check-up was conducted at Adiala, after which PIMS stated that Imran had shown significant improvement in his vision following his second dose of an intravitreal anti-VEGF injection. The third dose was subsequently administered on March 23.

Imran received his fourth anti-VEGF injection at the PIMS on April 28, 2026, as part of treatment for right central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO). An optical coherence tomography (OCT) scan conducted before the procedure showed clinical improvement, according to the hospital. His fifth injection was administered on June 15, with doctors again reporting improvement in his eye condition.

Imran's wife, Bushra Bibi, also underwent a medical examination at Adiala in March after complaining of pain in her right eye. She was reportedly examined by Dr Muhammad Arif Khan, head of the ophthalmology department at PIMS. article_html:
ISLAMABAD:

Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) founder Imran Khan was administered his sixth intravitreal anti-VEGF injection at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) in Islamabad during the early hours of Wednesday, according to a press release issued by PIMS.

“After obtaining informed consent and adopting standard monitoring, precautionary measures and clinical protocols, he was administered an intravitreal anti-VEGF injection by the ophthalmology team,” the statement said.

Imran has received a series of anti-VEGF intravitreal injections in his right eye as part of treatment for right central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO), a condition diagnosed after he reported reduced vision. He received his first injection at the PIMS on January 24. The hospital initially diagnosed him with right central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO), a condition affecting blood flow through the retina, after he reported reduced vision in his right eye.

According to PIMS, Imran was brought from Central Jail Adiala in Rawalpindi to PIMS during the intervening night of November 10 and 11 for a medical check-up and follow-up eye treatment, as advised by his treating ophthalmologist.

“Prior to the procedure, he underwent a medical examination, including ocular assessment. His vital parameters were found to be normal. He was clinically stable, and his general physical examination was normal,” the statement said.

Read: Sister seeks health transfer for Imran

“During his stay at PIMS, he remained vitally stable before, during, and after the procedure," adding that he was discharged at approximately 2:30am, with necessary instructions for further care and follow-up.

The statement said that Imran remained at PIMS for around 40 to 50 minutes before being transferred back to Adiala Jail after his condition was found to be satisfactory.

The development came a day after Imran's sister, Uzma Khan, moved the Supreme Court seeking an early hearing of the case concerning his transfer from Adiala Jail to Shifa International Hospital for medical treatment.

The issue of Imran's transfer dates back to August 18, when the SC ordered authorities to transfer Imran from Adiala Jail to Shifa International Hospital for specialised medical treatment. However, he was taken to PIMS instead and returned to jail after a medical examination. The PTI subsequently filed a contempt petition, alleging that the authorities had failed to implement the court's order.

Imran's treatment so far

In late January, Imran was first taken to the hospital for a minor eye procedure. Five days later, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said that doctors at PIMS had conducted an examination of his eyes and, after obtaining his written consent, carried out a minor medical procedure that lasted around 20 minutes.

Amid controversy surrounding the eye treatment, PIMS confirmed that Imran was administered an anti-VEGF intravitreal injection to treat right central retinal vein occlusion.

The confirmation came as PTI continued to express concern over the founder's health, alleging that jail authorities and the government were obstructing his treatment for a serious eye condition, and demanding immediate medical care that included Imran being treated at Shifa International Hospital.

In February, it was revealed by a report prepared by Barrister Salman Safdar on the Supreme Court’s direction that Imran had informed officials that his right eye was functioning at only 15% capacity. Safdar submitted the report to a two-member bench. As a result, the Supreme Court ordered that Imran be granted access to his personal physicians in Adiala Jail and that he be allowed telephone contact with his sons, Kasim and Sulaiman.

Read More: More than meets the eye

Later, a medical board examining Imran reported an improvement in his eyesight and did not recommend shifting him to a hospital. According to the medical report, Imran’s vision in his right eye improved from 6/36 to 6/9, while his left eye had 6/6 vision with the use of glasses. The assessment was carried out by a board comprising Dr Nadeem Qureshi and Dr Arif, following a detailed examination at Adiala jail.

In March, another medical check-up was conducted at Adiala, after which PIMS stated that Imran had shown significant improvement in his vision following his second dose of an intravitreal anti-VEGF injection. The third dose was subsequently administered on March 23.

Imran received his fourth anti-VEGF injection at the PIMS on April 28, 2026, as part of treatment for right central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO). An optical coherence tomography (OCT) scan conducted before the procedure showed clinical improvement, according to the hospital. His fifth injection was administered on June 15, with doctors again reporting improvement in his eye condition.

Imran's wife, Bushra Bibi, also underwent a medical examination at Adiala in March after complaining of pain in her right eye. She was reportedly examined by Dr Muhammad Arif Khan, head of the ophthalmology department at PIMS. The medical report stated that she had been experiencing blurred vision and black spots in her right eye; she also reported seeing flashes in the dark and said she was suffering from headaches.

The examination diagnosed Bushra Bibi with posterior vitreous detachment (PVD) in her right eye. The report also identified myopia and astigmatism. After the diagnosis, Bushra Bibi was prescribed eye drops and medication, along with the use of glasses. She was reportedly recommended a follow-up medical check-up after four weeks.

The former first lady then underwent eye surgery on the evening of April 16.

Imran and Bushra Bibi remain incarcerated in Rawalpindi's Adiala Jail. They were sentenced on December 20, 2025, to 17 years in prison in the Toshakhana-II case, which pertains to allegations that the couple unlawfully retained a Bulgari jewellery set gifted by the Saudi crown prince during an official visit to Saudi Arabia.

Imran has been in custody since August 2023, serving a sentence in a £190 million corruption case. He also faces pending trials under the Anti-Terrorism Act in connection with protests on May 9, 2023.

headline: Oil rebounds as Hormuz shipping attacks blunt hopes for Iran truce
description: Brent futures climb $1.04, or 1.1%, to $92.53 a barrel
author: Reuters
article_text:
Oil prices rose on Wednesday from the ‌previous session's two-month lows, as the market swung between hopes for a de-escalation in the US-Israeli war on Iran and concerns about attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.

Also on Wednesday, a regional governor said a drone attack caused a fire in the port area of ​Ust-Luga by the Baltic Sea in northwest Russia, injuring three workers.

Brent futures climbed $1.04, or 1.1%, to $92.53 a barrel ​at 0420 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate crude rose 67 cents, or 0.8%, to $86.71.

Recent data showed ⁠little sign of fewer attacks in November, after 37 ships were attacked in October, the highest monthly total since the ​start of the Middle East war, according to data from the Washington Institute for Near East Policy.

"There has been an ​increase of vessel attacks in the Gulf shipping lanes amidst uncertainty of the diplomacy talks," said June Goh, senior analyst at Sparta Commodities.

"With the US midterms well over and more crude flows out of the Middle East, there seems to be more bearish tones to the ​oil price."

She added that the top driver for oil is the extent to which Iran will come to the table ​with US demands to reach a diplomatic agreement.

A tanker was struck northeast of Lima in Oman, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations ‌agency said ⁠on Tuesday. Iran's Revolutionary Guards Navy said in a separate statement on Tuesday that two tankers caught fire after hitting naval mines on the "unauthorised route" in the strait.

"Even in the event a deal is struck, an increase in flows through the waterway would still depend on mine clearance, insurance costs and whether or not shipowners would even be willing to ​take the risk," LSEG Oil Research ​said in a November ⁠10 note.

In the previous session, oil prices initially fell by more than $3 a barrel after US officials downplayed the need for further military strikes against Iran, though some of the losses were ​clawed back after an Iranian security official said no talks were taking place between the two ​sides.

Meanwhile, US crude oil ⁠stocks rose in the latest completed week, market sources said, citing data from the American Petroleum Institute. Crude stocks rose by 9 million barrels for the week that ended on November 6, the sources said.

In Russia, oil refining capacity has been reduced by ⁠about 30% ​since late October following renewed Ukrainian drone attacks, industry sources said.

Russian ​and Ukrainian officials met in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday for their first peace talks since February as US President Donald Trump's envoys launched a fresh push ​to end the war.

"Even in the event a deal is struck, an increase in flows through the waterway would still depend on mine clearance, insurance costs and whether or not shipowners would even be willing to ​take the risk," LSEG Oil Research ​said in a November ⁠10 note.

Russian ​and Ukrainian officials met in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday for their first peace talks since February as US President Donald Trump's envoys launched a fresh push ​to end the war.

headline: Grand Theft Auto VI opens preloads nine days before launch
description: PlayStation 5 Pro version will have sharper graphics and will be the only one with ray-traced shadows
author: Anadolu Agency
article_text:
Rockstar Games said it opened early downloads for Grand Theft Auto VI on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S on November 10, nine days before its release.

Players who preordered a digital copy can download the game now.

The download may require up to 212 GB of free space, depending on the console, according to Rockstar's support site.

Rockstar said the game targets 30 frames per second on current consoles. The PlayStation 5 Pro version will have sharper graphics and will be the only one with ray-traced shadows.

Players will also be able to stream the game on Xbox One and Xbox Series X|S through Xbox Cloud Gaming. The streamed version will use Xbox Series S graphics settings, and Rockstar said internet speeds can affect performance.

GTA 6 digital pre-orders reportedly almost reach 8m ahead of launch

Grand Theft Auto 6 has reportedly accumulated an estimated 7.71 million digital pre-orders approximately two weeks before launch, with potential revenue reaching $751 million, according to analytics firm Sensor Tower.

The figures are based on the company's modelling of consumer activity and have not been confirmed by Rockstar Games or parent company Take-Two Interactive.

PlayStation 5 accounts for 74% of the estimated pre-orders, representing approximately $559 million in projected revenue. Xbox Series X|S makes up the remaining 26%, equivalent to around $192 million. Sensor Tower's data does not establish a definitive reason for the difference between the platforms.

The majority of customers have also reportedly opted for the more expensive edition. Earlier Sensor Tower estimates indicate that 89% of pre-orders were for the $100 Ultimate Edition, while 11% selected the $80 Standard Edition. The split was broadly similar across both platforms.

The estimated pre-order figures also place GTA 6 ahead of Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2, with Sensor Tower reporting a 148% lead at the equivalent point before launch. However, the comparison covers US digital pre-orders only and excludes physical sales.

Sensor Tower senior vice president and Video Game Insights general manager Karl Kontus estimates that GTA 6 could reach approximately 25 million pre-orders by launch, rather than the 40 million or more associated with a typical pre-order trajectory. He has suggested that demand is unusually concentrated in the pre-launch period.

Kontus also referenced Cyberpunk 2077, which recorded eight million publisher-confirmed pre-orders before release. His projection of approximately $2 billion in GTA 6 pre-order sales by launch remains an analyst estimate.

headline: Chelsea frustrated by Hacken in women's Champions League
description: Fujino brace inspires Manchester City to 4-1 win over Inter
author: AFP
article_text:
Chelsea were held to a goalless stalemate by Hacken in the Women's Champions League on Tuesday, while Manchester City earned a first win of the competition.

The London club hit the woodwork twice in Sweden as an inspired showing by Hacken goalkeeper Jennifer Falk also helped keep the visitors at bay.

Chelsea are third in the league phase table after four matches, one point behind defending champions and pacesetters Barcelona, although the perfect Catalans hold a game in hand.

However, several teams, including Lyon and Arsenal -- both of whom are just a point behind Sonia Bompastor's side -- could leapfrog them this matchday.

"It's a frustrating result," Blues boss Bompastor told UEFA. "We came here with the ambition of winning the game... But tonight it didn't go that way. We need to learn from this."

Women's Super League champions Man City enjoyed a 4-1 success at Inter Milan to earn a first win in the league phase after drawing their first three outings.

A first-half Aoba Fujino brace cancelled out Elisa Bartoli's opener for the hosts by half-time.

Kerstin Casparij and Grace Clinton were on target after the break to send City up to seventh in the table.

Paris Saint-Germain fell to a first defeat as Bayern Munich held on to win 2-1 at the Parc des Princes and climb to second in the table, ahead of Chelsea on goal difference.

Klara Buehl's strike five minutes from half-time proved the winner as she added to PSG goalkeeper Katarzyna Kiedrzynek's early own goal to put the Bavarians in a comfortable position.

Paulina Dudek halved the deficit from the spot midway through the second period but Bayern held on.

PSG lie in ninth place on five points.

In the Spanish capital, Real Madrid downed visitors Paris FC 3-0 thanks to three second-half strikes.

A first win of the league phase sent Pau Quesada's side eighth in the table on six points, while Paris FC lounge 16th on two points.

Arianna Caruso broke the deadlock in the 55th minute and Lineth Beerensteyn thumped home soon after.

Linda Caicedo made the points safe with nine minutes remaining as she finished smartly from Felicia Schroeder's reverse pass.

"It was really important to pick up the three points today because we hadn't won any of our first three games," Caruso said. "We have to try to finish among the top teams."

Roma held on to beat Swiss side Servette 2-1.

On Wednesday, eight-time winners Lyon are in action away to Juventus.

article_html:
LONDON:

Chelsea were held to a goalless stalemate by Hacken in the Women's Champions League on Tuesday, while Manchester City earned a first win of the competition.

The London club hit the woodwork twice in Sweden as an inspired showing by Hacken goalkeeper Jennifer Falk also helped keep the visitors at bay.

Chelsea are third in the league phase table after four matches, one point behind defending champions and pacesetters Barcelona, although the perfect Catalans hold a game in hand.

However, several teams, including Lyon and Arsenal -- both of whom are just a point behind Sonia Bompastor's side -- could leapfrog them this matchday.

"It's a frustrating result," Blues boss Bompastor told UEFA.
"We came here with the ambition of winning the game... But tonight it didn't go that way. We need to learn from this."

Women's Super League champions Man City enjoyed a 4-1 success at Inter Milan to earn a first win in the league phase after drawing their first three outings.

A first-half Aoba Fujino brace cancelled out Elisa Bartoli's opener for the hosts by half-time.

Kerstin Casparij and Grace Clinton were on target after the break to send City up to seventh in the table.

Paris Saint-Germain fell to a first defeat as Bayern Munich held on to win 2-1 at the Parc des Princes and climb to second in the table, ahead of Chelsea on goal difference.

Klara Buehl's strike five minutes from half-time proved the winner as she added to PSG goalkeeper Katarzyna Kiedrzynek's early own goal to put the Bavarians in a comfortable position.

Paulina Dudek halved the deficit from the spot midway through the second period but Bayern held on.

PSG lie in ninth place on five points.

In the Spanish capital, Real Madrid downed visitors Paris FC 3-0 thanks to three second-half strikes.

A first win of the league phase sent Pau Quesada's side eighth in the table on six points, while Paris FC lounge 16th on two points.

Arianna Caruso broke the deadlock in the 55th minute and Lineth Beerensteyn thumped home soon after.

Linda Caicedo made the points safe with nine minutes remaining as she finished smartly from Felicia Schroeder's reverse pass.

"It was really important to pick up the three points today because we hadn't won any of our first three games," Caruso said. "We have to try to finish among the top teams."

Roma held on to beat Swiss side Servette 2-1.

headline: England hand first call-up to Hill
description: The 24-year-old will compete with Burn, Quansah and Branthwaite for a defensive spot
author: AFP
article_text: England have called up uncapped Bournemouth defender James Hill for their Nations League matches against Croatia and Spain. Hill has been added to Thomas Tuchel's squad after centre-backs Marc Guehi and Ezri Konsa were ruled out of Thursday's clash with Croatia at Wembley. Guehi withdrew with an injury suffered in Manchester City's Premier League defeat at Nottingham Forest on Saturday. Newcastle defender Dan Burn was called up on Monday, while Arsenal star Konsa will not be fit to face Slaven Bilic's side at Wembley as he is following his own fitness programme. Konsa is expected to be fit for Sunday's game against world champions Spain in Madrid. The unheralded Hill has enjoyed a rapid rise this season, playing 15 times for Bournemouth to catch Tuchel's eye. Hill will be fighting for a spot in England's central defence along with Burn, Jarell Quansah and Jarrad Branthwaite. "Bournemouth defender James Hill has received his first call-up to the England squad," a Football Association statement said on Tuesday. "The 24-year-old, who represented his nation at under-20 and under-21 level, has joined England ahead of the forthcoming Nations League fixtures. "Meanwhile, Ezri Konsa will not be in contention for Croatia at Wembley on Thursday as he continues to follow his own programme but will return to full training later this week before Sunday's trip to Spain."

headline: McTominay reveals World Cup heart scare
description: The midfielder underwent cardiac ablation surgery in Manchester after experiencing an irregular heartbeat
author: AFP
article_text: Scotland midfielder Scott McTominay has revealed he had to have his heart shocked just two days before playing in his country's World Cup opener against Haiti. McTominay was said to have missed training in the lead-up to the 1-0 victory over Haiti in Massachusetts due to a stomach complaint. But, speaking at a press conference in Glasgow on Tuesday, the 29-year-old said: "I had to go and get the shock on my heart two days before the Haiti game." McTominay played in all three of Scotland's matches at the World Cup, but was below his best as they exited at the group stage after losing to Morocco and Brazil. "I was 100 percent (fit), but obviously when you're sat in a hospital bed two days before the first game of the World Cup about to get put to sleep, it's not ideal, is it?" he said. "You've prepared so well, I was in such good condition and then something like that happens and you're thinking, 'How is this happening to me?' "It's nowhere near an excuse, but it's something that you have to look back on and say, 'Well, it's part of the process'." McTominay returned to action with Napoli at the start of this season. But after playing their first two Serie A matches, he spent September on the sidelines after undergoing a corrective operation. McTominay underwent a cardiac ablation procedure in Manchester to treat a mild, benign heart arrhythmia. That meant McTominay missed Scotland's first four matches under new boss Sebastien Pocognoli. He is back with the national team for the Nations League ties against North Macedonia and Switzerland over the coming week. "I'm good. I'm feeling much, much better than what I was," he said. "I feel like it was something that needed to be done. "Obviously, it looks a lot worse to people in the media and family and friends who reach out to you after they've seen news relating to a heart issue, but it was a relatively straightforward procedure which went really well."

headline: Carrick set to be sacked by Manchester United
description: An eight-match winless streak leaves the Red Devils facing a potential relegation battle
author: AFP
article_text: Michael Carrick is set to be sacked by Manchester United after his side's dismal start to the season, according to reports on Tuesday. United's hierarchy have been conducting an internal review of the club's miserable form. United are in the midst of their worst opening to a campaign in 40 years, leaving them languishing in the Premier League relegation zone after an eight-match winless run. It is believed Carrick's future will be decided at a meeting attended by influential shareholder Jim Ratcliffe, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox in Monaco on Wednesday. Although it is said that no final decision has been made, Berrada and Wilcox are reportedly leaning towards dismissing Carrick. Ratcliffe and United owners the Glazer family would then decide whether to act on that recommendation, with an announcement potentially coming on Thursday. Carrick was seen arriving at United's Carrington training base on Tuesday, but it appears to be only a matter of time before his turbulent reign comes to an end. The 45-year-old had been granted a stay of execution after he was widely expected to be axed in late October following a 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth. United's surprise decision to let Carrick limp on failed to produce a significant improvement in performances, particularly defensively. They were beaten 2-0 at Chelsea, then scrambled a last-gasp 3-2 win against Roma in the Champions League after falling two goals down. It looked certain that former United midfielder Carrick would be on the way out when his team twice trailed by two goals against Aston Villa on Sunday. When United scored twice in stoppage-time to rescue an improbable 4-4 draw, it was interpreted as a positive sign for Carrick as the players were still fighting for him. But United's powerbrokers look set to make yet another managerial change in a bid to avoid being dragged into an embarrassing relegation battle. United States boss Mauricio Pochettino, former Newcastle manager Eddie Howe, ex-Chelsea chief Antonio Conte and former Germany coach Julian Nagelsmann have all been linked with the United job. United have the rest of the two-week international break to resolve their managerial situation before returning to action at bitter rivals Liverpool on November 22. Carrick has presided over United's slide to 18th place -- their lowest position 10 games into a top-flight season since 1986-87 when they were 20th. He was hired on a permanent basis in the close-season after leading United to a third-place finish in the Premier League during his spell as interim boss. Carrick had won plaudits for steadying the ship after Ruben Amorim's volatile reign ended in the sack in January. But, hampered by the club's underwhelming recruitment in the transfer window, Carrick's team have endured a steep decline this term. United, who have not won the title since Alex Ferguson's final season as boss in 2012-13, only signed midfield trio Youri Tielemans, Carlos Baleba and Andrey Santos in the summer transfer window despite the glaring need for new forwards. Carrick struggled to maintain discipline among his squad, dropping captain Bruno Fernandes after he criticised his manager's tactics during a 4-1 thrashing at Champions League debutants Como.
